description: Diversity, ecology, cell biology and evolutionary origins of multicellular eukaryotes, illustrated through mosses and liverworts; fungi and slime molds; and fresh water and marine algae. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. Or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology.

subject: BIOL
title: Vascular Plants
description: A comparative study of pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, integrating form, function and ecology. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology. Equivalency: APBI 210

subject: BIOL
title: Fundamentals of Ecology
description: Dynamics of plant and animal populations, structure of ecological communities and functioning of ecosystems. Interpretation of research results and application to environmental issues. Labs meet once a month. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001 or 8 transfer credits of first-year BIOL.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics for Life
description: How genetic differences determine individual characteristics, and how they are inherited, analyzed, and modified. Emphasis on genetic diversity, human ancestry, personal genomics, and cancer genetics. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of BIOL 112, BIOL 121 or (b) SCIE 001. ; or (c) a corequisite of one of CHEM 203 or CHEM 223 and one of BIOL 112 or BIOL 121.

subject: BIOL
title: Fundamentals of Genetics
description: Genotype and phenotype, mechanisms of inheritance, genetic analysis. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: Either (a) all of BIOL_V 112, BIOL_V 121 or (b) SCIE_V 001 or (c) a corequisite of one of CHEM_V 203 or CHEM_V 223 or CHEM_O 203 and one of BIOL_V 112 or BIOL_V 121 or (d) 8 transfer credits of first-year BIOL_V.

subject: BIOL
title: Fundamentals of Physiology
description: Principles of cellular and organismal physiology illustrated with examples from unicellular organisms, plants and animals, focusing on transport processes, water balance, nutrient acquisition and communication. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of BIOL 112, BIOL 121 or (b) SCIE 001. or (c) 8 transfer credits of 1st year BIOL and 6 credits of 1st year chemistry.

subject: BIOL
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Statistical procedures for biological research; estimation, hypothesis testing, goodness of fit, analysis of variance and regression; use of computers for statistical analysis. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 121, SCIE_V 001. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 180, SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Biomathematics
description: Introduction to uses of mathematics in the biological sciences; experimental design and modelling of biological processes. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Recommended co-requisites: one of BIOL 300, STAT 200.

subject: BIOL
title: Biodiversity, Human & Planetary Health
description: Effects of biodiversity on human health, from human microbiome to ecosystem. Strategies for protecting, restoring and managing for biodiversity, human and planetary health. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 111, BIOL 121, GEOS 207, SCIE 001 and third-year class standing.

subject: BIOL
title: Green Planet: Biology and History of Plants that Changed Civilizations
description: Biological, cultural, and societal significance of staple crops selected as foods, medicines or raw materials by different societies, and their pivotal role in the rise and fall of past and present civilizations. Prerequisite: 3rd-year class standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Ecology
description: Ecology of populations, communities and ecosystems. Tests of ecological theory with experiments and application to environmental issues. Labs meet once a month. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: BIOL 230.

subject: BIOL
title: Natural History Collections and Biodiversity Science
description: An introduction to biodiversity and specimen-based science, including theory and best practices for creating, curating and preserving natural history collections, working ethically with collections, and the historical, contemporary and future role of these collections to science and society. Pre-requisites: A minimum of 3rd-year class standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Animal Behaviour
description: Animal behavior from an ecological and evolutionary perspective; the methods used to study behaviour and test its adaptive significance. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001; and 3rd-year class standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Experimental Methods in Animal Behaviour
description: Designing, conducting, and analyzing studies of animal behaviour, with an emphasis on field-based methods. Students conduct capstone research projects. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: One of BIOL 300, STAT 200. Corequisite: BIOL 310.

subject: BIOL
title: Elements of Biodiversity
description: The units of biodiversity, from genes to ecosystems, how they are structured in space, and their importance to human well-being and ecosystem health. Prerequisite: One of APBI 260, BIOL 230, FRST 201, GEOB 207, GEOS 207. Equivalency: CONS 314

subject: BIOL
title: Weed Science
description: Importance, identification, dissemination and biology of weeds; preventative, cultural, biological and chemical methods of control. Equivalency: APBI328

subject: BIOL
title: Survey of Algae
description: A survey of the algae, considering their morphology, life history, classification, and ecology. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Morphology and Evolution of Bryophytes
description: A study of evolution, taxonomy and morphology of mosses, liverworts and hornworts with emphasis on living plants in their environment. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Structure and Evolution of Ferns and Fern-allies
description: Anatomy, morphology and relationships of the ferns and fern-allies, with assessment of both fossil and extant taxa. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Structure and Reproduction of Fungi
description: The evolutionary diversity of the fungi as shown by their morphology and reproductive biology. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Seed Plant Taxonomy
description: Introduction to seed plant taxonomy emphasizing descriptive morphology and identification. Each student will be required to submit a plant collection. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001. Equivalency: APBI_V 324

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Animal Mechanics and Locomotion
description: Comparative aspects of the functional design of skeletal systems and the mechanics of swimming, flying and terrestrial locomotion, with particular reference to the vertebrates. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Experimental Biology of Invertebrates
description: Behaviour and ecology of invertebrates as revealed by hands-on experiments in the laboratory and field. Marine emphasis. Prerequisite: BIOL 205. Corequisite: Either (a) STAT 200 or (b) BIOL 300.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Entomology
description: A survey of the structure, classification and biology of insects; ecology, life-histories and insect-plant relations. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001. Equivalency: APBI_V 327

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolution of Parasites
description: Morphology, life histories, ecology and evolution of parasites (and infectious agents more broadly) infecting humans and animals. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001

subject: BIOL
title: Cell Receptor Signaling, Communication and Regulation
description: How cells react to external signals, and how these responses are regulated. Experimental approaches and common themes will be examined using a variety of cell receptors as models. . Prerequisite: BIOL_V 200. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Developmental Biology (Lecture)
description: Animal development and its underlying causal principles; introductory embryology. Prerequisite: Either (a) BIOL 201 or (b) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 260 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234.

subject: BIOL
title: Developmental Biology
description: Animal development and its underlying causal principles; introductory embryology. Prerequisite: Either (a) BIOL 201 or (b) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 260 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234.

subject: BIOL
title: Protistology
description: Cell biology, ecology, and evolution of protists; origins of multicellularity; the role of protists in micropaleontology, parasitology, and oceanography. Prerequisite: BIOL 200

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Genetics
description: Isolation and identification of genes, analysis of gene structure; gene expression and its regulation in prokaryotes and in eukaryotes; developmental genetics. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 233, BIOL 234, MICB 322, FRST 302.

subject: BIOL
title: Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology
description: Natural selection; population genetics, quantitative genetics and systematics; classical and molecular approaches to the study of evolution. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 233, BIOL 234.

subject: BIOL
title: Introductory Genetics Laboratory
description: A laboratory course demonstrating the fundamental principles of inheritance: Mendel's Laws, sex-linkage, mapping, mutagenesis, chromosome structure, developmental biology, biochemical and population genetics. Prerequisite: BIOL 200. Corequisite: One of BIOL 233, BIOL 234.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Genomics
description: An introduction to genome biology and applications of genomics. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 234, BIOL 233, FRST 302.

subject: BIOL
title: Introductory Cell Biology Laboratory
description: Designing and conducting cell biology experiments using unicellular eukaryotes or prokaryotes with emphasis on techniques in microscopy and cell biology. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 200 and 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science and one of (a) BIOL_V 180 (or BIOL_V 140), or (b) SCIE_V 001, or (c) 3rd-year class standing in Combined Honours Biophysics.

subject: BIOL
title: Introductory Molecular Biology Laboratory
description: Designing and conducting molecular biology experiments using bioinformatics recombinant DNA techniques. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 200 and 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science.

subject: BIOL
title: Integrative Biology Laboratory
description: Field-based and laboratory-based investigation of organisms. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher in Combined Major in Science, and one of (a) BIOL 121 and BIOL 180 (or BIOL 140), or (b) SCIE 001, or (c) 8 transfer credits of first-year biology.

subject: BIOL
title: Plants and Peoples
description: The interactions of plants and human societies: the role of people in the origin, evolution and dispersal of food, drug and economic plants, and the influences of plants on human societies. Suitable for upper-level Arts students.

subject: BIOL
title: Human Heredity and Evolution
description: Relates genetic and evolutionary concepts to humans. Primarily for upper-level students in the Faculty of Arts. Credit will be granted for only one of BIOL 121 or BIOL 344. Not open to students in the Life Sciences.

subject: BIOL
title: Human Ecology
description: Basics of ecology are introduced, focussing on observations of the natural world. Assignments, including a group project, consider connections between research, awareness and practical uses of ecology. Not for credit in the Life Sciences.

subject: BIOL
title: Microbes and Society
description: An elementary course in molecular biology primarily for Arts students. The historical development of recent discoveries in molecular biology with emphasis on bacteria and viruses and their interaction with humans. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.) Not for credit in Life Sciences.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles and Methodology in Biological Research
description: Contemporary research in the Botany and Zoology Departments; history and methodology of scientific discovery; seminars on current problems. Restricted to Honours students in Biology. Not to be taken concurrently with BIOL 449.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of Cannabis
description: Biological aspects of cannabis, including structure and function, photosynthesis, plant growth, specialized metabolites, neuroscience and the human endocannabinoid system, and applications for human use in medicine, consumer products and textiles. Prerequisite: 3rd-year class standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Darwinian Medicine
description: Using the Darwinian theory of natural selection to explore explanations of infectious diseases, allergies, cancer, mental illness, and other human diseases. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: www.vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-sc… Prerequisite: Third-year standing. Equivalency: ISCI 350

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Physiology I
description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants. Restricted to Majors and Honours students in Biology. Prerequisite: Either (a) BIOL 121 and one of CHEM 123, CHEM 130; or (b) SCIE 001. CHEM 233 is recommended. Equivalency: APBI351, FRST311

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Physiology II: Plant Development
description: Introduction to the processes involved in growth and development: cell division, tissue culture, meristems, differentiation, and the action of major growth regulators, and photomorphogenesis. Emphasis on experimental approaches. Prerequisite: Either (a) BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234; or (b) FRST 302. CHEM 233 is recommended.

subject: BIOL
title: Neural and Muscular Physiology
description: Excitable membranes, neural signaling and transmission; transduction and coding of sensory information; muscle contraction. Prerequisite: BIOL 200.

subject: BIOL
title: Cellular Dynamics
description: The cytoskeleton, cell dynamics, and regulation of cellular activities. Preference will be given to Majors or Honours students in Biology and Combined Honours Biophysics. Prerequisite: BIOL 200 and one of APBI 312, APBI 351, BIOL 260, BIOL 351, BIOL 352, BIOL 361, FRST 311.

subject: BIOL
title: Laboratory in Animal Physiology
description: Experimental studies in animal physiology. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 204 or BIOL_V 260.

subject: BIOL
title: Comparative Cardiovascular, Respiratory and Osmoregulatory Physiology
description: Cardiovascular, respiratory, and osmoregulatory physiology. Preference will be given to students who are in Biology, Nutritional Sciences, and Combined Honours Biophysics. Prerequisite: BIOL 204 and one of BIOL 260, BIOL 361. Equivalency: APBI 311

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Muscle Physiology and Energetics
description: Introduction to the structure and function of the muscular system, metabolism and energetics from a comparative perspective across vertebrates and invertebrates. Prerequisite: BIOL 260 and one of BIOL 200, BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Neurobiology I
description: Introduction to the structure and function of the nervous system, excitable membranes, and synaptic signaling using representative vertebrate and invertebrate species. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 260, NSCI 200, PSYC 270, PSYC 271, PSYC 304, CAPS 301.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Neurobiology II
description: Examination of the neural systems underlying sensation, action, and complex behaviours using representative vertebrate and invertebrate species. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: BIOL 371.

subject: BIOL
title: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Work experience in an industrial setting, taken during Winter Session (Term 2) of third-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following third-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 398 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Theory of Evolutionary Dynamics
description: Evolution as a dynamical system based on ecological interactions. Adaptive dynamics and evolutionary game theory. Credit will be granted for only one of BIOL_V 401 or BIOL_V 560. . Prerequisite: BIOL_V 301 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Aquatic Ecology
description: Theoretical and applied limnology; ecology of inland water organisms in relation to physical, chemical and biological factors. One weekend field trip required. Prerequisite: BIOL 230 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200.

subject: BIOL
title: Microbial Ecology
description: Theoretical and applied ecology of microbes. Focus on microbial symbionts of animals, plants and seaweeds. Research project development through critical analysis of microbial ecological literature and computational analysis of ecological data. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 121, SCIE_V 001, BIOL_V 230 and one of BIOL_V 300, FRST_V 231, STAT_V 200. 4th-year class standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Ecological Methodology
description: Design, execution, and analysis of ecological surveys and experiments. Practical field methods for estimating population metrics and describing community structure. Computer techniques for the statistical analysis of ecological data. Prerequisite: BIOL 230 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200.

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Ecology I
description: Plant community ecology including a consideration of the major approaches to sampling, analyzing and interpreting vegetation patterns. Instruction given in field work and computer analysis of field data. Prerequisite: BIOL 230. BIOL 324 is recommended.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Applied Ecology
description: Principles of animal and community ecology applicable to the management of animal resources; application of statistical and computer techniques for measuring, analyzing, modelling, and simulating resource systems; problems of multiple resource use. Prerequisite: BIOL 300

subject: BIOL
title: Field Course in Ecology
description: A two-week intensive course in field methods used in ecology. Fieldwork for this course is normally in the summer. A fee will be assessed for living and traveling expenses. Pre-registration required. Prerequisite: BIOL 230 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200. BIOL 306 is recommended.

subject: BIOL
title: Current Topics in Animal Behaviour
description: Lectures and seminar discussions on selected topics in animal behaviour. Prerequisite: BIOL 310

subject: BIOL
title: Insect Ecology
description: Behavioural, population and community ecology of insects. Interactions between insects and plants and the application of the principles of insect ecology to biological control of insects and weeds. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 205, BIOL 327, APBI 327. Equivalency: APBI 427

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Biogeography
description: Description and interpretation of present and past floristic vegetational patterns; integration of evolutionary, ecological, and plant biogeographical concepts. Terrestrial and aquatic plants are considered. Restricted to students of third and fourth years. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Zoogeography
description: The role of physical, ecological, and evolutionary processes in determining the geographic distribution of animals including humans, with implications for speciation and conservation. Restricted to students in third and fourth year. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Evolutionary Processes in Plants
description: Experimental and comparative analysis of evolutionary processes, speciation, and phylogenetic patterns in plants. Prerequisite: BIOL 336.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Conservation Biology
description: Ecological basis of conserving biological diversity and ecosystem services; application of ecological theory to global and local conservation problems in the context of economic, legal, political, and social perspectives. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: One of BIOL 230, FRST 201.

subject: BIOL
title: Phylogenetic Biology
description: Biodiversity from an evolutionary perspective. The evolutionary (phylogenetic) tree of genetic descent that links all organisms: its reconstruction, interpretation, and implications for fields from ecology to molecular biology. Prerequisite: BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234. BIOL 336 is recommended

subject: BIOL
title: Evolutionary Ecology
description: Ecological adaptation and evolutionary processes in contemporary populations; natural selection, variation, optimization, foraging theory, coevolution, arms races; life history theory, evolution of sex, sexual selection, evolution in managed populations. Prerequisite: BIOL 336 and BIOL 230.

subject: BIOL
title: Ocean Conservation and Sustainability
description: An interdisciplinary conservation course with a solutions-oriented approach to marine issues, drawing from natural sciences, social sciences, business, law, and communication. . Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Plant-Microbe Interactions
description: Biology and physiology of selected plant-microbe relationships. Impacts of plant-microbe relationships on society. Prerequisite: BIOL 200 and one of BIOC 202, BIOC 203, BIOL 201, BIOL 233, BIOL 234, BIOL 260. Equivalency: APBI 426

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Stress Ecophysiology
description: Molecular mechanisms of plant responses to extreme environments. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: BIOL 351. BIOL 406 or 407 are recommended.

subject: BIOL
title: Tropical Ecology and Conservation
description: Ecology, function, history and conservation of tropical systems. Focus on ecological and evolutionary principles using tropical landscapes as a geographic template. Assessment of factors that make tropical systems vulnerable to degradation. Research project development using analysis of tropical ecology literature. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001 and one of BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201, GEOS_V 207, GEOB_V 207.

subject: BIOL
title: Biomechanics
description: An analytical approach to the study of skeletal mechanics and animal locomotion. Selected topics in the structure and properties of biological materials, the functional design of skeletons for locomotion, and the fluid mechanics of swimming and flight. Prerequisite: BIOL 325

subject: BIOL
title: Mammalogy
description: Natural history, behavioral ecology and conservation of terrestrial mammals. The laboratory includes classification, life histories, and ecology, with particular attention to species from British Columbia. Prerequisite: BIOL 204

subject: BIOL
title: Ornithology and Herpetology
description: Ecology, evolution, behavior, and conservation of birds, amphibians, and reptiles. Laboratories and field projects will focus on identification, systematics, and natural history, with particular attention to species from British Columbia. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001.

subject: BIOL
title: Evolutionary Morphology of Marine Invertebrates
description: Comparative analysis of marine invertebrate morphology from a macroevolutionary perspective. Origin and evolution of reoccurring adaptations in meiofaunal, benthic, pelagic, and deep-sea invertebrates, including their larval stages. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 205 and 3rd-year class standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Genome Evolution
description: Integration of molecular genetics and genomics with evolutionary biology. Emphasis on the evolutionary dynamics of genomes and the evolutionary implications of recent discoveries in molecular genetics and genomics. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 335, BIOL_V 336, BIOL_V 338, BIOT_V 380.

subject: BIOL
title: Evolutionary Cell Biology
description: Ultrastructure, biogenesis, and evolution of eukaryotic cells and cell organelles, including their macromolecular basis. Prerequisite: BIOL200 And fourth-year standing.

subject: BIOL
title: Research Strategies and Techniques in Cell Biology
description: Major physiological mechanisms that define eukaryotic cells, explored through student visits to UBC research laboratories and discussion of recent scientific literature, with emphasis on the techniques and strategies that enable researchers to test hypotheses and advance new concepts. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 200 and one of BIOL_V 233, BIOL_V 234 and 4th-year class standing.

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Genetics
description: Emphasis on molecular aspects. Systems and techniques for genetic analysis in plants; isolation and regulation of plant genes; genetic dissection of plant-specific processes; transposable elements; gene transfer in plants; cytoplasmic inheritance; genetic engineering. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: BIOL 335

subject: BIOL
title: Population Genetics
description: Theoretical and experimental aspects of population and quantitative genetics. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: BIOL 336 and either (a) BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234; or (b) FRST 302.

subject: BIOL
title: Integrated Functional Genomics
description: Global transcript, protein, and metabolite profiling technologies and their integration; applications focus on plant functions and plant interactions with pathogens and pests. One of BIOL_V 335, BIOL_V 338, BIOT_V 380. Equivalency: FNH_V 436.

subject: BIOL
title: Laboratory in Animal Cell Molecular Biology
description: The use of recombinant DNA techniques to explore problems in animal developmental biology. Prerequisite: All of BIOL 331, BIOL 335 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203.

subject: BIOL
title: Zoological Physics
description: Animal systems viewed from a physicist's perspective. Topics include sensory systems, energy budgets, locomotion, internal flows, physical advantages of grouping. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001. BIOL 325 is recommended. Equivalency: PHYS 438

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Microscopy Techniques
description: Microscopy techniques used in biological research. Principles, applications and hands-on training of optical and electron microscopy. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . . Prerequisite: BIOL_V 200. Corequisite: One of BIOL_V 448, BIOL_V 449 and Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Plant Genomics
description: Concepts, principles, applications, and recent discoveries in genome structure, genetics, and comparative genomics in plants with a focus on economically important plants. Corequisite: One of BIOL_V 335, BIOL_V 338, BIOT_V 380. Equivalency: APBI_V 440.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Topics in Cell Biology
description: Analysis of cellular organelles and the intracellular traffic between them, concentrating on mammalian cell systems. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 340, BIOL 341 and one of BIOL 361, BIOL 362, BIOL 370, BIOL 371.

subject: BIOL
title: Darwin's Fishes
description: A series of computer-assisted lectures using ichthyology and the work of Charles Darwin to illustrate basic principles of biology, and their practical implementation, i.e., how biologists select research programs, generate and test hypotheses, and present their case to peers and the public. Prerequisite: 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science is required.

subject: BIOL
title: History and Philosophy of Biology
description: The nature of science, this history of evolutionary and molecular biology, philosophical questions about scientific methods and fundamental conclusions of biology. Prerequisite: 4th-year class standing in any degree program.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles and Methodology in Biological Research
description: Seminars, debates, workshops and tutorials designed to produce competence in specific areas of Biology. Restricted to Honours students in Biology. Corequisite: BIOL 449

subject: BIOL
title: Directed Studies in Biology
description: A course designed to allow students to undertake an investigation on a specific topic as agreed upon by the faculty member and the student. Permission of the supervisor required. No more than six credits of BIOL_V 448 may be taken with the same supervisor.

subject: BIOL
title: Directed Biological Research
description: A course designed to allow students to undertake a research project in selected fields. Open only to Honours students in Biology, with permission of the supervisor. Presentation of a thesis and an oral examination are required. Corequisite: BIOL 447

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Adaptation of Animals to the Environment
description: Physiological, biochemical, and molecular strategies of adaptation of animals to environmental challenges. The evolution of genetic and biochemical systems, and their impact on animal structure and function. Prerequisite: One of APBI 311, BIOL 361, BIOL 362, BIOL 364, BIOL 370, BIOL 371 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203. BIOL 457 is recommended.

subject: BIOL
title: Comparative Neurobiology
description: Advanced investigations of the evolution of animal nervous systems, integrating studies of diverse species to understand fundamental neurobiology. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 371, BIOL 372, CAPS 301, PSYC 304, PSYC 367, PSYC 370.

subject: BIOL
title: Insect Physiology
description: Physiological adaptations used by insects, including adaptations used to survive in extreme environments. Homeostatic mechanisms, neurophysiology, and experimental techniques. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 204, BIOL_V 205, BIOL_V 327, APBI_V 327 and one of BIOL_V 361, BIOL_V 364, BIOL_V 370, BIOL_V 371, APBI_V 311.

subject: BIOL
title: Comparative Animal Physiology
description: Selected topics in physiology emphasizing comparisons between diverse phylogenetic groups of animals. Prerequisite: One of APBI 311, BIOL 362, BIOL 364.

subject: BIOL
title: Comparative Neurobiology
description: Current approaches in neurobiology, from the cellular to the behavioural level, are examined using representatives of vertebrate and invertebrate nervous systems. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 361, BIOL 362, BIOL 364, CAPS 301, PSYC 360.

subject: BIOL
title: Comparative and Molecular Endocrinology
description: A comparative study of vertebrate and invertebrate endocrinology. Prerequisite: One of APBI 311, BIOL 364.

subject: BIOL
title: Comparative Environmental Physiology
description: A survey of physiological adaptions of animals to different environments. Prerequisite: One of APBI 311, BIOL 364.

subject: BIOL
title: Developmental Neurobiology
description: Cellular, molecular and physiological aspects of nervous system development with applications to understanding adult nervous system function and neurological disorders.

subject: BIOL
title: Neurobiology of Sensory and Motor Systems
description: Analysis of the mechanisms of sensory processing and motor orchestration using vertebrate and invertebrate model systems. Neural circuit structure, specialization, information coding, integration, and behaviour. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 372, CAPS 301, PSYC 304, PSYC 367, PSYC 370.

subject: BIOL
title: Neurobiology of Vision
description: Advanced investigation of animal vision; critical analysis of recent literature and research project development in visual neurobiology. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 372, CAPS 301, PSYC 304, PSYC 367, PSYC 370.

subject: BIOL
title: Ecological Plant Biochemistry
description: The structure, biosynthesis, distribution and biological function of secondary plant metabolites. Prerequisite: Either a) BIOL_V 200 and one of either BIOL_V 201 or BIOC_V 202, or b) BIOT_V 380. Equivalency: FRST_V 413.

subject: BIOL
title: Gene Regulation in Development
description: Control of gene expression in development; the genetic and physiological basis of epigenetic determination; inductive interactions. Prerequisite: Either (a) BIOL 335 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203; or (b) BIOT 380.

subject: BIOL
title: Animal Developmental Genetics
description: Role of genes in embryonic development. Emphasis on tissue specific expression patterns and the role of genetic networks in establishing cell types. Prerequisite: BIOL 463

subject: BIOL
title: Diversity and Evolution of Fishes
description: Introduction to fish diversity, with a focus on their phylogenetic interrelationships and the evolutionary, ecological, and biogeographic processes involved in generating patterns of fish biodiversity. Prerequisite: BIOL 204

subject: BIOL
title: Applied Biology of Fishes
description: Physiological ecology and exploitation biology of teleost fishes; computer-based analysis and modeling of fish populations. Prerequisite: BIOL 465

subject: BIOL
title: Topics in Biology
description: Selected topics in a specific area within Biology. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the Department. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in a Life Science specialization.

subject: BIOL
title: Student Directed Seminars
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Normally not suitable as a specific BIOL program elective. Prerequisite: 3rd-year class standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following fourth-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: BIOL
title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during the Winter Session (Terms 1 and 2) following fourth-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 399, BIOL_V 498. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Foundations of Chemistry
description: Atomic and molecular properties, chemical reactions, bonding, nomenclature, kinetics, equilibrium processes, acids and bases, oxidation and reduction. Intended for students who do not receive a satisfactory score on the UBC Chemistry Basic Skills Test, and need to establish a foundation of chemistry skills before proceeding to other first year chemistry courses. . Prerequisite: Not open to students with credit for Chemistry 12. Permission of the department head. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure, Bonding and Equilibrium in Chemistry (Lecture)
description: Fundamentals of bonding theories, structural chemistry and equilibrium with applications relevant to modern society. . Prerequisite: Not open to students with credit for Chemistry 12. A satisfactory score on the UBC Chemistry Basic Skills Test. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure, Bonding, and Equilibrium in Chemistry
description: Fundamentals of bonding theories, structural chemistry and equilibrium with applications relevant to modern society. Prerequisite: Not open to students with credit for CHEM 12. A satisfactory score on the UBC Chemistry Basic Skills Test.

subject: CHEM
title: Introductory Chemical Laboratory I
description: An introduction to the principles and techniques of the chemistry laboratory. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 110, CHEM 120.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure and Bonding in Chemistry (Lecture)
description: Fundamentals of bonding theories, structural chemistry, with applications relevant to modern society. . Prerequisite: One of CHEM 12, CHEM_V 100. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure and Bonding in Chemistry
description: Fundamentals of bonding theories and structural chemistry, with applications relevant to modern society. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 12, CHEM_V 100. Equivalency: CHEM_V 141

subject: CHEM
title: Thermodynamics, Kinetics and Organic Chemistry
description: Fundamentals of chemical reactivity: thermodynamics; kinetics; organic chemistry, including stereochemistry; applications relevant to modern society. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 111, CHEM 121, CHEM 141.

subject: CHEM
title: Thermodynamics, Kinetics and Organic Chemistry (Lecture)
description: Fundamentals of chemical reactivity: thermodynamics; kinetics; organic chemistry, including stereochemistry; applications relevant to modern society. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141.

subject: CHEM
title: Introductory Chemical Laboratory II
description: An introduction to the principles and techniques of the chemistry laboratory. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 111, CHEM 115, CHEM 121, CHEM 141.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Bonding, Molecular Structure and Properties for Lab Sciences
description: Bonding theories, their predictions, experimental tests, and consequences regarding chemical structure and observable properties. Applications relevant to modern society are emphasized. For students interested in lab-focused sciences such as Chemistry, Physics, Biochemistry, Microbiology and related disciplines. Restricted to students in the Faculty of Science. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 12, CHEM 100. Equivalency: CHEM121

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry for Engineering
description: Chemical bonding, properties of matter. Chemical thermodynamics with applications to phase equilibria, aqueous equilibria and electrochemistry. Processes at surfaces. Prerequisite: CHEM 12.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry
description: Structure, bonding and physical properties of aliphatic and aromatic compounds; mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-heteroatom bond formation; functional group interconversion and oxidation/reduction reactions. Only open to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 203 or CHEM 223, CHEM 225 or CHEM 233, 235. Prerequisite: Either (a) CHEM 123 or (b) all of CHEM 130, CHEM 135 or (c) SCIE 001.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Chemistry
description: Chemical kinetics and thermodynamics and spectroscopy useful in biological, medical, agricultural, earth, and related sciences. Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100 and one of CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 154.

subject: CHEM
title: Coordination Chemistry
description: Fundamental concepts and principles governing bonding and reactivity of coordination complexes: ligand field theory; symmetry and point groups; frontier molecular orbital theory. . Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 123, SCIE_V 001. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Chemical Analysis (Lecture)
description: Quantitative chemical analysis; chemical and physical principles of spectrophotometry, potentiometry, and chromatography. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 130, SCIE_V 001. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Chemical Analysis
description: Quantitative chemical analysis; chemical and physical principles of spectrophotometry, potentiometry, and chromatography. . Prerequisite: Either (a) CHEM_V 123 or (b) all of CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 135 or (c) SCIE_V 001. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry
description: Spectroscopy of organic compounds. Mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-carbon bond formation; functional group interconversion. Preference will be given to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_O 203 or (b) a score of 76% or higher in CHEM_V 233 or CHEM_O 213.

subject: CHEM
title: Introductory Analytical Chemical Laboratory
description: An introduction to the principles and techniques in the analytical chemistry laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 210 and one of CHEM 123, CHEM 135.

subject: CHEM
title: Fundamentals of Reactivity in Inorganic Chemistry
description: Chemical reactivity of inorganic systems: oxidation/reduction chemistry; multiply-bonded systems; main group chemistry. . Prerequisite: CHEM_V 208. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry (Lecture)
description: Structure, bonding and physical properties of aliphatic and aromatic compounds; mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-heteroatom bond formation; functional group interconversion and oxidation/reduction reactions. Only open to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Students should consult the Credit Exclusion List for credit exclusions relating to second-year organic chemistry courses. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, SCIE 001.

subject: CHEM
title: Introductory Synthetic Chemical Laboratory
description: An introduction to the principles and techniques in the synthetic organic and inorganic chemistry laboratory. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 135.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry for the Biological Sciences
description: Reactions and properties of carbonyl compounds, carbohydrates, amino acids, nucleic acids. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 233 or CHEM 203 or CHEM 223. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, SCIE 001.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Techniques of organic chemistry. To be taken in conjunction with, or in the term following, CHEM_V 233. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM_V 235 or CHEM_V 203. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 135, SCIE_V 001. Corequisite: CHEM_V 233 or CHEM_O 213.

subject: CHEM
title: Intermediate Synthetic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Techniques in synthetic organic and inorganic chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. . Prerequisite: Either (a) CHEM_V 203 or (b) all of CHEM_V 223, CHEM_V 225 or (c) all of CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 235. Corequisite: CHEM_V 213. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Inorganic Chemistry for Engineers
description: Chemistry of selected groups of inorganic compounds, considered in relation to industrial processes. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Chemistry for Engineers
description: States of matter, properties of gases, phase diagrams. Elementary chemical thermodynamics and kinetics. Reaction equilibria. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry for Engineers
description: A description of the properties and reactions of organic compounds. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001.

subject: CHEM
title: Communicating Chemistry
description: Effective argumentation and communication skills in chemistry. Only open to students in a Chemistry specialization. . Prerequisite: Third year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Aqueous Environmental Chemistry
description: Properties and composition of natural waters, including gas and solid equilibria, pH and acidification, redox chemistry, complexation, corrosion, ion exchange, colloids and microbial transformations. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHBE 220. and Third year standing.

subject: CHEM
title: Atmospheric Environmental Chemistry
description: Introduction to structure, composition and chemical processes occurring in Earth's atmosphere, including interactions with solar radiation, stratospheric ozone layer, photochemical smog and acid rain. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHBE 220. and Third year standing.

subject: CHEM
title: Fundamentals of Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
description: Principles of chemical thermodynamics; introduction to statistical mechanics; phase equilibria; electrochemistry. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 130 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253.

subject: CHEM
title: Biophysical Chemistry
description: Diffusion and transport phenomena; interaction of radiation and matter. Methods for determining molecular weight, size, and shape of molecules in solution. Prerequisite: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253 and either (a) a score of 76% or higher in CHEM 205 or (b) CHEM 304 or (c) PHYS 203.

subject: CHEM
title: Instrumental Analytical Chemistry
description: Theory, design, and application of instrumental methods of chemical analysis including spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, electroanalysis, and chemical separations. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 210, CHEM_V 211.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics and Spectroscopy
description: Principles of quantum mechanics; atomic wavefunctions; angular momentum; spin; atomic term symbols. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 123, SCIE_V 001 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Organic Chemistry for the Life Sciences
description: Chemistry of organic substances having particular relevance to the life sciences. Prerequisite: CHEM 213.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory I
description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 211, CHEM 215 and all of CHEM 213, CHEM 245.

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Catalysis
description: Fundamental aspects of chemical catalysis: kinetic models; catalytic processes in biochemistry and industry; emerging topics in catalysis. . Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 218, CHEM_V 250. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Practical Skills for Chemical Research
description: The nature of scientific research; practical skills for chemical research; communicating science. Restricted to Honours students with third year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory third year standing. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Integrated Chemistry Laboratory I
description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry specializations. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 211, CHEM 215 and all of CHEM 208, CHEM 213, CHEM 245.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Materials Chemistry
description: Basic principles of materials chemistry: classification; nomenclature; synthetic methods; characterization. . Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 208, CHEM_V 250 and one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Research Ethics and Data Analysis Skills
description: Research ethics; data analysis skills for chemical research. Restricted to Honours students with third year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory third year standing. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
description: Application of carbonyl group chemistry, cyclization reactions, conformational analysis and rearrangement reactions in organic synthesis. Prerequisite: CHEM 213.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory II
description: Further development of principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM 315.

subject: CHEM
title: Global Challenges: A Chemical Perspective
description: Importance of chemistry in society. Detailed case studies drawn from modern chemistry: human health, energy, commodity chemicals, materials, green chemistry, agriculture. Prerequisite: one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 211, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 260.

subject: CHEM
title: Integrated Chemistry Laboratory II
description: Further development of principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry Major or Honours specializations. Prerequisite: CHEM_V 325.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory
description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry for students in Combined Major in Science or a Minor in Chemistry integrating experiments from organic, inorganic, physical and analytical chemistry. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 203, CHEM 211, CHEM 235.

subject: CHEM
title: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the winter term of the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the summer following the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM_V 398. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Spectroscopy
description: Rotational, vibrational, electronic and magnetic resonance spectroscopy and associated techniques; group theory. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and one of CHEM_V 312, PHYS_V 304.

subject: CHEM
title: Diffraction Methods
description: Crystal structures; point and space groups; X-ray diffraction, neutron diffraction, electron diffraction of gases and surfaces. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 402 or CHEM 514. Prerequisite: CHEM 208.

subject: CHEM
title: Surface Chemistry and Surface Analysis
description: Surfaces and phenomena occurring at surfaces and interfaces: adsorption, thermodynamic treatments, technological applications. Methods for characterization and modification of surfaces. Dynamic electrochemistry and its application to understanding fuel cells. Prerequisite: CHEM_V 304 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253.

subject: CHEM
title: Computational Chemistry
description: Application of numerical techniques to study chemical systems; molecular simulation. Prior computer programming experience is not required. . Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 154 and one of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 170 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121 and Third-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Biophysical Chemistry
description: Interactions of macromolecules in solution: ligand, antibody and ion binding to macromolecules; thermodynamics of polymer solutions; excluded volume effects; phase separation; partition in two phase polymer solutions. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 304, CHEM 305, PHYS 203.

subject: CHEM
title: Polymer Chemistry
description: Structure and availability of monomers; Propagation mechanisms; synthesis of polymers with predetermined properties; measurement and interpretation of physical properties of polymers. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 213, CHEM 260 and one of CHEM 205, CHEM 304, CHBE 220.

subject: CHEM
title: Statistical Mechanics in Chemistry
description: Introductory concepts of statistical mechanics and statistical thermodynamics. Applications to chemistry with emphasis on understanding chemical reactivity. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 503/CHEM 407 or PHYS 455. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 304, PHYS 203.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Dynamics
description: Macroscopic and microscopic kinetics; photochemistry; theory of reaction rates; reaction cross sections, energy distributions, experimental methods. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 408 or CHEM 508. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 304, PHYS 203 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 304.

subject: CHEM
title: Astrochemistry
description: Application of physical chemistry concepts and principles to the study of molecules in interstellar media and celestial bodies. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 409 or CHEM 509. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 312, PHYS 304. Students with CHEM 205 with a minimum grade of 76% may be admitted with permission of the instructor.

subject: CHEM
title: Properties of Materials
description: Electromagnetic, optical, thermal and mechanical properties, and chemical reactivity of solids; electrons in periodic systems: bands, zones; excitations: excitons, phonons, plasmons, polaritons; crystalline order and disorder; ionic conductivity. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 410 or CHEM 502. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 304, PHYS 203 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 304.

subject: CHEM
title: Synthesis and Chemistry of Natural Products
description: Methods and tactics for the synthesis of biologically active natural products and analogs, particularly alkaloids, polyketides, steroids and terpenes. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 411 or CHEM 566. Prerequisite: CHEM 460.

subject: CHEM
title: Electronic Structure of Atoms and Molecules
description: Introduction to variational methods; many-electron systems; semi-empirical methods; perturbation theory; computational methods. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 312, PHYS_V 304 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223.

subject: CHEM
title: Bioorganic Chemistry
description: Enzyme catalysis; mechanistic enzymology; chemistry of cofactors; biosynthetic transformations; natural product biosynthesis; topics in chemical biology. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM_V 413, CHEM_V 569, or BIOC_V 403. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 313, CHEM_V 330.

subject: CHEM
title: Coordination Chemistry of the Transition Elements
description: Molecular and electronic structures and reactivities of coordination compounds of the transition elements. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 414 or CHEM 525. Prerequisite: CHEM 218.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical and Theoretical Organic Chemistry
description: Energetics and catalysis in organic reactions. Pericyclic reactions. Substituent effects. Linear free energy relationships. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM_V 416 or CHEM_V 563. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 313, CHEM_V 330.

subject: CHEM
title: Nuclear Chemistry and Radiochemistry
description: Basic treatment of the nucleus, with analogy to concepts in chemistry. Nuclear stabilities and associated radioactive decay processes. Nuclear structure. Applications of radioisotopes in chemistry. The interaction of radiation with matter. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130. and Third year standing. CHEM 312 is recommended.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallic Chemistry
description: The chemistry of compounds containing organic groups directly bonded to metals and metalloids. Emphasis will be placed on the structure and bonding of the compounds and their use in synthetic chemistry. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 418 or CHEM 524. Prerequisite: CHEM 318.

subject: CHEM
title: Establishing a Career in Chemical Research
description: Current research and career perspectives in chemistry. Restricted to Honours students with fourth year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory fourth year standing. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Applications of Materials Chemistry
description: Contemporary materials chemistry, including design and synthesis of materials for energy, electronics, and health applications. Prerequisite: CHEM 327.

subject: CHEM
title: Developments in Contemporary Chemistry
description: A review of modern developments in general chemistry for teachers of Secondary School chemistry (Not for credit in the Faculty of Science). Course is offered periodically in extra-sessional sessions.

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Chemical Separation
description: Unified theory of separation science; liquid and gas chromatography; capillary electrophoresis; electrochemical and spectroscopic detection; separation methods coupled with mass spectrometry and tandem mass spectrometry; biochemical applications. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 434 or CHEM 534. Prerequisite: CHEM 311.

subject: CHEM
title: Bio-Inorganic Chemistry
description: A discussion of the involvement of inorganic chemistry in biological systems. Chemistry of cations, metalloenzymes, and simpler model systems. Reactions of coordinated ligands, chemistry of sulfur and phosphorus. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 435 or CHEM 526. Prerequisite: All of CHEM 218, CHEM 304.

subject: CHEM
title: Projects in Experimental Chemistry
description: Principles of experimental design, practice and problem solving in chemistry, including the opportunity to pursue projects in a research setting. Students cannot take both CHEM_V 445 and CHEM_V 449. Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 345, CHEM_V 335. Students satisfying the prerequisite requirement using CHEM_V 335 must have 4th-year class standing in a Chemistry Combined Major specialization.

subject: CHEM
title: Directed Studies in Chemistry
description: Students will undertake an investigation of a specific topic as agreed upon by the student and the faculty supervisor. Open to third- and fourth-year chemistry students.

subject: CHEM
title: Seminar and Thesis
description: Original research work under the direction of a faculty member. Weekly seminar. Required of all Honours students. Open to Majors students with a satisfactory standing and permission of the department head. Students cannot take both CHEM_V 445 and CHEM_V 449. Prerequisite: Students will have completed their Year 3 laboratory requirements as outlined in their specialization.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Synthesis: A Mechanistic Approach
description: Presentation, mechanistic discussion and analysis of modern synthetic methods using principles of physical organic chemistry. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 460 or CHEM 560. Prerequisite: CHEM 330.

subject: CHEM
title: Synthetic Chemical Biology
description: Synthetic, mechanistic, and biochemical approaches to chemical biology, including the design of drugs, probes, and catalysts. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM_V 461 or CHEM_V 561. . Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 313, CHEM_V 330. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure Determination and Reaction Analysis
description: Application of mass spectrometry and modern spectroscopic techniques, including multidimensional NMR spectroscopy, to reaction analysis and detailed characterization of complex organic and organometallic molecular structures. Prerequisite: CHEM 245 and one of CHEM 313, CHEM 318, CHEM 330.

subject: CHEM
title: Topics in Chemistry
description: Selected topics in a specific area of Chemistry. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the Department. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in a Chemistry specialization and permission of the Department.

subject: CHEM
title: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the summer following fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM_V 399. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHEM
title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the fall term of the fifth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry. Prerequisite: [CHEM498]

subject: PHYS
title: Introductory Physics
description: Kinematics, force, energy, momentum, use of graphs and vectors in physics; thermal energy, heat transfer, Earth's energy balance; electricity. Students with credit for Physics 12 may not obtain credit for this course unless they took AP, IB, or A-level Physics and were offered advanced credit for PHYS 100. Prerequisite: Not open to students with credit for PHYS 12. Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12 is required; Physics 11 is required for first-year students, strongly recommended for others.

subject: PHYS
title: Energy and Waves
description: Fluids, harmonic oscillator, travelling waves, standing waves, sound, and interference of light waves, including diffraction. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity, Light and Radiation
description: Introduction to optics, electricity and magnetism, electric circuits, radioactivity, including biological applications. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 107. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121.

subject: PHYS
title: Enriched Physics 1 (lecture)
description: Classical mechanics including conservation laws, angular momentum of rigid bodies and simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, with an introduction to special relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical mechanics and solid state physics. Prerequisite: Either (a) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, MATH 12 or (b) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, PREC 12 or (c) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, CALC 12 or (d) a score more than 85% in PHYS 100. PHYS 12 = Physics 12; MATH 12 = Principles of Mathematics 12; PREC 12 = Pre-Calculus 12; CALC 12 = Calculus 12. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

subject: PHYS
title: Enriched Physics 1
description: Classical mechanics including conservation laws, angular momentum of rigid bodies and simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, with an introduction to special relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical mechanics and solid state physics. Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, MATH 12 or (b) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, PREC 12 or (c) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, CALC 12 or (d) a score of 85% or higher in PHYS 100. MATH 12 = Principles of Mathematics 12; PREC 12 = Pre-Calculus 12; CALC 12 = Calculus 12; PHYS 12 = Physics 12. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184.

subject: PHYS
title: Enriched Physics II
description: Electricity and magnetism, electrical circuits, induction, electromagnetic waves, Maxwell's equations and applications. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107 or (b) a score of 85% or higher in one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121.

subject: PHYS
title: Enriched Experimental Physics
description: A laboratory course accompanying PHYS 108 with emphasis on data collection and analysis and experimental techniques. Prerequisite: PHYS 107. Corequisite: One of PHYS 108, PHYS 118.

subject: PHYS
title: Dynamics and Waves
description: Kinematics including curvilinear motion. Forces and Newton's laws of motion. Work-energy theorem, conservation of energy. Conservation of momentum, collisions. Torque, rotational dynamics, angular momentum. Oscillations and waves. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS_V 100, PHYS_O 112. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity, Light and Radiation
description: Optics, electricity and magnetism, electric circuits, electromagnetic waves. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 157 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Physics Lab I
description: Introductory laboratory course, with emphasis on data collection, data analysis techniques, and scientific reasoning. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS_V 100, PHYS_O 112. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Physics Lab II
description: A second laboratory course emphasizing the synthesis and development of further sophistication around the data collection, data analysis techniques and scientific reasoning developed in PHYS 119. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 107, PHYS 119.

subject: PHYS
title: Energy and Waves (Lecture)
description: Fluids, harmonic oscillator, travelling waves, standing waves, sound, and interference of light waves, radioactivity including biological applications. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS_V 100, PHYS_O 112. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100.

subject: PHYS
title: Elements of Physics
description: Thermometry, thermal properties of matter, heat, oscillations, waves, sound, wave optics; geometrical optics, elementary electricity and magnetism, simple DC and AC circuits. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

subject: PHYS
title: Introductory Physics for Engineers I
description: Heat, thermodynamics, oscillations, waves, and sound. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

subject: PHYS
title: Introductory Physics for Engineers II
description: Electricity and magnetism, DC and AC circuits, optics. Prerequisite: PHYS 157. Corequisite: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121.

subject: PHYS
title: Introductory Physics Laboratory for Engineers
description: A laboratory course with emphasis on experimental design, measurement and analysis techniques. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100. Corequisite: One of PHYS 157, PHYS 158.

subject: PHYS
title: Mechanics I
description: Statics of particles, equilibrium or rigid bodies, rigid body statics and internal forces, trusses; kinematics: rectilinear motion; dynamics: Newton's second law, friction, impulse, momentum, work and energy. Recommended pre-requisites: one of PHYS 12, PHYS 100 and one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184. Recommended co-requisite: one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121.

subject: PHYS
title: Relativity and Quanta
description: Special relativity: Lorentz transformation, dynamics and conservation laws. Quantum physics: the experimental evidence for quantization; a qualitative discussion of the concepts of quantum mechanics and their application to simple systems of atoms and nuclei. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 153 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103; or (b) SCIE 001.

subject: PHYS
title: Thermal Physics I
description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics and statistical physics; entropy, laws of thermodynamics, heat engines, free energy, phase transitions, Boltzmann statistics, quantum statistics. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 158, SCIE_V 001. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200.

subject: PHYS
title: Intermediate Experimental Physics
description: Use of analog electronics and amplifiers, digital electronics and analog-to-digital conversion and the use of computers in data analysis and simulations in thermodynamic, electronic and modern physics experiments. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 109 or (b) one of PHYS 102, PHYS 153 or (c) SCIE 001 or (d) all of PHYS 158, PHYS 159 or (e) all of PHYS 118, PHYS 119 or (f) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 119. Corequisite: One of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Computational Physics
description: Introduction to UNIX/Linux; software tools for processing, fitting and displaying data; numerical methods and application in the physical sciences. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 158, SCIE_V 001. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222.

subject: PHYS
title: Intermediate Mechanics
description: Review of kinematics, Newton's laws, angular momentum and fixed axis rotation. Rigid body motion, central forces, non-inertial frames of reference. Introduction to Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 170, SCIE_V 001, PHYS_O 111 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200.

subject: PHYS
title: Intermediate Experimental Physics I
description: Analog electronics and amplifiers, digital electronics, analog-to-digital converters and an introduction to use of computers in data analysis and simulations. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118 and one of PHYS_V 109, PHYS_V 119 or (b) PHYS_V 102 or (c) all of PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 159 or (d) SCIE_V 001. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_O 200.

subject: PHYS
title: Intermediate Experimental Physics II
description: Thermodynamics experiments, modern physics experiments and use of computers in data analysis. Prerequisite: PHYS_V 219. Corequisite: MATH_V 215 or MATH_O 225.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Modern Physics
description: Wave-particle duality of matter, special relativity, processes in atomic, nuclear and solid state, and introduction to quantum mechanical devices and techniques. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 158, PHYS 153, SCIE 001.

subject: PHYS
title: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the winter term of the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics. Prerequisite: PHYS_V 200. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: PHYS
title: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics. Prerequisite: PHYS_V 298. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity and Magnetism
description: Maxwell's equations and their applications, electrical fields and potentials of static charge distributions, current, fields of moving charges, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 153, PHYS 158, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 317 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
description: Principles and applications of quantum mechanics, wave mechanics, the Schroedinger equation, expectation values, Hermitian operators, commuting observables, one-dimensional systems, harmonic oscillators, angular momentum, three-dimensional systems. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 200, PHYS 250. Corequisite: One of MATH 257, MATH 316, PHYS 312.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Biophysics
description: Physical principles involved in biological systems at the microscopic and molecular scales. Diffusion, low Reynolds number dynamics, the physicist's view of biomolecular structure, models of molecular motors and membranes. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 153, PHYS 158, SCIE 001 and either (a) PHYS 203 or (b) one of ENPH 257, CHEM 201, CHEM 205 and one of MATH 302, MATH 318, STAT 241, STAT 251, STAT 302.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Mechanics
description: Variational calculus, Lagrangian dynamics, rigid body motion including free and forced precession, Hamiltonian mechanics, Poisson brackets, canonical coordinates, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, action angle variables. Introduction to dynamical chaos: determinism, Lyapunov exponents. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 216, ENPH 270 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258.

subject: PHYS
title: Electrical Laboratory
description: Selected experiments in electromagnetism and electronics; computer data acquisition; advanced data analysis and simulation. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 209, PHYS 229, ENPH 259.

subject: PHYS
title: Machine Learning for Physics and Astronomy Data Analysis
description: Fundamental principles and applications of data-centric research techniques in Physics and Astronomy. Topics include algorithms for data structuring, dimensionality reduction, linear regression and classification, artificial neural nets, convolutional neural nets, unsupervised learning. Prerequisite: One of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200, STAT 203, STAT 241, STAT 251, MATH 318 and one of PHYS 210, CPSC 103, CPSC 110, APSC 160, EOSC 211 and one of PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 158, SCIE 001.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Mathematical Physics
description: The application of ordinary and partial differential equations to physical problems; boundary and initial value problems associated with heat, wave and Laplace equations. Fourier analysis; expansions in Bessel and Legendre functions. Credit will be granted for only one of PHYS 312 and MATH 316. Prerequisite: [MATH215]

subject: PHYS
title: Fluids
description: Kinetic theory: Diffusion, viscosity and sound waves. Introduction to hydrodynamics: Laminar flow, capillary and gravity waves, convection and turbulence. Dimensional analysis. Prerequisite: MATH 215. Corequisite: PHYS 203.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Physics of Materials
description: Crystal structure, elasticity and phonons, elementary electronic transport, defects, alloys, liquid crystals and polymers. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 203, ENPH 257, CHEM 201, CHEM 205, CHEM 304 and one of PHYS 200, PHYS 250, CHEM 312. Corequisite: [MATH215]

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Acoustics
description: Experimental techniques of acoustics: data acquisition hardware and software, microphones, loudspeakers, noise, vibration and modal analysis. Prerequisite: One of ENPH 259, PHYS 209, PHYS 229.

subject: PHYS
title: Electronics Laboratory
description: A project-oriented lab introducing the design and construction of microprocessor-controlled devices. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 209, PHYS 219, ENPH 259.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Physics
description: Quantum physics, nuclear energy and particle physics at a level suitable for third- and fourth-year Science students not proceeding to a physics degree. Not for credit towards a B.Sc. in Astronomy, Biophysics or Physics. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 180, MATH 184 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157; or (b) SCIE 001.

subject: PHYS
title: Energy and Climate
description: The fundamental physics behind global issues of energy use and climate change. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 102, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 108, PHYS 117, PHYS 118, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157, PHYS 158; or (b) SCIE 001.

subject: PHYS
title: Revolutions in Understanding the Universe
description: Ancient Greek ideas of substance and forms and modern concepts of forces and fields. The twentieth-century quantum revolution. The modern universe, from quarks and atoms to the big bang. Quantum paradoxes. Not for credit in the faculties of Science and Applied Science. No mathematics beyond Grade 10 required.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics of Music
description: An introduction to the physical principles important to the production, transmission and perception of musical sounds. The treatment will be non-mathematical; with emphasis on demonstrations. Topics may include the description of sound waves, resonances, scales, physics of hearing, examination of specific musical instruments, etc. Not for credit in the Faculties of Science and Applied Science.

subject: PHYS
title: Physical Science by Inquiry
description: A guided sequence of hands-on science modules intended primarily for prospective elementary schoolteachers, to help them to work constructively in a science teaching role. Not for credit in the Faculties of Science and Applied Science. Prerequisite: Secondary school algebra.

subject: PHYS
title: Frontiers in Physics and Astronomy
description: Current research topics in physics and astronomy are investigated and explored. Technical communication and research skills are studied and developed via oral presentations and written scientific reports on these current research topics. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in a physics honours program or fourth-year standing in a physics or astronomy major program.

subject: PHYS
title: Directed Research Project in Physics
