description: Moves beyond continental landmasses to consider global oceanic connections, mobility and materiality, and seascape epistemologies or ways of knowing through a cultural, social and historical geographies perspective. Restricted to students with third-year standing or above.

subject: GEOG
title: Contemporary Europe: Identity and Geopolitics
description: Political, economic, and social geographies of post Cold War Europe with a special emphasis on east-central Europe: societal transformations in the formerly socialist states; European Union and NATO enlargement; the external relations of these two organizations. Restricted to students with at least second-year standing.

subject: GEOG
title: Geographies of Social Movements in the Americas
description: The politics of North-South solidarity in theory and practice through community service learning models. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: GEOG
title: Geography of Africa
description: A comparative regional analysis of Africa with a focus on contemporary environmental and development issues. Credit will be allowed for only one of GEOG_V 396 or GEOG_V 496. Equivalency: GEOG_V 396.

subject: GEOG
title: Geographies of the Middle East
description: Critical analysis of economic, social, and political development and processes defining the modern Middle East region.

subject: SOCI
title: Introduction to Sociology
description: Introduction to problems in the analysis of social structures and processes. Basic sociological concepts will be introduced and their application demonstrated in various areas of sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 100 or both SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Social Interaction and Culture
description: Culture, identity, social interaction, relationships and socialization. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 101 or SOCI 100.

subject: SOCI
title: Inequality and Social Change
description: Inequality, institutions, social structure and social change. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 102 or SOCI 100.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Family
description: An introduction to contemporary family forms and relations.

subject: SOCI
title: Ethnicity
description: An introduction to the study of the relations between ethnic groups and of the interplay between ethnicity and other social factors.

subject: SOCI
title: Global Population Dynamics
description: Core processes that influence world population patterns and trends.

subject: SOCI
title: Canadian Social Structure
description: Descriptive and analytic survey of such features as demographic characteristics, class structure, ethnicity, and regional variation in Canadian society as a basis for understanding current social issues.

subject: SOCI
title: Research Methods
description: An introduction to sociological research methods. Diverse types of qualitative and quantitate data and methods to answer research questions. Prerequisite: One of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102, SOCI_V 200.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Indigenous Peoples
description: Sociological perspective of Indigenous peoples and issues both internationally and within Canada.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Personal Life
description: A sociological examination of everyday life exploring the social in the personal.

subject: SOCI
title: Shopping, Society, and Sustainability
description: Major theories of consumer society, evaluating impacts of shopping on human and non-human environments and popular solutions to these impacts.

subject: SOCI
title: Introduction to Social Interaction
description: Research on social interaction, with an emphasis on group (as opposed to individual) processes and behaviour.

subject: SOCI
title: Crime and Society
description: Crime as a social phenomenon, with emphasis on the changing definitions of crime in relation to social and political change in Canadian and other societies.

subject: SOCI
title: Work, Technology, and Society
description: Social forces responsible for changing patterns of technological innovation and work organization in modern industrial societies. Emphasis on the organization of work, labour force dynamics, and technological change.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Creativity
description: The application of sociological concepts to the examination of creative processes.

subject: SOCI
title: Data and Society
description: Impacts of changing information and communication technologies on societies and social interactions.

subject: SOCI
title: Health and Society
description: An introduction to health and illness through a sociological lens.

subject: SOCI
title: Citizenship and Identity
description: The concepts of citizenship, identity, and human rights as social processes shaping individuals and communities (both local and global).

subject: SOCI
title: Global Pandemics
description: Global pandemics in relation to social inequality, social interaction and social institutions.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of International Development
description: Causes and consequences of uneven development in countries throughout the world. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Ethnic and Racial Inequality
description: A critical examination of classical and contemporary theories and research evidence concerning ethnic and racial inequality at the societal and interpersonal levels. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Migration
description: Sociological approaches to the movement of peoples and its impact over time. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Canadian Society
description: Social organization of Canadian society: relationships between social institutions and social processes (e.g., economics, education, family, law, media, and politics); including issues of ancestry, ethnicity, gender, region, and social class. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Gender Relations
description: The nature of gender relations, their social and cultural expression, and theories of gender inequality. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Masculinity
description: How masculinity differs across social contexts and time periods. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Diversity in Family Forms
description: An examination of diversity within and between families and of diverse family forms. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 or SOCI_V 200 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of the Life Course
description: Individuals and families through the life course. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 or SOCI_V 200 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Social Statistics I
description: The testing of sociological theories using quantitative data analysis techniques on numerical data from social surveys, experiments and official statistics. SOCI 328 excludes credit for a number of other statistics courses in various departments. Please consult the Science Credit Exclusion List ( https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… ) before registering. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Adornment
description: The application of sociological concepts to the understanding of objects that we use to adorn our bodies. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Consumers and Consumption
description: The structure and culture of consuming and consumption. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Aging
description: Demographic, economic, and social trends associated with aging, ageism, and aging populations. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 or SOCI_V 200 before taking this course. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI_V 344 and SOCI_V 444. Equivalency: SOCI_V 444. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Work and Inequality
description: The meaning of work and leisure, properties of work organization, the division of labour, and the relation of work and social inequality. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Community Studies
description: Study of the organization of human communities; a focus upon collective activities including family, work, neighbourhood, and formal and informal networks. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology and Natural Resources
description: Sociological perspectives on property, resource industries (such as agriculture, fishing, forestry and mining), resource development, and resource communities. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Social Inequality
description: Tendencies toward equality and inequality; manifestations of inequality (occupation, education, gender, ethnicity, income, power) and their consequences; caste and class features of major stratification systems; theories of social class; stratification profile of contemporary industrial societies. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Built Environments
description: Physical, social, and economic aspects of built environments, including housing and community planning. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Sexualities
description: Sexual identities, communities, practices, and norms across social and historical contexts. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 or SOCI_V 200 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociological Theories: Classical and Contemporary Approaches
description: An examination of selected traditions, conceptual problems, and current topics in the field of sociological theory. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 370 or both SOCI 371, SOCI 372. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Classical Traditions in Theory
description: An examination of selected traditions, conceptual problems and topics in the foundational theories of sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 371 or SOCI 370. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Contemporary Directions in Theory
description: A survey of theories in contemporary sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 372 or SOCI 370. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociological Methods: Survey Research
description: Questionnaire design, interviewing, sampling, and analysis of survey data. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 217.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociological Methods: Experimental Research
description: Research strategies associated with the implementation of experimental methods in sociology. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociological Methods: Qualitative Research
description: Examination of the different traditions of qualitative sociological inquiry and the associated methodological features used to study the interpretive practices and meanings in the everyday lives of individuals. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociological Methods: Historical Research
description: Key approaches and debates in historical research methods. Using archival sources, historical texts, and sociological arguments to?examine how the past shapes the present. Prerequisite: One of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 and SOCI_V 217.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Health and Illness
description: Classic and contemporary sociological perspectives on health, illness, and health care. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Drugs and Society
description: Social dimensions of the causes, consequences, regulation, and treatment of substance use from Canadian and international perspectives. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Selected Topics in Canadian Society
description: Selected areas of study relating to Canadian society such as BC Studies; French Canada's demographic problems; rural communities; social welfare and community programs in Canada. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Feminist Theory
description: The emergence of feminist theory, its relationship to sociology, and the major theoretical schools of thought. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Theories of Family and Kinship
description: Theoretical approaches to the study of the family and family forms. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 200.

subject: SOCI
title: Selected Topics in Sociological Theory
description: An in-depth examination of selected sociological theories. Consult the department for this year's offerings. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Social Statistics II
description: Primary emphasis on applications of statistical techniques to data in Sociology. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above. Prerequisite: SOCI_V 328.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of the Environment
description: Sociological approaches to the study of environmental conflicts, issues, movements, impact of changing technology, economic development on the environment. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Food
description: Cultural, economic, and political aspects of food production and consumption, including connections to class, ethnicity, and gender. Food-related social movements will be included. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Urban Sociology
description: Demographic, behavioural, and organizational aspects of urban structures and of urbanization in different societies and periods. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Global Citizenship
description: Sociology approaches to global citizenship, including its contested nature and intellectual lineage.

subject: SOCI
title: Directed Studies
description: General reading and/or a research undertaking, with the agreement, and under the supervision, of a Department faculty member selected by the student. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above. And permission of the Department.

subject: SOCI
title: International Service Learning
description: International field placement normally for eight to ten weeks; pre-departure seminars (eight to twelve seminars or equivalent) with student presentation seminars upon return from the field.

subject: SOCI
title: Economic Sociology
description: Analysis of economic actions and institutions using the concepts and methods of sociology. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Society, Economy and Family
description: The study of family in social and economic contexts. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 or SOCI_V 200 before taking this course. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI_V 441 and FMST_V 440. Equivalency: FMST_V 440. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Families and Work
description: The effect of combining family and work roles. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, SOCI_V 102 or SOCI_V 200 before taking this course. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI_V 442 and FMST_V 442. Equivalency: FMST_V 442. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Honours Tutorial
description: Requires the presentation of at least one research paper. Restricted to students in the Sociology Honours program. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

subject: SOCI
title: Political Sociology
description: The social and economic bases of political power, including the study of the state, ideology, political movements, revolutions, and political violence. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Social Movements
description: A study of the sources, stages, and effects of social movements in developing and modernized societies. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of the Arts
description: An examination of the arts as social practices from the standpoint of the relationships among artists, critics, patrons, and public; and the social institutions through which these relationships are structured. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Education
description: Examines the role of schooling in modern society including links with inequality, knowledge production, socialization and the economy. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Queer Theory and Politics
description: Empirical expressions and political possibilities of queer theory. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above. Prerequisite: SOCI_V 369.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Crime and Justice
description: Critical examination of specific forms of crime in relation to the criminal justice system including law, enforcement, and corrections. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Mental Illness
description: A sociological approach to the meaning of mental illness; the organization of psychiatric treatment; problems in the explanation of the distribution of mental illness in a population. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Sociology of Soccer
description: Soccer and colonialism, soccer and global politics, and inequalities in soccer by gender, sexuality, race and class. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Social Determinants of Health
description: Relationships between social phenomena (e.g., personal beliefs, lifestyle practices, social support, socio-economic status, social class, gender, and ethnicity) and the health of human populations. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Urban Ethnographic Field School (UEFS)
description: Approximately 50 hours of volunteering and fieldwork based in community organizations with theoretical approaches to urban spaces. Students will engage in collaborative research while considering a range of theoretical and methodological approaches. Students may earn a maximum of 6 credits from ANTH_V 480 and SOCI_V 480. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Contemporary Chinese Society
description: Current social topics in Chinese society; perspectives on gender, inequality, culture, and social relations. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: SOCI
title: Advanced Studies in Sociology
description: An intensive examination of selected topics in Sociology. Consult the department for this year's offerings. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI_V 100, SOCI_V 101, or SOCI_V 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

subject: FREN
title: Beginners' French I
description: Basic vocabulary, the rudiments of grammar and familiarization with cultures of the French-speaking world. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Not for credit for students who completed Core French 11, 12 and/or French Immersion (BC Curriculum or equivalent). Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 101 or FREN_V 103.

subject: FREN
title: Beginners' French II
description: A continuation of FREN_V 101. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Not for credit for students who completed Core French 11, 12 and/or French Immersion (BC Curriculum or equivalent). This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 101. Credits will be granted for only one of FREN_V 102 or FREN_V 103.

subject: FREN
title: Intensive Beginners' French
description: Fundamentals of the French language. Aligned with CEFR level A1. This course is recommended for students who are not complete beginners in French. Credit will be granted for FREN_V 103 or both FREN_V 101, FREN_V 102.

subject: FREN
title: Elementary French I
description: Continued improvement in listening, speaking, reading and writing. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of Core French 11, FREN_V 102, FREN_V 103 or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 201 or FREN_V 111. Equivalency: FREN_V 111.

subject: FREN
title: Elementary French II
description: A continuation of FREN_V 201. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 201 or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 202 or FREN_V 112. Equivalency: FREN_V 112.

subject: FREN
title: Intermediate French I
description: Refinement of reading, writing and speaking skills through the study of contemporary literature and other authentic documents of the French-speaking world. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of Core French 12, FREN_V 202 or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 301 or FREN_V 122. Equivalency: FREN_V 122.

subject: FREN
title: Intermediate French II
description: A continuation of FREN _V 301. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 301 or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 302 or FREN_V 123. Equivalency: FREN_V 123.

subject: FREN
title: Introduction to Literature in French
description: Critical reading of foundational literary texts in French from genres of prose fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and theatre. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 302 or assignment based on placement test.

subject: FREN
title: Critical Writing
description: Practical tools for university-level writing in French. Apply stylistic devices and rhetorical structures to form questions and arguments, analyse literary and cultural objects, and produce a variety of essay genres. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 302 or assignment based on placement test.

subject: FREN
title: Introduction to Quebec Literature
description: Survey of representative literary texts from Quebec viewed in their historical, social, and cultural contexts. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

subject: FREN
title: Arts, Cultures and Society from the Middle Ages to the Revolution
description: Exploration of early French culture and literature from the Middle Ages to the close of the Early Modern period and the French Revolution; the impact of society on the arts and vice versa. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

subject: FREN
title: Arts, Cultures and Society from Romanticism to the Present Day
description: Exploration of modern and contemporary French culture and literature from the early 19th century to the present day; the impact of society on the arts and vice versa. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

subject: FREN
title: French at Work
description: Communicative French for students preparing for a career in the francophone world. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 123 or FREN_V 302.

subject: FREN
title: French Grammar
description: Principles of grammar theory and contextualized French grammatical concepts. Emphasis on terminology and analysis of grammatical issues. Aligned with CEFR level B2. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 123 or FREN_V 302.

subject: FREN
title: Advanced French Grammar
description: Advanced grammar theory and critical analysis of difficult French grammatical structures. Emphasis on autonomous examination of complex grammatical issues. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401. Prerequisite: One of FREN_V 223, FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: French to English Translation
description: Principles, practical strategies and methods of translation from French to English. Overview of the main challenges involved in intercultural communication. If your French is stronger than your English, please take FREN_V 457 before FREN_V 357. This course is recommended for students who have taken FREN_V 352, and one of FREN_V 224, FREN_V 401.

subject: FREN
title: Introduction to French Linguistics
description: A survey of basic terminology, methods, problems, and theoretical trends in French linguistics, specifically designed to provide students with a foundation for advanced language study in French. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

subject: FREN
title: Special Topics Abroad
description: Study of Francophone literature, history, culture, or communities in an authentic context. Topics and locations may vary. Consult Department for current offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 202 or FREN_V 112 or assignment based on placement test.

subject: FREN
title: Upper-Intermediate French I
description: Communicative proficiency at an autonomous level: vocabulary enrichment, pronunciation practice, grammatical analysis and development of efficient reading and writing techniques. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of French Immersion 12, FREN_V 123 or FREN_V 302 or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 401 or FREN_V 224. Equivalency: FREN _V 224.

subject: FREN
title: Upper-Intermediate French II
description: A continuation of FREN_V 401. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 401 or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 402 or FREN_V 225. Equivalency: FREN _V 225.

subject: FREN
title: Medieval French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of French-language literature of the Middle Ages (11th-15th centuries) in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Renaissance: Studies in 16th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of sixteenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Ancients and Moderns: Studies in 17th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of seventeenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Enlightenment and Revolution: Studies in 18th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of eighteenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Tradition and Modernity: Studies in 19th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of nineteenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: The Modern and Contemporary French Novel
description: Major historical, social and artistic movements reflected in representative novels published in France from the 19th Century to the present. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: French Digital Culture
description: Contemporary issues and debates on how media and digital technologies have impacted French culture and society. Examines how text, language, and writing are used in digital media. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Contemporary French Literature and Culture
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of twentieth- and twenty-first century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Popular Fiction
description: Popular genres in modern French fiction, including science fiction, crime, romance, fantasy and historical fiction. Aesthetic characteristics, historical context and cultural relevance. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: African and Caribbean Francophone Literatures
description: Representative and contemporary writings from African and Caribbean francophone cultures. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Women's Writing
description: Representative women's writings from the Middle Ages to the present; contemporary women's writings in the Francophone world. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Selected Topics in French Literature and Culture
description: Study of a literary or cultural topic that extends beyond one chronological period and/or place proper. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: French Cinema
description: Study of major past and contemporary French film productions. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Francophone Cinema
description: Study of major past and contemporary film productions from around the Francophone world. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Quebec Literature and Culture
description: Study of representative aspects of Quebec literature and culture through the study of literary texts, films, and artistic productions in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Indigenous Literatures of Francophone Canada
description: Study of the literature and cinema of First Nations, Inuit and Métis creators working in French and in Francophone spaces in Canada. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Francophonie: History and Current Debates
description: Historical origins, cultural and linguistic paradoxes of Francophonie. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Francophone Literatures and Cultures of North America
description: Forms of French language cultural expression in North America in their historical context. Discussion of issues around minority linguistic and cultural rights. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Cultures of the Francophone World
description: Forms of cultural expression of the Francophone world studied in their context. Regions may include the Americas, Africa, East Asia, Europe, Indian Ocean, Middle East, and/or the Pacific. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Postcolonial Studies
description: Interdisciplinary approaches to Postcolonial Studies through francophone literature and theory. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Old French
description: The phonetics, grammar, and vocabulary of major Old French dialects; corpus of various literary texts. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FREN
title: French Phonetics
description: Theory and practice of the sound system of the French language. Anatomy of speech production, sound discrimination, phonetic description and transcription. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: Creative Writing in French
description: Theory, techniques and practice of creative writing in French in a variety of genres. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: English to French Translation
description: Extensive practice in English-French translation of a wide range of texts and discourses, such as literary, legal, medical, administrative, commercial materials. Analysis of linguistic and cultural problems posed by translation of specialized material. If your French is stronger than your English, please take FREN_V 457 before FREN_V 357. This course is recommended for students who have taken FREN_V 352, FREN_V 357, and one of FREN_V 225, FREN_V 402.

subject: FREN
title: History of the French Language
description: Overview of the development of the French language from its Latin roots to its modern forms. Examination of the internal and external factors which brought about changes in its phonology, morphology, syntax and lexis. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: Studies in Modern French Linguistics
description: Current topics in French linguistics. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: Morphology and Syntax of the French Language
description: Analytical principles pertaining to the study of words and word-stems (morphology), and phrases and sentences (syntax) in written and spoken French. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: Lexicology and Semantics of the French Language
description: Study of the vocabulary of modern French, focusing on basic principles in lexical semantics, lexicology, phraseology, lexicography, terminology and new technologies, neology. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: French Language and Societies
description: Study of language in its social context, covering aspects of sociolinguistics within and across the French-speaking communities of the world. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: Contemporary Varieties of French
description: Study of the different varieties (or dialects) of contemporary French and issues related to French-speaking communities around the world. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: French Theory
description: Core ideas of French theorists. Influence of French theory on the social sciences and humanities, focusing on Marxism, feminism, structuralism, deconstruction, postmodernism and postcolonialism. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: History of the Book
description: A historical approach to the social transformations of the book trade in France. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Early Encounters: Travel Literature and Colonial Writing in French
description: Narratives of travel and exploration in French before 1800 and their relationship to colonization, knowledge production and representations of the self and others. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Research Seminar in French Literature and Culture
description: Research on critical topics related to French literature and culture. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 311.

subject: FREN
title: Research Seminar in French Language and Linguistics
description: Research on critical topics related to French language and linguistics. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below. Prerequisite: FREN_V 352.

subject: FREN
title: Directed Reading
description: Focus on a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of the department head and of a supervisory faculty member is required. This course is recommended for the fourth year students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402.

subject: FREN
title: Honours Essay
description: Restriction: this course is restricted to students in one of these programs: BA in fourth-year with one of these specializations: HON FREN or HON RMST.

subject: MUSC
title: Principles of Musical Form
description: Explain rhythmic, melodic, textural, and harmonic materials and processes of music, and how they create small-scale structures. Fluency with music notation advised. B.Mus. and B.A. Music students with a strong background in music theory may test into MUSC_V 101.

subject: MUSC
title: Diatonic Harmony and Voice Leading
description: Harmonic and linear functions of diatonic chords; common progressions and sequences; introduction to tonal hierarchy and prolongation; simple modulation. Compositional and analytical exercises. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 100, MUSC 110.

subject: MUSC
title: Introduction to the Theory of Music
description: Concepts of rhythm, pitch, timbre, and texture. Notation and aural recognition of rhythmic and pitch patterns. Basic principles of melody and form. Background in Western music theory or notation unnecessary. This course is inapplicable to the B.Mus. or B.A. Music.

subject: MUSC
title: Introduction to Diatonic Harmony
description: Triads, key and elementary harmony in Western music. Elements of musical form. Aural training and exercises in composition, modeled on historical styles. Not for credit in the B.Mus. Prerequisite: [MUSC103] or permission of the instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Aural Skills I
description: Sight singing; melodic and harmonic dictation; rhythm production; error detection; tuning; perception of harmony, form, and tonality; improvisation in set idioms. Restricted to B.Mus. students. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Aural Skills II
description: Continuation of MUSC_V 105. Restricted to B.Mus. students. Prerequisite: a score of 68% or higher in MUSC_V 105. Students may register for MUSC_V 106 prior to meeting the pre-requisite but will be required to withdraw if the pre-requisite is not met by the first day of class. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Composition I
description: An introduction to musical composition.

subject: MUSC
title: Introduction to Contemporary Art Music
description: Contemporary music repertoire, emphasizing music from the past fifty years. Required of undergraduate Composition majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Class Brasses and Percussion
description: Group instruction in music performance. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

subject: MUSC
title: Introduction to Music Technology
description: Practical and theoretical training in technologies that support current artistic and academic practice, such as MIDI, podcasts/videocasts, websites, social media, and software for score notation, music education, and basic audio/video editing.

subject: MUSC
title: History of Music I
description: An overview of Western music from antiquity through the Middle Ages and Renaissance, providing a framework for understanding musical styles and practices, and examining selected compositions in greater analytical and historical depth.

subject: MUSC
title: History of Music II
description: The development of Western music from circa 1600 to circa 1800. Prerequisite: MUSC 120. Or permission of the instructor

subject: MUSC
title: Class Woodwinds
description: Group instruction in music performance. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

subject: MUSC
title: Music and Human Experience
description: A multi-disciplinary survey of music in selected world traditions and genres, connecting it to ideas of time, evolution, history, anthropology, philosophy, and contemporary globalised culture.

subject: MUSC
title: Class Voice
description: Group instruction in music performance. Required of all first-time secondary voice students. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

subject: MUSC
title: Opera Repertoire I
description: A musico-dramatic study and analysis of representative works in the international operatic theatre from 1600 to the present, through musical, literary and graphic sources. Each sequential year of study, the student is expected to show increased facility in musical and dramatic analysis as well as a greater understanding of the works under examination. Open to students outside the B.Mus. program by permission of the instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Piano Repertoire I
description: Performance and discussion of the repertoire for string-keyboard instruments essential to the performer and teacher. Special attention to matters of structure, style, and performance practices. Required of piano performance majors and open to piano concentrators, space permitting. First term prerequisite to second term.

subject: MUSC
title: Class Piano I
description: Required of all first-time secondary piano students.

subject: MUSC
title: Collaborative Piano I
description: Skills and performance practice with primary emphasis on voice/piano partnership principles and repertoire. Strong sight-reading skills essential. For Piano majors; open to others by audition.

description: Symphony Orchestra, Symphonic Wind Ensemble, or Concert Winds. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC

description: Performance of early Western instrumental and vocal ensemble music. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Contemporary Players (Lower Years)
description: Performance of contemporary music. An ensemble of variable size, including both instrumentalists and singers, will be formed to present several concerts of 20th-century music during the academic year. May be taken twice for credit. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Jazz Ensemble (Lower Years)
description: Performance techniques and repertoire. May be taken twice for credit. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: World Music Ensembles (Lower Years)
description: Training on traditional instruments and their techniques, with emphasis on ensemble performance. Different sections focus on the music of different cultures, e.g., Bali, China, Ghana, Korea. May be taken twice for credit. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Introduction to Piano Chamber Music
description: A survey of repertoire and performance issues.

subject: MUSC
title: Intensive Chamber Ensemble (Lower Years)
description: Intensive coaching in chamber ensemble for advanced players. Performance of works prepared is expected. May be taken twice for credit. Corequisite: Any small ensemble (MUSC 156-166) and permission of the instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Lyric Diction
description: A study of the basic phonetics and accepted principles of lyric diction of the four languages most commonly used in concert and operatic repertoire: French, German, Italian, and English.

description: Study of various forms in tonal music and the rhythmic, melodic, textural, and harmonic processes that create them on small and large scales. Compositional and analytical exercises. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 111, MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC

description: The development of Western music from circa 1900; an introduction to jazz and popular music and to music of selected non-Western societies. Prerequisite: All of MUSC 220, MUSC 100.

subject: MUSC
title: Compositional and Analytical Approaches to Post-Tonal Music
description: Concepts essential to understanding and performing art music, since 1900, in which functional triadic harmony is absent or subsidiary to other musical processes. Detailed consideration of works of major composers up to the present, through analysis, composition, and musicianship exercises. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Readings in Orchestral Repertoire
description: Laboratory course for orchestral performance majors. Emphasis on reading a large cross-section of standard orchestral repertoire, especially music currently being programmed by local professional orchestras. Restricted to Orchestral Instruments majors, except by permission of the instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Composition III
description: Continuation of MUSC_V 207. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 207 and permission of Composition Division based on submission of scores.

subject: MUSC
title: Instrumentation
description: The study of string, woodwind, brass and percussion instruments; orchestral sections and scoring for various small ensembles. Activities include demonstrations of instruments, scoring projects, analysis and listening. For credit towards the B.Mus. and the B.A. in Music; not open to other students. Prerequisite: MUSC 200. and completion of the second-year piano requirement.

subject: MUSC
title: Orchestration
description: The study of orchestration through the analysis of orchestral works, listening and scoring projects. Activities also include choral arranging and scoring for stage band and wind ensemble. Prerequisite: [MUSC309]

subject: MUSC
title: Fundamentals of Conducting
description: Basic conducting techniques: patterns, cueing, dynamic shading, and physical presentation. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 200 and completion of the second-year piano requirement.

subject: MUSC
title: Instrumental Conducting
description: The relation of conducting gestures to instrumental sound; development of practical skills in directing ensembles and reading scores, considering instruments' special characteristics. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 311.

subject: MUSC
title: Choral Conducting
description: The relation of conducting gestures to choral sound; development of practical skills in directing ensembles and reading scores; attendant issues of vocal technique and pedagogy. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 311.

subject: MUSC
title: Electroacoustic Music
description: Study of acoustics, audio technology, and electroacoustic composition. Composition of original works using the UBC Electroacoustic Music Studio or students' own software/hardware. Prerequisite: MUSC 119 and one of MUSC 100, MUSC 103. Permission of instructor is also required.

subject: MUSC
title: Computer Music
description: The study of computer applications to music, focusing on digital synthesis techniques and languages, methods of algorithmic composition, and the design of music editors. Prerequisite: [MUSC319] or permission of instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Music Appreciation, Twentieth-Century
description: Designed for students with little or no musical background. Not for credit toward the B.Mus. or B.A. in Music.

subject: MUSC
title: Topics in Western Music
description: Study in one major genre of Western music (e.g., The Symphony, Women in Opera, History of the Song Cycle). No musical knowledge is required. Not for credit toward the B.Mus. or B.A. in Music.

subject: MUSC
title: History of Popular Music
description: Genres of popular music from 1950 to the present and their changing aesthetic, social, cultural, and historical dimensions. Prior experience with music notation and terminology is not required. This course is not acceptable for credit toward the B.Mus., or toward the B.A. major, honours, or minor in Music.

subject: MUSC
title: The Guitar in History and Practice
description: Introduction to guitar performance and repertoire for non-majors. Lectures explore guitar repertoires from selected regions and eras. Not for credit toward the B.Mus. or the Major/Minor in Music (B.A., B.F.A., B.Sc.). Students are expected to provide their own guitars.

subject: MUSC
title: Music Appreciation
description: An introductory course for which previous musical background is helpful, but not required. Contents include a discussion of musical concepts, evolution of forms, style, and media and detailed study of selected works from the concert repertoire. Popular forms of music (jazz, folk, rock, etc) not included. Not for credit towards the B.Mus. or B.A. in Music.

subject: MUSC
title: Cantonese Music
description: A history of musical genres with Cantonese lyrics from the nineteenth century to the present. Topics include music and text relationships, major singers, major genres (narrative songs, Cantonese opera, Cantopop). Credit will be granted for only one of MUSC_V 327 or ASIA_V 335. Equivalency: ASIA_V 335.

subject: MUSC
title: World Music Cultures
description: Introduction to the principles of ethnomusicology and an examination of at least two contrasting musical traditions. May be repeated once for credit if different traditions are covered.

subject: MUSC
title: Music in Vancouver's Ethnic Communities
description: Examination of music within the ethnic context as found in the urban environment of Vancouver. The musics of several traditions (e.g., Chinese, Jewish, English folk) will be studied together with the social issues surrounding their preservation. For credit toward the B.Mus. and the B.A. in Music, but open to students not majoring in music.

subject: MUSC
title: Workshop in World Rhythm
description: Theory and practice of selected rhythmic systems of world music cultures, focusing on West African drumming, and including other systems such as Indian Tala and Peking opera percussion. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Accompanying on the Harpsichord I
description: Basic techniques and styles of continuo playing. Open to keyboard players with no previous harpsichord experience.

subject: MUSC
title: Opera Theatre Techniques I
description: Performance techniques associated with the musical theatre of various historical periods. Basic dance. Most operatic excerpts will be in English.

subject: MUSC
title: Opera Workshop I
description: Participation in performances by the School. Open also to students outside Music without credit, after audition.

subject: MUSC
title: Piano Pedagogy I: Theory and Studio Management
description: Basic principles of teaching piano. Business aspects of establishing and maintaining a music studio. For Piano Performance majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of the instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Aesthetics and Practice of Film Music

subject: MUSC
title: Keyboard Harmony and Transposition
description: Designed for the keyboard performance major and keyboard concentrator in General Studies.

subject: MUSC

description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 151. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC

description: Sacred and secular music, vocal and instrumental. Prerequisite: All of MUSC 120, MUSC 121.

subject: MUSC
title: History of Jazz
description: Jazz styles and their cultural contexts; the relationship of performers and audiences; issues of race and gender; non-Western influences. Prerequisite: MUSC 221.

subject: MUSC
title: University Chamber Strings (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 159. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: String Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Piano Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)

subject: MUSC
title: Wind and Percussion Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 162. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: History and Repertoire of the Guitar and Related Instruments
description: A chronological survey, from the Renaissance to the present day, of music for the guitar and related instruments and of the development of the instruments themselves. Instruments considered include Renaissance and Baroque lutes, the vihuela, and early types of guitar as well as the modern six-string guitar. Musical forms and genres, national schools and the works of principal composers of every period are explored and attention is given to national systems, continuo realization, historical ornamentation and pedagogical systems. Prerequisite: [MUSC221]

subject: MUSC
title: Song Repertoire I
description: An exploration of the solo art song repertoire from 1600 to the Romantic period. Repertoire essential to the performer and teacher will be studied through live and recorded performance with special attention given to poetic content and musical style. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: University Choral Union (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 154. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Intensive Chamber Ensemble (Upper Years)
description: Intensive coaching in chamber ensemble for advanced players. Performance of works prepared is expected. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Corequisite: One of MUSC 350, MUSC 351, MUSC 359, MUSC 360, MUSC 361, MUSC 362, MUSC 366, MUSC 453, MUSC 456, MUSC 457, MUSC 463, MUSC 466. and permission of the instructor. description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC_V 271, MUSC_V 272, MUSC_V 281, MUSC_V 283, MUSC_V 291, MUSC_V 292, MUSC_V 293.

subject: MUSC
title: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC_V 271, MUSC _V 272, MUSC_V 281, MUSC_V 283, MUSC_V 291, MUSC_V 292, MUSC_V 293. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Special Projects
description: For fourth-year students who receive permission of the Director of the School of Music to do advanced studies in their major field.

subject: MUSC
title: Selected Topics in Music
description: See School of Music schedule for description and prerequisites. Restricted to B. Mus. and B.A. in Music students.

subject: MUSC
title: Composition IV
description: Continuation of MUSC_V 307.

subject: MUSC
title: Jazz Theory and Arranging
description: Jazz scales, chord relationships, substitutions, orchestration, listening, and score analysis. Restricted to B.Mus. and B.A. in Music students. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Introduction to Schenkerian Analysis
description: The key concepts of Schenker's theory of tonality. Applications to the analysis of short pieces in various tonal styles, emphasizing clear and correct graphing. Issues of interpretive scope. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Analysis of Tonal Music
description: Analytical approaches that complement Schenkerian analysis, including motivic construction, harmonic rhythm and phrase rhythm, chromaticism and enharmonicism, features of musical form, aspects of structure and hierarchy at the small and large scale. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Analytical Studies in the Development of Musical Modernism (1860 - 1940)
description: Analysis of late- and post-romantic works within a theoretical framework that bridges earlier to later works. Assignments in various formats, emphasizing analysis but possibly including composition. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Contemporary Art Music: Theory and Analysis
description: A technical approach to the diverse concert-music repertoire since 1950, including orchestral, chamber, solo, and electro-acoustic genres. Applicable theories of pitch and rhythm, with reference to composers' own writings. Prerequisite: MUSC 300.

subject: MUSC
title: Counterpoint
description: Analysis and composition of pieces that rely on the control and development of imitative, polyphonic textures. Models to be taken from one or more European historical repertoires. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Imagining Musical Performances
description: How performance and analysis engage the musical imagination, as complementary activities; how analytical observations can stimulate performance, and vice versa. Selected topics, with special emphasis on temporal factors. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

subject: MUSC
title: Musical Scoring for Film
description: Addresses the practical aspects of composing music for film through assignments of written scores. Prerequisite: [MUSC319] Permission of instructor is required.

subject: MUSC
title: Interactive Performance Systems
description: Collaborative projects developing new connections between sound and gestures in live concert performance or responsive environments using multiple digital technologies. May be repeated once for credit. Prerequisite: MUSC 320.

subject: MUSC
title: Music Technology Capstone Project
description: Supervised individual music technology project on an approved topic. Restricted to students in the Minor in Applied Music Technology Prerequisite: MUSC 419. And permission of the Instructor.

subject: MUSC
title: Topics in World Music
description: The history, theory, style, organology, and forms of the music of a particular culture in its aesthetic and cultural context. Students should consult the School as to which music culture will be covered in a particular year. May be repeated once for credit if different cultures are covered. Prerequisite: [MUSC328] or instructor's permission.

subject: MUSC
title: Major Composers
description: The musical works of no more than two significant composers will be examined. Specific topics will be announced; may be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: All of MUSC 120, MUSC 121, MUSC 220, MUSC 221.

subject: MUSC
title: Accompanying on the Harpsichord II
description: Continuation of MUSC_V 333 with emphasis on more advanced continuo and obbligato techniques. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 333.

subject: MUSC
title: Opera Theatre Techniques II
description: Advanced studies in acting, movement, gesture, dance and stage combat. Emphasis on communication and the art of singing and acting recitative in foreign languages.

subject: MUSC
title: Opera Workshop II
description: A continuation of MUSC 339.

subject: MUSC
title: Piano Pedagogy II: Applications
description: Teaching musical concepts and keyboard skills; observation of group and private lessons; supervised practicum. For Piano Performance majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of the instructor. Recommended pre-requisite: MUSC 340.

subject: MUSC
title: Vocal Techniques
description: A study of the scientific principles related to vocal performance: acoustical, physiological and psychological. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

subject: MUSC
title: Song Interpretation
description: Interpretation and performance practice of Art Song repertoire for voice and piano collaborations. Restricted to MMus and BMus in Piano Performance, Opera, Voice Performance, and students in the Diploma in Collaborative Piano Studies program.

subject: MUSC
title: Opera Coaching
description: Principles and practice, focusing on current Opera Workshop repertoire. Reproducing orchestrations on the piano; preparing scores; study of the voice and the rehearsal process; coaching languages; related conducting skills. Prerequisite: [MUSC249]

subject: MUSC
title: Establishing a Career in Music
description: Best practices of the contemporary business of music, focusing on understanding present market conditions, and on targeting specific opportunities through grant-writing, resums, press kits, publicity, recordings, and marketing. Restricted to fourth-year B.Mus. students.

subject: MUSC
title: Historical Performance Practice
description: Principles and practical application of the historically-informed performance of music. Philosophy, aesthetics, and key performance conventions of Western music before ca. 1800. Recommended: concurrent registration in MUSC 157 (Early Music Ensemble).

subject: MUSC
title: Selected Topics in Vocal or Instrumental Genres
description: Intensive study of one genre of music (e.g., orchestral music 17601849; the Lied in Austria and Germany) through analysis and the consideration of cultural milieu and historical development. Specific topics will be announced. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 credits.

subject: MUSC
title: University Singers (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 153. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: History of Opera I
description: The development of opera between 1600 and 1800. Prerequisite: All of MUSC 121, MUSC 220.

subject: MUSC
title: History of Opera II
description: The development of opera between 1800 and the present. Prerequisite: All of MUSC 220, MUSC 221.

subject: MUSC
title: Vocal Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 156. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Early Music Ensemble (Upper Years)
description: Performance of early Western instrumental and vocal ensemble music. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 157. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Contemporary Players (Upper Years)
description: Performance of contemporary music. An ensemble of variable size, including both instrumentalists and singers, will be formed to present several concerts of 20th-century music during the academic year. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 163. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Jazz Ensemble (Upper Years)
description: Performance techniques and repertoire. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 164.

subject: MUSC
title: Song Repertoire II
description: A sequel to MUSC_V 365, exploring the solo art song repertoire from the Romantic era to the present. Prerequisite: MUSC_V 221.

subject: MUSC
title: World Music Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: Training on traditional instruments and their techniques, with emphasis on ensemble performance. Different sections focus on the music of different cultures, e.g., Bali, China, Ghana, Korea. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 165. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MUSC
title: Chamber Music Master Class
description: Enrolment by audition only.

subject: MUSC
title: Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Group projects and workshops with students majoring in other creative arts. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Credit will be granted for only one of MUSC_V 469 or THTR_V 469 or VISA_V 469 or CRWR_V 440. Equivalency: THTR_V 469, VISA_V 469, CRWR_V 440.

subject: MUSC

description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.
