subject: ARTH
title: Ways of Seeing: Introduction to Visual Studies
description: Drawing on examples from across history and around the world, this course deals with the role of the visual in society, culture, and everyday experience.

subject: ARTH
title: World Art and Architecture Before 1800
description: Introduction to the histories of art and the built environment in a global context.

subject: ARTH
title: Byzantium: Arts of an Empire
description: Art, architecture, and material culture of the Byzantine Empire situated in the eastern Mediterranean (c. 300-1453); focus on social and cultural contexts of artistic production, including interactions with neighboring cultures. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 210, CNRS 207 or AMNE 279. Equivalency: AMNE 279

subject: ARTH
title: Art, Patrons, and Audiences in the Middle Ages
description: A thematic study of the relationship between patrons and audiences in painting, sculpture, and architecture through the 15th century.

subject: ARTH
title: Art, Colonialism, and Indigeneity
description: Tensions and conflicts resulting from the expansion of trade and encounters among cultures, ethnicities, and religious practices, explored in visual art and architecture from the sixteenth century to the advent of the modern era.

subject: ARTH
title: What is Modern Art?
description: Select issues in 20th-century art and the visual and built environment.

subject: ARTH
title: Art & Feminism(s): Histories, Lineages, Legacies
description: Feminist art and visual culture, from the political activism of the feminist first wave to its intersections with present-day social justice movements.

subject: ARTH
title: Asian Arts: From Chinese Warriors to Bollywood Posters
description: A thematic examination of Asian arts, such as historic, religious, and secular painting and sculpture to contemporary visual culture.

subject: ARTH
title: Asian Architecture: Sacred and Urban Spaces
description: Select built forms in Asia, such as temples, tombs, palaces, cities and gardens, and their relations to cultural, social and political systems.

subject: ARTH
title: Pre-Hispanic Arts of Central and South America
description: The relevance of various arts to social institutions in ancient societies of Peru and Mesoamerica.

subject: ARTH
title: Indigenous Arts of North America
description: A survey of the artistic production by Indigenous peoples of North America from pre-contact times to the present.

subject: ARTH
title: Art and the Moving Image
description: Intersections between visual art and the moving image in both a theoretical and historical context.

subject: ARTH
title: Special Topics in Art History
description: Thematic and issue-based courses in art history. Topics vary year to year.

subject: ARTH
title: Seminar on Methods and Approaches in Art History
description: Theories, problems, and literature in the study of art history. Required of all Major and Honours students in art history. Prerequisite: 3 credits of ARTH_V coursework at any level. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ARTH
title: Arts of Africa and the African Diasporas
description: Comparative exploration of art practices and their relationship to colonial and postcolonial histories. Credit will be granted for only one of ARTH_V 309 or AFST_V 309. Equivalency: AFST_V 309.

subject: ARTH
title: Art and the Religious Transformation of the Late Roman Empire
description: Visual culture and religious diversity of the Late Roman Empire (2nd-7th c.); social, political, and religious contexts of art, including diverse viewing practices and cultural frameworks. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 310, CNRS 333 or AMNE 379. Equivalency: AMNE 379

subject: ARTH
title: Early Medieval Art
description: From pagan adornment to Christian devotion to service of Christian or Islamic rule (AD 500-1000). Art and architecture of the Early Medieval world's diverse and transforming social, political, cultural contexts.

subject: ARTH
title: Medieval Art in the Age of Monasticism
description: Art in Europe between 1000 and 1200; the role of monasteries as leading institutions and patrons of art and large-scale architecture.

subject: ARTH
title: Art, Church, Society and their Margins in the Later Middle Ages
description: Diversification of the arts and architecture with the expansion of patronage in late medieval society. Credit will be granted for only one of ARTH_V 313 or ARTH_V 333.

subject: ARTH
title: The Archaeology of Ancient Iraq and Syria: Babylon and Beyond
description: An overview of the archaeology of the ancient Near East, with special emphasis on the civilizations of Mesopotamia, from the appearance of the first cities (c. 3400 BCE) to the end of the Persian period (c. 330 BCE). AMNE 170 recommended as preparation. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 319, NEST 319, or AMNE 372 Equivalency: AMNE 372

subject: ARTH
title: Entangled Worlds: Spain and Colonial Latin America (1500-1700)
description: Role of visual art and culture within Catholic Spain and colonial Latin America is surveyed, with emphasis on transculturation from mudejar to mestizaje.

subject: ARTH
title: Public and Private Bodies: Italian Renaissance Art and Culture
description: Visual art and culture within the social, political, and religious contexts of the Papacy and the city-states ca. 1350-1550 (Siena, Florence, Venice, Mantua).

subject: ARTH
title: Early Modern Italian Art and Culture (ca. 1550-1700)
description: Focus primarily on Rome as the center of artistic, cultural, economic, and religious power in the seventeenth century.

subject: ARTH
title: Heaven and Earth: Renaissance Art and Culture in Northern Europe
description: Early Modern painting, sculpture, and the graphic arts from the great devotional triptychs, through the Reformation, to the emergence of a secular art (1400-1600).

subject: ARTH
title: Urban and Courtly Arts in Early Modern Northern Europe (1600-1700)
description: The role of visual art in 17th century court cultures, commercial urban centres, and emergent nation states.

subject: ARTH
title: Ancient Egypt: The Archaeology of the Land of the Pharaohs
description: The material remains of the ancient Egyptians from monumental tombs and temples to the artifacts of daily life; the development of Egyptian civilization from the rise of the first rulers to its incorporation into the Roman Empire. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 325, NEST 304, or AMNE 371. Equivalency: AMNE 371

subject: ARTH
title: Greek Art and Architecture
description: Visual culture of the ancient Greek world in the second and first millennia BCE, especially from c. 1000 to 30 BCE. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 331, CLST 331, or AMNE 376. Equivalency: AMNE 376

subject: ARTH
title: Roman Art and Architecture
description: Visual culture of the ancient Roman world from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 332, CLST 332, or AMNE 377. Equivalency: AMNE 377

subject: ARTH
title: Visual Culture in the Age of Enlightenment and Revolution (1715-1830)
description: Art, architecture, and social space in Europe and America: redefining gender, identity and nation in the era of industrialization and political change.

subject: ARTH
title: 19th-Century Art and Social Space
description: Ideologies of gender, class, race, ethnicity, and economics in 19th-century European and American visual culture.

subject: ARTH
title: 20th Century Art and Culture: The Triumph and Demise of Modernism
description: A critical survey of western art and cultural production from the turn of the century to the development of Pop Art.

subject: ARTH
title: 20th Century Art and Culture: The Postmodern
description: A critical examination of international visual art and culture from the 1950s to the present; the role of art in consumerist society and the emergence of postmodernism.

subject: ARTH
title: Latin American Art: Modern and Contemporary
description: Analyses of specific works and texts will emphasize visual inventions and meaning in the light of recent theoretical debates

subject: ARTH
title: Inventing Canada Through Art
description: The institutions and art movements that constructed a view to the country now known as Canada, from colonial contact, to Confederation, through the mid-1900s. Emphasis on the significance of locality and situated approaches to understanding the land.

subject: ARTH
title: Contemporary Conversations about Art in Kanata/Canada
description: Radical shifts in thinking about Canadian art and culture since the mid-20th century. The art movements, debates, and institutions that contribute to the complexity of artistic approaches to representing Canada today.

subject: ARTH
title: History of Photography: Archive, Spectacle, Reality
description: History and theory of photography, from the competitive context of invention in the 1830s to contemporary uses in social media.

subject: ARTH
title: Architecture in Europe: Building the Fabric of the Modern State (1715-1837)
description: The role of architecture within the development of the modern state. A survey of broad cultural dynamics, particular building projects and design careers.

subject: ARTH
title: Architecture in Europe: Modern Paradigms of Design (1837-present)
description: An examination of new requirements imposed on architecture by the consolidation of a capitalist economy, industrialization, new technologies and scientific methods.

subject: ARTH
title: Architecture in North America: Colonial Projects and Disruptions (1605-1867)
description: The role of architecture in the imposition of European governance within North America; the modification of received conventions in relation to topographical, ethnic-religious and political factors.

subject: ARTH
title: Architecture in North America: Independent Design Idioms (1867-present)
description: The emergence of a distinctive architecture that superseded British and European agendas; the growth of private and public patronage and the establishment of modern design and practice.

subject: ARTH
title: Grounding the Islamic Image
description: Contextualizing the complex language of images in the Islamic world.

subject: ARTH
title: Art and Urban Culture in the Islamic World
description: A thematic and comparative study of visual arts and architecture in their urban contexts.

subject: ARTH
title: Historic India: Images, Temples and the Construction of Indian Art History
description: North and South Indian art and architecture with an emphasis on Buddhism and Hinduism.

subject: ARTH
title: Nepal and Tibet: Art, Ritual and Performance
description: Art of the Himalayan region situated within social and religious practices, festivals, and performances.

subject: ARTH
title: Mughal India: Art, Architecture and the Spectacle of Empire
description: The complex relationship of Mughal imperial architecture and painting with those of the Hindu Rajput courts.

subject: ARTH
title: Modern and Contemporary India: Art in Colonial and Independent India
description: The development of a new Indian art during the colonial period and nationalist movement; the construction of India's contemporary visual culture.

subject: ARTH
title: Chinese Art and Architecture: Patronage and Collecting
description: The commission, production, preservation, and transmission of Chinese monuments and artworks focusing on the court and questions of cultural policies.

subject: ARTH
title: Chinese Art for the Afterlife
description: Close analyses of Chinese tomb objects and tombs as spatial constructs in their historical, ritual, and social context.

subject: ARTH
title: Chinese Painting: Word and Image
description: Analyses visual narratives and relationships between painting, calligraphy, and poetry in court and literati painting.

subject: ARTH
title: Chinese Modern and Contemporary Art
description: Chinese art and its global entanglements from Qing Encounters to the 21st century.

subject: ARTH
title: Art in Japan: Objects and Spaces
description: Changing relationship between art objects and the built environment in the Japanese archipelago, in its social and historical context.

subject: ARTH
title: Art in Japan: The Problem with Painting
description: Key debates in the history of painting and its institutionalization.

subject: ARTH
title: Art in Japan: Print Media
description: Historical and theoretical questions concerning the development of print media in Japan, from Edo period woodcuts to the advent of digital technologies.

subject: ARTH
title: Art in Japan: Modern Visual Culture
description: Self and community in the art and visual culture of modern Japan.

subject: ARTH
title: Arts of Mexico's Early Peoples
description: Pre-Aztec monumental and portable arts of the Olmec, Zapotec, Teotihuacan and Classic Veracruz peoples.

subject: ARTH
title: Arts of the Aztec period in Mexico.
description: Symbolic meanings and political agendas of Aztec architecture, sculpture and manuscript illustration investigated using Spanish accounts.

subject: ARTH
title: Maya Public Ritual Arts
description: Architecture, sculpture, costume, and visual productions associated with Maya public ritual, including the ancient ball game and modern cofrada dances.

subject: ARTH
title: Maya Arts of Everyday Life
description: Social context and meaning of the Maya's elaborate architecture, sculpture, mural paintings, jewelry, ceramics, figurines, and textiles, ancient and modern, of residences from humble to palatial.

subject: ARTH
title: Arts of the Northwest Coast Peoples: The North
description: The histories, historiography and cultural diversity of the Northern Northwest Coast region; persistence and innovation in the arts in communities, and in cross-cultural and market spheres.

subject: ARTH
title: Arts of the Northwest Coast Peoples: The South
description: The histories, historiography and cultural diversity of the Southern Northwest Coast region; persistence and innovation in the arts in communities, and in cross-cultural and market spheres.

subject: ARTH
title: Art as Technology
description: Relationship between artistic practice and media, examined through a history of paradigm shifts in technology.

subject: ARTH
title: The Artist in the World
description: Critical approach to the figure of the artist in art, film and texts, from the Early Modern period to the present.

subject: ARTH
title: Is Art History Queer?
description: Issues in the history of art through the lens of queer theory.

subject: ARTH
title: Queer Partnerships in Art & Art-Making
description: Diverse forms of human contact and creative collaboration, their effects on art and art-making, and their capacity to challenge conventions of artistic genius as dependent on masculinity, singularity, and heteronormativity. ARTH 382 recommended as preparation.

subject: ARTH
title: Art and Ecologies
description: Reparative possibilities of art and art history as ways of sensing and responding to human impact on planetary life.

subject: ARTH
title: Special Topics in Art History
description: Thematic and issue-based courses in art history. Topics vary year to year.

subject: ARTH
title: Seminar in African Art
description: Key debates in the art of Africa and the African diaspora. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 410 or ARTH_V 410. Equivalency: AFST_V 410. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ARTH
title: Seminar in Visual and Digital Media Theory
description: A thematic examination of key arguments in visual and digital media theory, focusing on developments in lens-based and digital media in relationship to twentieth-century and contemporary artistic practice.

subject: ARTH
title: Art History Internship
description: Prequisite: ARTH_V 300 and departmental approval. Interested students may contact the department for details on how to proceed. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ARTH
title: Honours Essay
description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: COMM
title: Introduction to Business
description: An overview of all functional areas of business. Students will be introduced to the computer and internet tools commonly used in business. For non-Commerce students only. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 100 or COMR_V 100. Equivalency: COMR_V 100
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Business Fundamentals
description: The different disciplines of business and their combination in management planning and decision-making. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Values, Ethics, and Community
description: An introduction to the roles and responsibilities of business at individual, organizational, and societal levels. Students will examine their personal values and lay the foundation for ongoing, active exploration of career paths through which they can achieve their goals. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Business Immersion
description: A broad introduction to the field of business and how the different disciplines within business interact and combine in business decision-making. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM

description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Introduction to Quantitative Decision Making
description: Introduction to decision models in business, including basic optimization, linear programming, probability, decision analysis, random variables, simulation, and solving decision problems using spreadsheet tools. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

Varshney Business Career Centre. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 337 and CPSC_V 103. Prerequisite: COMM_V 205. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

Prerequisite: COMM_V 205 or CPSC_V 213 or CPEN_V 212. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

Applications of queuing models will be included in both services in general and healthcare. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 340 or COMM_V 443. Prerequisite: COMM_V 204. Equivalency: COMM_V 443. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM

faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

Topics include real estate cycles and bubbles, search models and vacancy, the relationship between real estate and the economy, housing demand, and models of housing supply. Prerequisite: COMM_V 204. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
