faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Business Data Communications
description: Basic data communications concepts and technology; local area, wide area, and enterprise networks; the Internet; wireless networking; network development life cycle; network security and management. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 439 or CPSC_V 317, and COMM_V 439 or CPSC_V 417. Prerequisite: COMM_V 335 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Advanced Business Logistics
description: Analysis of logistics systems within firms and across supply chains. The formulation of corporate logistics strategies. Corequisite: COMM_V 204. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Air Transportation
description: An integrative treatment of air transport management including: demand analysis, sales and marketing, globalization trends, aircraft selection and fleet planning; airport economics and management. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Maritime and International Transportation
description: The characteristics of shipping services and the role of shipping services in the design and management of international logistics systems. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Transportation Economics
description: Economic characteristics of passenger and freight transportation services; market structure of the transportation industry; economic impact of public regulation and promotion and the role of economic analysis in resolving problems of Canadian policy. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 446 or ECON_V 480. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301, ECON_V 206. Equivalency: ECON_V 480 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Applied Project Management
description: Project management methodology based on the practices defined by the Project Management Institute, including planning, execution, monitoring, control, and completion. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 301. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Business Logistics and Logistics Services Management
description: General services management including warehousing, transportation, intermodal, order-fulfillment, dispatching, and more. Prerequisite: COMM_V 204. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Financial Accounting - Intermediate II
description: Intermediate II. Continuation of the examination of accounting as a means of measurement and as an information system for external reporting purposes. Prerequisite: COMM_V 353 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Climate-Focused ESG Reporting and Analysis
description: Analysis of organizations' sustainability reports and climate disclosures through key sustainability reporting concepts, frameworks, and standards as they evolve. The course includes practical application of concepts through real-world examples and cases of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) reporting. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Taxes and Decision Making
description: Analysis of business and financial decisions in the presence of taxes. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Financial Accounting-Advanced
description: An examination of advanced financial accounting. Prerequisite: COMM_V 353, COMM_V 450 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Accounting for Management Control and Incentives
description: Design of accounting systems for facilitating and influencing management decisions, with emphasis on performance evaluation in organizations. Prerequisite: COMM_V 294 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Principles of Auditing
description: Principles of internal control, audit evidence, sampling and testing; audit reports; standards; responsibilities of the external auditor. Prerequisite: COMM_V 353. Corequisite: COMM_V 450. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Information Technology Risks, Protection and Audit
description: Business risks associated with the use of information technology. Controls for integrity, security safety, and privacy of hardware, software, data and communications. Methods for auditing information systems and their controls. Prerequisite: COMM_V 335 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Financial Statement Analysis
description: An examination of financial statement information from the perspective of decision makers external to the firm, e.g., investors and financial institutions. Prerequisite: COMM_V 293, COMM_V 298 and COMM_V 370. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Social and Nonprofit Marketing
description: Examines the role, use, and application of marketing in government agencies and nonprofit institutions. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Business Development
description: Principles and practice of personal selling and leadership of teams: strategy, tactics, and implementation. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Integrated Marketing Communication
description: Marketing communication campaign strategy, conceptual framework, and practical application for integrated marketing communications, including advertising. Prerequisite: COMM_V 362 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Public Relations
description: Managing an organization's strategic communications and relationships with diverse publics to handle issues, strengthen reputation, fulfill social responsibilities, and build trust. Topics include stakeholder engagement, issues management, crisis communications, and events and sponsorship. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Digital Marketing
description: Investigation of Internet-based marketing, emphasizing customer-focused perspectives, competitive situations and analysis of the effectiveness of business websites using marketing principles and practices. Prerequisite: COMM_V 296. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: New Venture Design
description: Teams comprising students in COMM_V 466 and APSC_V 486 propose a new product, produce a viable prototype, and develop a business plan for the marketplace. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 466, COMM_V 497, COEC_V 497, COMR_V 497, APSC_V 486, or APSC_V 496E. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Brand Management
description: Issues and challenges commonly faced by brand managers, including: assessing brand meaning, evaluating brand health, assessing a brand's leverage potential, evaluating brand extensions, managing brands through a crisis, and assessing brand value. Prerequisite: COMM_V 296. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Marketing Applications
description: A capstone marketing course where student teams develop comprehensive marketing plans for corporate clients by conducting industry analyses and crafting creative marketing strategies. Prerequisite: All of COMM_V 362, COMM_V 363, COMM_V 365. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: International Marketing
description: An analysis of the scope and significance of contemporary international business operations with particular reference to the marketing management problems encountered by firms with multinational branches and subsidiaries. Prerequisite: COMM_V 296. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Venture Capital
description: Theory and evidence concerning venture capital markets. Contracting, fundraising, and financing choice covered in depth, with the aim of catering to students looking to raise money for entrepreneurial ventures or to invest in entrepreneurial ventures. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 370, COMM_V 387. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Mergers and Acquisitions
description: Mergers and acquisitions as a focal point in making important corporate decisions deduced from careful study of relevant business cases. Prerequisite: COMM_V 370. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Fixed Income Markets and Management
description: Fixed income instruments and derivatives. Risk profiles and their use in establishing fixed income investment portfolios. Performance attribution techniques. Corequisite: COMM_V 374. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Investment Policy
description: The management of security portfolios for individual and institutional investors; relation of investment policy to money markets and business fluctuations. Prerequisite: COMM_V 371. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Advanced Topics in Investment Management
description: Applications of contemporary research, innovations, and technologies in the allocation of capital across asset classes, portfolios of assets, and individual securities. Empirical analyses of current market data using software and quantitative tools to implement potential investment and trading strategies. Prerequisite: All of COMM_V 370, COMM_V 371. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Risk Management and Financial Engineering
description: Principles of financial engineering and risk management. Use of derivatives in risk management. Valuation and hedging models for contingent claims. Prerequisite: COMM_V 374. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Advanced Topics on Corporate Finance
description: Corporate Finance is the process by which corporations raise money, allocate funds to real assets, and manage the flow of funds back to the investors. Topics will vary according to interests of students, instructors, and developments in the field. Corequisite: All of COMM_V 370, COMM_V 371. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative. Education Program in Commerce. Prerequisite: COMM_V 381 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the fall term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce. Prerequisite: COMM_V 480 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: New Product Development
description: How new products are developed and the factors that influence success and failure throughout the various stages of development. Equivalency: COMR_V 482. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Leadership and General Management
description: Integration and application of business knowledge to make business decisions across disciplines; development of personal leadership ability and style. Case-based with guest speakers. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Sustainability Marketing
description: Role of marketing in creating social value. Integration of marketing fundamentals with core social, environmental, and economic principles of sustainability. Analysis of current sustainability trends. Development of strategic and practical marketing recommendations for for-profit enterprises. Potential and pitfalls of sustainability marketing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Social Entrepreneurship
description: An applied course that examines the innovative, growing, and rapidly evolving field of social entrepreneurship, which tackles social and environmental challenges through business perspectives and methods. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 485 or COMR_V 485. Equivalency: COMR_V 485 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Special Topics in Business
description: Equivalency: COMR_V 486. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Environmental Management
description: Explores corporate environmental strategy by introducing economic principles underlying environmental policy, law, and technologies for pollution prevention and abatement, environmental management systems, ISO-14001, energy systems, eco-marketing, and life-cycle analysis. Credit will be granted for only one of COEC_V 475, COMM_V 487, COMM_V 597, or ECON_V 371.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Public Sector Management
description: This course focuses on some of the distinctive aspects of managing in the public sector. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Investing in CDL Start-ups
description: Students work with the Creative Destruction Lab team to support science and technology start-ups through market, customer, and financial analysis. Students learn how investors assess opportunities through due diligence, valuation, and investment memos, gaining direct experience with early-stage investment decisions. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Directed Studies in Commerce
description: An investigation and report on a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and a senior student. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Strategic Management
description: Concepts and processes for the strategic management of private sector, single and multi-business unit enterprises are analysed using the case method. Methodologies which draw on economic and organizational theory are integrated to form the foundations for strategic analyses. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 491 or COEC_V 491. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396. Equivalency: COEC_V 491. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Management Simulation
description: Student teams manage hypothetical firms in a complex simulation, coordinating production, finance, marketing and strategic planning in competition with other teams. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Business and Sustainable Development
description: An overview of environmental issues, focusing on corporate strategy, government policy and interactions between these two sectors of the economy. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: New Enterprise Development
description: The particular problems and experiences encountered in starting, developing and managing new enterprises. The course includes lectures, guest speakers, and case studies. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 497, COMM_V 466, COEC_V 497, COMR_V 497, APSC_V 486, or APSC_V 496E. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396. Equivalency: COEC_V 497, COMR_V 497. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: International Business Management
description: Development of general environmental framework for international business studies by drawing on international and development economics, research into government-business relations and studies in comparative socio-cultural systems and political systems. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 498 or COEC_V 498. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: COMM
title: Internship
description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Commerce and Business Administration

subject: KIN
title: Human Anatomy
description: The basic structure and function of human anatomy. Emphasis is on the neural, muscular, and skeletal systems. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…

subject: KIN
title: Health and Exercise Management
description: Role of physical activity in the maintenance of a healthy life. Application of basic physical fitness and exercise methods, exercise techniques and fitness appraisal.

subject: KIN
title: Neural and Musculoskeletal Physiology
description: Structure and function of the skeletal system, muscular system, integumentary system, neuro-hormonal control, and endocrinology. Emphasis will be to develop an understanding of the integrative nature of the systems discussed. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult…

subject: KIN
title: Visceral Anatomy and Physiology
description: Structure and function of the cardiovascular system, respiratory system, urinary system, digestive system, and immune system. Emphasis will be to develop an understanding of the integrative nature of the systems discussed. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/school… .

subject: KIN
title: Lifespan Motor Development
description: A lifespan approach to motor development that examines underlying factors affecting physical growth, physical activity behaviour, and human motor performance, while highlighting contemporary issues and trends in society. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Sport and Exercise Psychology
description: Psychological theories and research related to sport and exercise behaviour. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/school… . . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Leisure and Sport in Society
description: Introduction to the political, economic and social basis of leisure and sport; concepts, theories and problems. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Research Methods in Kinesiology
description: Critical evaluation of research studies and methods with emphasis on the physical activity context. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: Second-year standing or higher.

subject: KIN
title: Introduction to Statistics in Kinesiology
description: Basic concepts and principles of descriptive and inferential statistics, and distribution-free statistical techniques. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: Second-year standing or higher.

subject: KIN
title: Human Motor Behaviour I
description: Processes underlying human movement and learning motor skills and factors influencing acquisition, performance, and movement control. . Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or HES_O 101 or BIOL_O 131. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Biomechanics I
description: Application of elementary principles of physics and math to a quantitative analysis of movement. Analysis will also focus on the development of forces within muscles and their effect on initiating and controlling human movement. . Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 131. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Exercise Testing and Prescription for Healthy Individuals with Special Considerations
description: Pre-exercise screening, exercise testing, and exercise prescription for improving health and performance for the general population and low-risk populations with special considerations. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 120 and (c) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (d) KIN_V 132 or BIOL_O 133 or HES_O 111.

subject: KIN
title: Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Health
description: Study of nutrition and its application to physical activity and health. Macro- and micronutrient classification and recommended daily intakes, their digestion, functions in the body and their role in supporting physical activity and health will be discussed. . Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (b) KIN_V 132 or BIOL_O 133 or HES_O 111. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Exercise Physiology I
description: Acute and chronic effects of exercise on body systems; basic concepts of cardiovascular, respiratory and muscular responses to physical activity. . Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 120, KIN_V 131, KIN_V 132. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Health Policy and Society
description: Health policy and the social context in relation to active health. . Prerequisite: KIN_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Field Work in Exercise Training for Healthy Aging
description: Opportunity to gain hands-on experience working with qualified exercise professionals to improve cardiovascular and musculoskeletal fitness in healthy middle aged and older adults using evidence-based group exercise programming. Restricted to students in the B.Kin. program with second-year standing or above. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: KIN_V 120. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Human Athletic Performance
description: An exploration of human movement and related issues pertaining to sports and athletic performance. Restricted to non-B.Kin. students only. Not for credit in the B.Kin. Program. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Human Functional Musculoskeletal Anatomy
description: The musculoskeletal structures and neural innervations involved in the control of human movement. Attention will be given to surface anatomy and to the practical application of human anatomy as it pertains to clinical, athletic, or everyday situations. Prerequisite: KIN_V 110 and KIN_V 131.

subject: KIN
title: Sensorimotor Control of Human Movement
description: Processes and mechanisms involved in the sensory, perceptual, and cognitive contributions to human movements. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102.

subject: KIN
title: Neuromuscular Integration of Human Movement
description: The neurophysiological and functional neuroanatomical processes involved in the sensory and motor control of movement, posture and balance in the human. Peripheral and central sensorimotor structures, and neurological diseases that affect human movement and balance control will be discussed. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101.

subject: KIN
title: Biomechanical Properties of Tissues
description: Mechanics of muscular contraction and how the mechanical properties of the muscle, ligaments, tendons, and bone work synergistically. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102.

subject: KIN
title: Programming and Data Science for Kinesiology
description: Think algorithmically to process, visualize, and analyze data related to various research questions. Through a combination of readings, lectures, tutorials, and problem sets, students will learn some of the most important tools and techniques in the Python data science ecosystem. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Restricted to students with third-year standing. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102.

subject: KIN
title: Exercise Prescription and Behaviour Change for Individuals with Chronic Disease and Disability
description: Exercise prescription and behavioural support strategies for promoting health-enhancing levels of fitness for populations with chronic disease and disability. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 120 and (c) KIN_V 205 or HES_O 240 and (d) KIN_V 206 or HES_O 340.

subject: KIN
title: Prevention of Athletic Injuries
description: Training and safety strategies for the prevention of injuries to the musculoskeletal system and sense organs. Credit will be granted for only one of KIN_V 324 or KIN_V 420. Prerequisite: KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120.

subject: KIN
title: Clinical Exercise Physiology
description: Explore the physiological, pathological, and pharmacological factors influencing exercise responses and prescription in clinical populations. Emphasis is on cardiovascular, pulmonary, metabolic, renal, cancer-related, and autoimmune conditions, integrating diagnostic assessment, exercise testing, and safety considerations. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 120, KIN_V 131, KIN_V 132, KIN_V 235.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Applications of Exercise Physiology
description: Explore how the cardiovascular and respiratory systems are regulated and integrated during exercise. Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235.

subject: KIN
title: Creating Effective, Developmentally Appropriate, Physical Activity Learning Environments
description: The pedagogical skills and knowledge required to design, and implement, developmentally appropriate physical activities learning environments in a variety of settings. Prerequisite: One of KIN 140.

subject: KIN
title: Leisure Services for Persons with a Disability
description: Policy issues relating to leisure opportunities for persons with disabilities. Prerequisite: All of KIN 160, KIN 262.

subject: KIN
title: Foundations of Coaching
description: Methods of athletic conditioning, planning the program, psychology of training and coaching, athletic evaluation. Prerequisite: KIN 150.

subject: KIN
title: Physical Activity and Disability
description: Physical activity counselling, education programming principles, exercise considerations, and strategies for promoting inclusive physical activity for people with disabilities. Prerequisite: KIN 150 and Third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Current Topics in Exercise and Health Psychology
description: Exploring concepts, principles, and theories as they relate to the practice of promoting and supporting recommended physical activity for individuals and population groups. Particular attention will be directed at contemporary issues, controversies, evidence informed initiatives, and innovative new approaches. Prerequisite: KIN_V 150 or HES_O 131 and third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Applied Approaches to Childhood Movement
description: An exploration of current and emerging trends, challenges, and opportunities for supporting movement experiences throughout the childhood years. . Prerequisite: KIN_V 140.

subject: KIN
title: Sport, Peace, and Conflict
description: Relationships that sport and leisure have with peace, conflict, and social inequality in Canada and internationally. Prerequisite: KIN 160.

subject: KIN
title: Leisure, Sport and Popular Culture
description: Selected aspects of leisure and sport examined in relation to modern social structures and cultures. Prerequisite: KIN 160.

subject: KIN
title: The Modern Olympics: Power, Politics, and Performance
description: Examination of the Modern Olympic Games as an event with important political, economic, environmental, and cultural ramifications. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Indigenous Sport and Physical Culture in Settler Canada
description: Historical and contemporary issues in Canada that shape Indigenous sport and physical activity, health programs, and policies. Prerequisite: All of KIN 160, KIN 262.

subject: KIN
title: Neuroanatomy of Human Movement
description: Neuroanatomy of human motion in healthy and clinical populations. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102.

subject: KIN
title: Sensori-Motor Control of Human Balance
description: Examining the sensory, motor, and biomechanical factors that contribute to human balance control during quiet standing and postural reactions to internal and external perturbations. Emphasis on understanding the characteristics of healthy balance control and changes associated with age and disease. Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 131, KIN 211, KIN 216, and third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Sensori-motor Neuroplasticity in Movement and Exercise
description: Concepts in neuroplasticity related to sensori-motor control of movement and exercise. The focus will be on plasticity (both adaptive and maladaptive) that arises because of either training or injury/non-use as it relates to movement control and exercise. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Computational Modelling of Human Sensori-Motor Control and Learning
description: Learn the fundamentals of modeling human behavior, including Bayesian probability theory, learning algorithms, and simulation. Gain proficiency with simulating Bayesian and non-Bayesian models with Python code to use these approaches to address novel research questions. Prerequisite: KIN_V 206 or HES_O 340 and KIN_V 318, or another introductory Python programming course (e.g., CPSC_V 110, Python version of DSCI_V 100).

subject: KIN
title: Laboratory Investigations in Neuromechanical Kinesiology
description: Integration and application of laboratory principles and techniques for experimental investigations of topics in neuromechanical kinesiology, including biomechanics, motor behaviour, and neurophysiology. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 131, KIN_V 211, KIN_V 216.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Exercise Prescription in Chronic Conditions: Evidence-Informed Practice
description: Chronic conditions and their presentation, comorbidities, medications, pathophysiological basis, and their effects on exercise response and capacity will be discussed. The aim is to build competence in evidence-informed decision-making when assessing and prescribing exercise for clients with complex chronic conditions. Prerequisite: KIN_V 320.

subject: KIN
title: Professional Practice in Kinesiology
description: Exploration of professional practice in Kinesiology, encompassing key concepts such as scope of practice, clinical communication skills, professional ethics, shared decision-making, team-based care, entrepreneurship, and evidence-informed practice. Interprofessional collaborative approach to client care, fostering skills crucial for effective on-the-job decision-making. Prerequisites: All of (a) KIN_V 120 and (b) KIN_V 205 or HES_O 240 and (c) KIN_V 206 or HES_O 340.

subject: KIN
title: Clinical Exercise Assessment
description: Conduct cardiovascular fitness, musculoskeletal, functional, and risk stratification testing, with specific consideration for populations living with chronic disease and disability. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the B.Kin. program with fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Medical Aspects of Sport and Exercise
description: Training and safety strategies for the management and prevention of disorders of internal organs and central nervous system. Topics include environmental and nutritional factors in conditioning and pre-event preparation. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101.

subject: KIN
title: Indigenous Health and Wellness
description: The complex social, cultural, historical, and economic factors that shape health and wellness within Indigenous communities will be explored through extensive blended learning and experiential learning opportunities. Credit will only be granted for one of KIN_V 428 and KIN_V 468. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 160 and KIN_V 235.

subject: KIN
title: Sport Nutrition
description: Sport nutrition guidelines, physiological mechanisms of fuel use in the body, nutritional strategies to support weight change, hydration, and ergogenic aids the needs of special athlete populations. Prerequisite: All of (a) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (b) KIN_V 132 or BIOL_O 133 or HES_O 111 and (c) KIN_V 232 or HES_O 200.

subject: KIN
title: Exercise, Nutrition, and Metabolism
description: Exploring the physiological and biochemical changes that occur in skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and liver following exercise. Interactions between exercise, nutrition, and commonly prescribed medications used for the treatment of diabetes and cardiovascular disease will also be examined. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 232, KIN_V 235, and third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Pulmonary Physiology of Exercise
description: Operation of the lungs, chest wall, and ventilatory control mechanisms during dynamic whole-body exercise. Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235, KIN 335.

subject: KIN
title: Skeletal Muscle Physiology: Molecular Adaptions to Training, Disuse and Aging
description: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of muscle adaptability to aerobic and resistance training, inactive and aging: signaling cascades controlling hypertrophy and atrophy, satellite cell contribution to muscle repair, and mitochondrial/ribosomal biogenesis. BIOL 112 or similar recommended. Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235, KIN 335.

subject: KIN
title: Planning Physical Education, Sport and Exercise Programs
description: Processes, techniques and considerations in the planning, implementation and evaluation of physical education, sport and exercise programs in both public and private agencies. Prerequisite: All of KIN 140, KIN 262 and Third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Exploring Alternative Methods for Teaching Games and Sports
description: Examination of innovative, developmentally appropriate, conceptual and tactical approaches to team game instruction. Prerequisite: One of KIN 140.

subject: KIN
title: Inclusive Approaches to Sport Psychology
description: Examination of the psychological and behavioural processes of athletes from a social justice perspective. The focus will be on the role of social structures, sociocultural norms, power relations, and social identities in shaping athletes' perceptions and lived experiences in sport. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 150, KINIV 160, and third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Understanding and Changing Physical Activity Behaviour
description: Examining the influence of psychological factors across different settings and populations, with a particular focus on interventions aimed at enhancing mental health. Understanding psychology can be used to design effective interventions at the individual and community level. Prerequisite: KIN_V 150 or HES_O 131.

subject: KIN
title: The Psychology of Team Effectiveness
description: Within sport and other contexts that demand high performance, humans often work together as part of teams. Discover what makes those teams effective, why some teams flourish and others flounder, and how we might develop better teams. Prerequisites: KIN_V 150 and KIN_V 205.

subject: KIN
title: Psychobiology of Physical Activity
description: Exploration of the role of physical activity and exercise on brain health, mental health, and underpinning psychological and biological mechanisms. This course deepens students' capacity to read and interpret scientific evidence. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 150, KIN_V 205, KIN_V 206.

subject: KIN
title: Aging, Health, and Society
description: Examination of current issues in the sociology of aging and health. Prerequisite: All of KIN 160, KIN 262.

subject: KIN
title: Hockey in Canadian Society
description: Examines Canadian society through the lens of hockey. Explores the deep and symbiotic relationship between the nation and the game and the implications this relationship has for social, political, and cultural life in Canada. Prerequisite: KIN_V 160.

subject: KIN
title: Health Promotion and Physical Activity
description: Current perspectives on health promotion and health education; design and implementation of health promotion strategies in a variety of arenas, particularly health promotion/education strategies aimed at encouraging physical activity. Prerequisite: All of KIN 150, KIN 160, KIN 205, KIN 262.

subject: KIN
title: Interculturalism, Health and Physical Activity
description: Examination of multiculturalism and interculturalism in the delivery of community-based physical activities for diverse populations; connections between physical activity and health in different cultural contexts. Community service learning and participation in culturally unfamiliar physical activities are core elements. Prerequisite: All of KIN 160, KIN 262.

subject: KIN
title: Restoring Wellness Through Indigenous Land-Based Practices
description: Examining how colonialism and settler colonialism altered Indigenous physical practices and concepts of wellness and consider how Indigenous peoples and their communities are reclaiming and reengaging with physical culture and land-based practices to restore and maintain their sense of well-being. Prerequisite: All of KIN_V 160, KIN_V 262, and third-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Exercise Management of Chronic Neurological Balance and Mobility Conditions
description: Work with an inter-professional health team to assess and rehabilitate neurological balance and mobility deficits. Students will assist in the delivery of exercise-based rehabilitation at the Physical Therapy Rehabilitation Clinic and the BC Brain Well Program. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail. Corequisite: KIN_V 320 and KIN_V 411. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Kinesiology Field Work in Primary Care Medicine
description: Work in a team-based primary care setting with patients focusing on exercise prescription and program delivery under the clinical care of family physicians, dietician, practice support coaches and kinesiologists. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail. Prerequisites: KIN_V 320 and KIN_V 335. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Physical Activity Counselling and Prescription for People with Spinal Cord Injury
description: Gain hands-on experience working with members of the Physical Activity Research Centre at the Blusson Spinal Cord Centre. Apply skills in exercise testing, prescription, and physical activity counselling. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: KIN_V 320 (KIN_V 351 strongly recommended). This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Scientific Communication and Research Skills in Neuromechanical Kinesiology
description: Training in research methods, computational skills, and scientific dissemination related to neuromechanics research in Kinesiology. Students will learn the principles underlying scientific communication and apply these principles in the form of an oral dissemination of scientific results. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail. Prerequisites: Two of KIN_V 310, KIN_V 311, KIN_V 313, KIN_V 316, KIN_V 411, KIN_V 413, KIN_V 415, KIN_V 419. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Neuromechanics
description: Topics consider how neurological, cognitive, sensory, mechanical and muscular systems interact to control human motion and its response to the physical environment. Prerequisite: Two of KIN_V 311, KIN_V 313, KIN_V 316, KIN_V 411, 413, 415, KIN_V 419. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Systems Biology, Exercise and Health
description: Topics examine the roles of physical activity and fitness on physiological systems and underlying cellular and metabolic mechanisms. Prerequisite: Two of KIN_V 320, KIN_V 335, KIN_V 420, KIN_V 424, KIN_V 432, KIN_V 434, KIN_V 435, KIN_V 438. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Indigenous Sport, Physical Activity and Health
description: Topics explore the relationship between Indigenous physical cultures, physical activity, health and wellbeing. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Leadership Education for Physical Activity
description: Topics consider health-related fitness, physical competence, cognitive understanding, and positive attitudes about physical activity. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Psychology of Movement
description: Topics examines the application of psychology to understanding and supporting healthy sport, physical activity, and health behaviors. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Sociocultural Studies
description: Topics explore the social, cultural and global context of sport, exercise, physical activity, health, and the body. Prerequisite: Two of KIN_V 360, KIN_V 363, KIN_V 368, KIN_V 460, KIN_V 464, KIN_V 465, KIN_V 468. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Seminar in Interdisciplinary Research in Kinesiology
description: Topics will be approached from multiple perspectives in a course designed to explore the interdisciplinarity of the field of kinesiology. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing.

subject: KIN
title: Directed Studies in Kinesiology
description: Opportunity for students to conduct an independent study in a subject area of interest to them, under the direction of a KIN faculty member. Prerequisite: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program.

subject: KIN
title: Undergraduate Research Experience in Kinesiology
description: Opportunity for independent study that includes original data collection, under the direction of a KIN faculty member. Prerequisite: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program.

subject: APBI
title: Soil and the Global Environment
description: Soil as the base of the Earth's ecosystem pyramid. The interconnection between soil, climate change and human activity, the carbon cycle, water resources, food security, food safety, and biofuel production. Strategies for sustaining soil resources.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introduction to Soil Science
description: Physical, chemical and biological properties of soils; soil formation, classification, use and conservation. There are no prerequisites for this course, but background in Biology 12, Chemistry 12, and Physics 12 (or first-year university-level) is strongly advised.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Vascular Plants
description: A comparative study of pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, integrating form, function, and ecology. Prerequisite: One of (a) all of BIOL_V 121, BIOL_V 180 or (b) all of SCIE_V 001, BIOL_V 180 or (c) all of BIOL_V 121, BIOL_V 140 or (d) all of SCIE_V 001, BIOL_V 140, or (e) 7 credits of first-year biology. Equivalency: BIOL_V 210
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Animal Sheltering and Companion Animal Support Services
description: History, philosophy, and current practices of animal shelters and companion animal support services, with a focus on emerging issues from a One Health/One Welfare perspective. Prerequisite: Second-year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introduction to Horticulture
description: The cultivation of key temperate fruits, vegetables, greenhouse, ornamental and nursery crops in BC, integrated with scientific and practical aspects of their sustainable production and marketing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Biotechnology in Agricultural Food Production
description: Genetics, genomics, and biotechnology concepts with applications to agricultural food production and food safety. Prerequisite: All of BIOL 112, BIOL 121, BIOL 180.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Atmospheric Environments
description: Physical principles underlying weather and climates. Thermal, moisture and wind climates from the scale of plants and animals to the globe. Daily weather systems and climate change. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOS (or GEOB) 200, GEOS (or GEOB) 204 or APBI 244. Equivalency: GEOS (OR GEOB) 200
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Agroecology I: Introduction to principles and techniques
description: Basic ecological approaches for understanding and managing agricultural production and food systems. Includes hands-on field data collection, data analysis and problem-based discussions.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
description: Principles and practices necessary to understand practical concerns of sustainable food systems. Students who already present credit for APBI_V 260 are not permitted to receive credit for APBI_V 265.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introductory Topics in Applied Biology
description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in applied biology. Topics will vary from year to year.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Soil, People and Landscape
description: How environmental factors and landpeople relationships control the distribution of soil types in the landscape and the changes of soil properties in space and time. Prerequisite: APBI_V 200.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Comparative Cardiovascular, Respiratory and Osmoregulatory Physiology
description: Cardiovascular, respiratory and osmoregulatory physiology of vertebrates. Prerequisite: BIOL 204 and one of BIOL 260, BIOL 361. And 3rd year standing. Equivalency: BIOL364
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Reproductive Physiology
description: Function and processes involved in reproductive physiology in domesticated animals. This course will focus on physiological mechanisms related to puberty, reproductive cycle, fertilization, embryo development, pregnancy, and parturition. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 204, BIOL_V 260. 3rd year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Experimental Analysis of Animal Behaviour
description: Case studies will be used to discover how behavioural principles explain complexity in the behaviour of individual animals and contribute to our understanding of animal welfare. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. One of PSYC_V 100, PSYC_V 101 or PSYC_V 102 recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Animals and Society
description: Contemporary use of animals for food production, companionship, recreation and science; social and ethical issues concerning human impacts on animals; animals in human culture; protection of animals by society and the law. Prerequisite: At least third-year standing in any faculty.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Animal Welfare and the Ethics of Animal Use
description: Scientific assessment of animal well-being, ethical concepts applied to animal use, and animal welfare issues arising in agriculture, biomedical research and other areas. Credit will be granted for only one of APBI_V 315, ANSC_V 515, or AANB_V 515. Prerequisite: At least third-year standing in any faculty.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Equine Biology, Health and Welfare
description: Anatomy, physiology, reproduction, nutrition of the horse; common disease pathology, prevention and treatments; equine behaviour.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Welfare and Ethics of using Animals in Science
description: Historical and current debate, ethical perspectives, governance, and scientific understanding of experiences of animals in research.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introduction to Plant Breeding
description: Small-scale classical (i.e., non-biotechnological) plant breeding and seed saving. Practical approaches to crop improvement, designing and implementing a simple plant breeding program.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Aquaculture and the Environment
description: Interactions between aquaculture and the environment. Current issues, comparison of systems, species, production methods, environments, and socioeconomics. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 230, APBI 260, APBI 265, CONS 330, ENVR 200, ENVR 300. and third year standing. Or permission of the instructor.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Horticultural Techniques
description: Horticulture theory and methodology in an experiential learning format. Plant identification, seeding, propagation, canopy management, cultivation media, horticultural systems examined in the context of integrated crop management.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introduction to Seed Plant Taxonomy
description: Introduction to seed plant taxonomy emphasizing descriptive morphology and identification. Each student will be required to submit a plant collection. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121. Equivalency: BIOL_V 324.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introductory Plant Pathology
description: Study of the ecology of plant pathogenic organisms; principles of disease development and control.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Introduction to Entomology
description: A survey of the structure, classification and biology of insects; ecology and life-histories of insects; insect-plant relations. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121. Equivalency: BIOL_V 327.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Invasive Species Ecology and Management
description: Advanced understanding of invasion ecology and the complexities of invasive species management globally in the context of a changing climate. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 or ILS_V 108. Equivalency: BIOL_V 317, CONS_V 328.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Soil Biology
description: The diversity of soil organisms (bacteria, protozoa, fungi, animals, plants) in natural and managed ecosystems; roles in primary production, nutrient cycling, decomposition and reclamation; interactions between soil organisms; responses to environmental change. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121. Equivalency: FRST_V 310.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Plant Physiology
description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121 and either(a) CHEM_V 123 or (b) all of CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 113. CHEM_V 233 is recommended. Equivalency: BIOL_V 351, FRST_V 311.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Agroecology II: Ecology of Agricultural Systems
description: A variety of ecological processes shape agricultural landscapes. Students will learn the research foundations of applied ecology in agriculture and how to read and critique the scientific literature in this field. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 230, APBI 260, APBI 265.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Key Indicators of Agroecosystem Sustainability
description: A detailed exploration of biophysical, economic, and social ecosystem sustainability indicators for primary production subsystems.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Summer Practicum in Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
description: Based at the UBC Farm. Application required. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Prerequisite: One of APBI 260, APBI 265. and third-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Research Methods in Applied Biology
description: Research methods including research design, scientific critique, writing proposals and reports, and oral presentation. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Applied Biology program or permission of the instructor.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Soil Processes
description: Understanding environmental factors influencing soil-forming processes and their ecological implications. Credit will be granted for only one of SOIL 501 or APBI 401. Prerequisite: APBI 200.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Sustainable Soil Management
description: Application of fundamental, unifying, soil science principles in sustainable ecosystem management. Credit will be granted for only one of SOIL_V 502 or APBI_V 402. Prerequisite: APBI_V 200.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Soil Sampling, Analyses and Data Interpretation
description: Field and laboratory analytical techniques in the chemical, biological and physical assessment of soils. Credit will be granted for only one of SOIL_V 503 or APBI_V 403. Prerequisite: APBI_V 200.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Plant-Water Relations for Sustainable Agriculture
description: Plant water requirements for production and survival, physiological stress thresholds, soil-plant-atmosphere interactions, structure-function relationships, cutting-edge and traditional monitoring tools, precision agriculture, application for sustainable water management. Prerequisite: Third year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Pollination Biology
description: Fundamental research and topics in pollination biology related to various themes in applied biology including: natural selection, insect cognition, conservation and agriculture. Credit will be granted for only one of PLNT 506 or APBI 406. Prerequisite: One of APBI 260, APBI 265, BIOL 230.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Applied Animal Health and Physiology
description: Physiological processes related to common health disorders in production and domesticated animals. The course will incorporate anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pathology. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202 or BIOC_V 203.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Reproductive Physiology and Technology
description: A comparative overview of reproductive physiology and reproductive technologies in domesticated and laboratory animals. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 201. Third year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Belowground Ecosystems
description: Concepts, methods, and applications of belowground ecology with emphasis on biotic interactions in soil; roles that aboveground and belowground communities play in regulating the structure and function of terrestrial ecosystems and their responses to global change. Credit will be granted for only one of APBI_V 412 or FRST_V 512 or CONS_V 412. Prerequisite: Fourth year standing in a Bachelor of Science Program. Permission is required for registration. Equivalency: CONS_V 412.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Stress and Coping in Animals
description: Understanding, assessing, and managing stress in farm, companion, captive wildlife, and research animals: sources of stress; behavioural, emotional, cognitive, and physiological responses; effects on growth, reproduction, health. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. APBI 315 and courses in animal physiology and animal behavior recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Animals and Global Issues
description: Research seminar integrating diverse information to address global animal issues including: animal-source foods and human health, environmental impact of livestock production, trade in exotic animals. Prerequisite: One of APBI_V 314, APBI_V 315.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Applied Animal Behaviour
description: Application of principles and research methods of animal behaviour to practical problems in the care of farm, companion, wild and research animals, and in animal training, and human-wildlife conflict.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Compassionate Conservation
description: Evaluation of humane treatment of individual animals living in the wild and managed within conservation biology. Assessment of attitudes and viewpoints of the role of animal welfare in conservation biology. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. APBI 315 and BIOL 416 or CONS 330 recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Production and Postharvest Physiology of Vegetable Crops
description: Morphology, growth and development, production, composition, quality, and postharvest physiology of vegetable crops.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Intensive Fish Production
description: Management of fin fish throughout the life cycle; broodstock, egg, larvae, and juvenile. Control of environmental factors, including pathogens, for maximum productivity at all life stages. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. One of APBI_V 311, BIOL_V 204 or BIOL_V 260. APBI_V 312 recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Fish Health
description: Management of fish health in aquaculture; common fish pathogens, epidemiology, prevention, and treatment of diseases. Prerequisite: Third year standing or higher. One of APBI 311, BIOL 204 or BIOL 260. APBI 312 and APBI 418 strongly recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Fish and Climate Change
description: Effects of climate change on fish physiology, fisheries and aquaculture on regional and global scales. Third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Indigenous Food Systems in Canada
description: Indigenous food systems are a complex, relational web of connections between land, culture, and spirit. Topics include: major elements of Indigenous food systems and present-day food stories from Indigenous communities across the country. Prerequisite: LFS_V 350. Or third-year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Ecological Restoration
description: Perspectives and practices of ecological restoration in diverse ecosystems worldwide. Prerequisite: APBI 200 and one of FRST 201, APBI 260, BIOL 230. Equivalency: UFOR 403
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Plant-Microbe Interactions
description: Biology and physiology of selected plant-microbe relationships. Impacts of plant-microbe relationships on society. Prerequisite: BIOL 200 and one of BIOC 202, BIOC 203, BIOL 201, BIOL 233, BIOL 234, BIOL 260. Equivalency: BIOL421
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Insect Ecology
description: Behavioural, population, and community ecology of insects. Interaction between insects and plants and the application of the principals of insect ecology to biological control of insects and weeds. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 205, BIOL_V 327, APBI_V 327. Equivalency: BIOL_V 411.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Integrated Pest Management
description: Development and implementation of multi-disciplinary pest management programs in agricultural crops. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Plant Genomics
description: Concepts, principles, and recent discoveries in genome structure and comparative genomics in plants with a focus on economically important plants; applications of genomics approaches to questions in plant genetics, evolution, and ecology. Corequisite: BIOL_V 335. Equivalency: BIOL_V 440.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Wine Grape and Berry Biology
description: Grapevine genetics, morphology, and physiology and major biological features of other important berry crops for British Columbia such as blueberry, cranberry, and raspberry. Credit will be granted for only one of APBI_V 442, APBI_V 443, or PLNT_V 542. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 112 and BIOL_V 121.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Field Study of Wine Grape Production
description: Lectures, field trips, laboratory sessions focused on major issues related to grape and wine production. Origin of grape varieties and rootstocks, morphological features of the grapevine, training systems, canopy management strategies, berry composition, the impact of terroir on wine quality. Credit will be granted for only one of PLNT 542, APBI 442 OR APBI 443. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 112 and BIOL 121.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Agroforestry
description: Ecological, economic and social benefits of incorporating trees into agricultural landscapes. Lectures and groupwork designing agroforestry systems in temperate and tropical contexts. Prerequisite: One of FRST_V 201, APBI_V 260. Equivalency: FRST_V 444
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Agroecology III: Synthesis and Application
description: Application of agroecological knowledge towards the creation of real-world solutions for real-world problems. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Applied Agroecology
description: Analysis and solution of problems in agricultural production systems through the integration and application of agroecological knowledge and principles.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Conservation Agriculture and Biodiversity Monitoring
description: Biodiversity indicators and basic monitoring methods. Sources of agroecosystem biodiversity, including plants, insects, soil invertebrates, and vertebrates. Proficiency in using techniques to measure key abiotic factors in the field. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 300, GEOG 374, FRST 231, LFS 252. APBI 260 recommended
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Insects in Agroecosystems
description: Insect ecology and evolutionary biology of pests, predators, pollinators and other insect groups in agroecosystems. Application to biodiversity management and sustainable agricultural practices. Prerequisite: One of APBI 327, BIOL 327 and one of BIOL 300, GEOG 374, FRST 231, LFS 252, STAT 200.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Capstone in Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
description: Integrates classroom and applied learning at the UBC Farm with design project. Prerequisite: APBI_V 365.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Indigenous Ecologies
description: Application of Indigenous worldviews and knowledges to ecology. Colonial history of modern ecology, foundations and examples of Indigenous ecologies, restoration applying multiple worldviews, and Indigenized, culturally appropriate ecological research and decision-making processes. Credit will only be granted for only one of APBI 475, FRST 475, PLNT 575 or FRST 575. Prerequisite: One of BEST 203, BIOL 230, FRST 201, APBI 260, GEOS 207. Third-year standing. Equivalency: FRST 475
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Advanced Topics in Applied Biology
description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in applied biology. Prerequisite: 3rd year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Human Wildlife Conflict
description: Evaluation of the impacts of human wildlife conflicts on wildlife populations; application of innovative methods to reduce human wildlife conflicts. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. BIOL 230 or FRST 395 and APBI 315 or APBI 416 recommended. Equivalency: CONS495
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Applied Animal Biology Practicum
description: Application of principles and concepts of Applied Animal Biology to experiential learning in the fields of wild, companion, lab, and farm animal welfare and management. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. APBI_V 314 and/or APBI_V 315 are recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Directed Studies
description: Prerequisite: Approval of program advisor.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Undergraduate Essay
description: Preparation of a comprehensive and analytical review of an approved topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Consultation with a program advisor is required.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APBI
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Design and execution of an experimental/analytical research project leading to the preparation of a thesis. Prerequisite: Approval of a program advisor; consult before the end of classes in third year.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: APSC
title: Introduction to Engineering I
description: An introduction to the engineering profession including: roles and responsibilities of the engineer, the engineering disciplines, sustainability, an introduction to the engineering design process, introduction and application of the relevant foundational scientific principles, prototyping, engineering graphics, technical communication, and engineering ethics. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Introduction to Engineering II
description: An introduction to the engineering profession including: the engineering design process, sustainability, prototype testing, introduction and application of the relevant foundational scientific principles, team functioning, engineering graphics, and technical communication. . Prerequisite: APSC_V 100. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Integrated Experiential STEM Seminar 1
description: Term 1 seminar for Indigenous STEM Bridging Program students. Introduces STEM disciplines and academic skills: foundational scientific principles, lab science, coding, communication, study strategies, and experiential learning, with emphasis on Indigenous knowledge and approaches to science. Course available to students enrolled in the Indigenous STEM Bridging Program only. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Integrated Experiential STEM Seminar 2
description: Term 2 seminar for Indigenous STEM Bridging Program students. Introduces STEM disciplines and academic skills: foundational scientific principles, lab science, coding, communication, study strategies, and experiential learning, with emphasis on Indigenous knowledge and approaches to science. Course available to students enrolled in the Indigenous STEM Bridging Program only. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Introduction to Applied Science Co-op
description: An introduction to Applied Science Co-op including: completion of pre-employment workshops, career skills toolkits, networking opportunities, interview training, individual coaching sessions, and job search skills. Restricted to students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Applied Science Cooperative Education Program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Co-operative Education Work Term I
description: Supervised, technical work integrated learning experience in a public or private organization for a minimum of three months. Formal co-op assignments required. Restricted to undergraduate students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Applied Science and the Co-operative Education Program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Introduction to Engineering
description: Non-credit course designed to introduce students to Engineering. Information on the Faculty, the profession and the particular skills and type of work done by practising engineers in different disciplines. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Engineering Case Studies
description: Application of scientific principles and technical knowledge to practical problems. Introduction to the engineering design process and to engineering graphics. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Computer-Aided Engineering Graphics
description: Orthographic projection, technical sketching, development of the ability to visualize in three dimensions. Standards and conventions of engineering drawing, graphical presentation of engineering data. Micro-computer based graphics aids. Engineering geometry and the solution of space problems. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Introduction to Computation in Engineering Design
description: Analysis and simulation, laboratory data acquisition and processing, measurement interfaces, engineering tools, computer systems organization, programming languages. Credit will only be given for one of: APSC_V 160, CPSC_V 301, or EOSC_V 211. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Engineering Analysis I
description: Functions, limits, differentiation, applications of derivatives, integration, applications of definite integrals. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Engineering Analysis II
description: Integrals and transcendental functions, techniques of integration, applications of integration, polar coordinates, infinite sequences and series, vectors and the geometry of space, and partial derivatives. . Prerequisite: APSC_V 172. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Engineering Communication
description: Purpose, audience, content, format, and tone are studied, as are team-based report writings and presentations. Community Service Learning projects are integrated into existing assignments. An LPI level 5 is required for registration in this course. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Electricity, Magnetism, and Waves
description: Coulomb's law, electric field, Gauss' law, electric potential, conductors, capacitance, electric currents, resistance, DC circuits, magnetic fields and forces, sources of magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, mechanical waves, electromagnetic waves, light propagation, geometrical optics. . Prerequisite: APSC_V 172. Corequisite: APSC_V 173. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Linear Algebra for Engineers
description: Systems of linear equations, Gaussian elimination, engineering application of linear algebra, matrix operations, special matrices, determinants, vector space, orthogonality, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, linear transformation.

subject: APSC
title: Statics
description: Force vectors, Cartesian coordinate system, free body diagram, dot and cross products, forces equilibrium of particles, force and moment equilibrium of rigid bodies, analysis of trusses, frames and machines, friction, wedges, pulleys, and belts. Applications of linear algebra in statics. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Matter and Energy I
description: Thermometry, states of matter and phase change, ideal and real gases, 1st law of thermodynamics, 2nd law of thermodynamics, liquids, solutions. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Matter and Energy II
description: Atomic structures and bonding, solid crystals, chemical equilibrium, reactions in gas phase and in aqueous solutions, acid-base and redox reactions, kinetics of chemical reactions, thermochemistry, electrochemistry. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Technical Communication
description: Written and oral communication in engineering. Report preparation, business correspondence, and oral presentation of technical material. Credit will be granted for only one of BMEG_V 201, CHBE_V 201, CIVL_V 203, CPEN_V 281, ELEC_V 281, IGEN_V 201, MANU_V 201, MECH_V 226, MTRL_V 201, or APSC_V 201. . Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 112, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Technical Communication Engineering Physics
description: Written and oral communication in business correspondence, engineering design methods, report preparation, and oral presentations of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of the Engineering Physics Program. Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150, ENPH_V 259. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Technical Communication Engineering Physics II
description: Continuation of written and oral communication in business correspondence, engineering design methods, report preparation and oral presentations of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of the Engineering Physics Program. . Prerequisite: APSC_V 202. Corequisite: ENPH_V 253. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Co-operative Education Work Term
description: Supervised, technical work integrated learning experience in a public or private organization for a minimum of three months. Formal co-op assignments required. Restricted to students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Applied Science and the Co-operative Education Program. Prerequisite: APSC_V 110. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
title: Co-operative Education Work Term
description: Supervised, technical work integrated learning experience in a public or private organization for a minimum of three months. Formal co-op assignments required. Restricted to students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Applied Science and the Co-operative Education Program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: APSC
