subject: CHIN
title: Early Classical Chinese Poetry (to Han)
description: Readings in classical poetry from the pre-Qin to the end of the Han Dynasties, at an advanced level. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 461 or CHIN_V 464. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Early Classical Chinese Poetry (Han to Tang)
description: Readings in classical poetry from the Six Dynasties to early Tang, at an advanced level. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN 441/ 443/ 444/ 445/ 447/ 448/ 435/ 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN 463 or CHIN 464. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN 313, CHIN 314, CHIN 317, CHIN 318, CHIN 323, CHIN 437, CHIN 443, CHIN 444, CHIN 447, CHIN 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Early Classical Chinese Poetry (Intensive)
description: A combination of CHIN 461 and 463. Classical poetry from pre-Qin to the early Tang Dynasties, at an advanced level. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 464 or both CHIN_V 461, CHIN_V 463. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Fantasy in Chinese Literature
description: Themes in Chinese literature from pre-Qin to the present, with a focus on narratives about the supernatural, the marvelous, and the fantastic. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448, or placement approval. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Chinese Martial Arts Fiction
description: Chinese martial arts fiction as a form of cultural expression first created in classical Chinese fiction and then evolved into contemporary popular literature. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448, or placement approval. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Artistic Images in Chinese Literature from the Bronze Age to the Tang
description: Visual and material forms of Chinese culture, as represented in literary texts, from 1046 BCE to 978 CE. Emphasis on the interplay between images and words in the formation of ideas and cultures. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN 467 or CHIN 469. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN 437, CHIN 443, CHIN 444, CHIN 447, CHIN 448, or placement approval.

subject: CHIN
title: Artistic Images in Chinese Literature from the Song to the Present
description: Visual and material forms of Chinese culture, as represented in literary texts, from 1082 to 2020. Emphasis on the interplay between images and words in the formation of ideas and cultures. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN 468 or CHIN 469. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN 437, CHIN 443, CHIN 444, CHIN 447, CHIN 448, or placement approval.

subject: CHIN
title: Artistic Images in Chinese Literature from the Bronze Age to the Present
description: Combination of CHIN_V 467 and 468. Visual and material forms of Chinese culture, as represented in literary texts, from 1046 BCE to 2020 CE. Emphasis on the interplay between images and words in the formation of ideas and cultures. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 469 or both CHIN_V 467, CHIN_V 468. Recommended: one of CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448, or placement approval. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Reading and Writing Classical Chinese Poetry
description: Theory and skills of writing major forms of Classical Chinese poetry, including regulated verse and song lyrics. Emphasis on application of poetry and rules to the writing of metrical poems and critique of classical Chinese poetry. Recommended pre-requisites: placement exam certificate and permission of the instructor.

subject: CHIN
title: Later Classical Chinese Poetry (Tang)
description: Readings in classical poetry from the time of Du Fu (712-770) to the end of the Tang Dynasty, at an advanced level. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 471 or 474. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Later Classical Chinese Poetry (after Tang)
description: Readings in classical poetry from the Song to the Qing dynasties, at an advanced level. Not to be taken concurrently with any CHIN courses lower than 400-level. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 473 or 474. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Later Classical Chinese Poetry (Intensive)
description: A combination of CHIN 471 and 473. Classical poetry from the time of Du Fu (712-770) to the end of the Qing Dynasty, at an advanced level. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 474 or both CHIN_V 471, CHIN_V 473. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Tutorial in Chinese for Honours Students
description: Will require the presentation of at least one research paper. Review the course section information or consult the Department for details. May be taken for up to a total of 12 credits. Restricted to students in the Honours Asian Area Studies or Asian Language and Culture programs. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Modern Chinese Literature I (Heritage)
description: Selected readings from the May Fourth Era to present. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 481 or CHIN_V 484. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Supervised Study in the Chinese Language
description: Focus changes from year to year. Please see Department website (asia.ubc.ca) for further details. Open to undergraduate and graduate students. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Modern Chinese Literature II (Heritage)
description: Historical continuation of CHIN_V 481. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN_V 400-level language courses: CHIN 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 483 or CHIN_V 484. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Intensive Modern Chinese Literature (Heritage)
description: A combination of CHIN 481 and 483. Selected readings from the May Fourth Era to the present. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN_V 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 484 or both CHIN_V 481, CHIN_V 483. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Contemporary Chinese Fiction in Film
description: Contemporary Chinese films from the 21st century adapted from literary works. Recommended pre-requisites: One of CHIN 437, CHIN 443, CHIN 444, CHIN 447, CHIN 448, or placement approval.

subject: CHIN
title: Staging Drama in Modern China
description: Development, performance, intercultural interactions, and multi-media adaptations of modern Chinese drama. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN 437, CHIN 443, CHIN 444, CHIN 447, CHIN 448, or placement approval.

subject: CHIN
title: Reading Modern Sinophone Literature
description: Sinophone literature produced beyond mainland China after 1949 as a dynamic part of understanding cultural Chineseness in its local, communal and global context. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN 437, CHIN 443, CHIN 444, CHIN 447, CHIN 448, or placement approval.

subject: CHIN
title: Classical Chinese I (Heritage)
description: The development of early Chinese from the classical period through the Six Dynasties (5th century BCE to 6th century CE). Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN_V 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 491 or CHIN_V 431 or CHIN_V 494. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Classical Chinese II (Heritage)
description: Focus in on the Tang and Song dynasties (617 - 1279). Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN_V 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 493 or CHIN_V 433 or CHIN_V 494. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Intensive Classical Chinese (Heritage)
description: A combination of CHIN_V 491 and 493. Readings on classical philosophy, history, literature, and culture. Not to be taken concurrently with any of the following CHIN 400-level language courses: CHIN_V 441, 443, 444, 445, 447, 448, 435, 437. Credit will be granted for only one of CHIN_V 494 or CHIN_V 434 or both CHIN_V 431, CHIN_V 433 or both CHIN_V 491, CHIN_V 493. Recommended pre-requisites: one of CHIN_V 313, CHIN_V 314, CHIN_V 317, CHIN_V 318, CHIN_V 323, CHIN_V 437, CHIN_V 443, CHIN_V 444, CHIN_V 447, CHIN_V 448. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CHIN
title: Chinese-English Modern Literary Translation
description: Practicum in the art of literary translation from modern Chinese into English, covering a range of literary genres and emphasizing peer learning. Open to both heritage and non-heritage students. This course is recommended for students with credit for any 300-level CHIN_V course and placement approval. For more information on placement approval, please visit Placement Tests at http://asia.ubc.ca/undergraduate/placement-tests/ .

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Cinema Studies
description: Basic aesthetic, economic, sociological, and technological aspects of film. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 100 or CINE_V 100. Equivalency: FIST_V 100.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Canadian Cinema
description: History and aesthetics of Canadian cinema. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 200 or CINE_V 200. Equivalency: FIST_V 200.

subject: CINE
title: Early Cinema
description: Aesthetics, economics, history, and technological characteristics of international early film. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 210 or CINE_V 210. Equivalency: FIST_V 210.

subject: CINE
title: Hollywood Cinema 1930-1960
description: Analysis of the aesthetics, economics, history and technological characteristics of the Classical Hollywood period. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 220 or CINE_V 220. Equivalency: FIST_V 220.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Asian Cinema
description: Overview of the cinemas of China, India, Japan, and Korea. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 230 or CINE_V 230. Equivalency: FIST_V 230.

subject: CINE
title: Media Industries
description: Overview of today's film and media industries, and of the concepts governing their practices. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 240 or CINE_V 240. Equivalency: FIST_V 240.

subject: CINE
title: Cult Cinema
description: Overview of world cult cinema. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 300 or CINE_V 300. Equivalency: FIST_V 300.

subject: CINE
title: Studies in Film Theory
description: A seminar introducing the many theoretical approaches to film: formalist, historical, Marxist, psychoanalytic, semiotic, and structuralist. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 331 or CINE_V 331. Equivalency: FIST_V 331.

subject: CINE
title: Studies in Genre or Period
description: A seminar examining one or more genres or periods, such as the Western, Film Noir, Science Fiction, Films of the 1980's. Also includes study of national cinemas. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 332 or CINE_V 332. Equivalency: FIST_V 332.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in Documentary
description: An analysis of the representational strategies and ethics of the form. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 334 or CINE_V 334. Equivalency: FIST_V 334.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in European Cinema
description: Topics may include a study of a European national cinema. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 336 or CINE_V 336. Equivalency: FIST_V 336.

subject: CINE
title: Asian and Australasian Cinema
description: Topics may include an analysis of a national cinema, such as that of China, India, or Australia. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 338 or CINE_V 338. Equivalency: FIST_V 338.

subject: CINE
title: Media Audiences
description: Overview of approaches for studying audiences and receptions of film and contemporary media. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 340 or CINE_V 340. Equivalency: FIST_V 340.

subject: CINE
title: Studies in Auteurism
description: A seminar examining the work of one or more directors, such as John Ford, Francois Truffaut, Denys Arcand, Margarethe Von Trotta, or of a screenwriter over many films. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 430 or CINE_V 430. Equivalency: FIST_V 430.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in Motion Picture Forms
description: Animation, experimental, and/or multimedia. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for FIST_V 432 or CINE_V 432. Equivalency: FIST_V 432.

subject: CINE
title: Studies in Film
description: A seminar devoted to a topic of current interest in film. Topic will change from year to year. May be repeated for credit when topics differ. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for FIST_V 434 or CINE_V 434. Equivalency: FIST_V 434.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in American Cinema Since 1960
description: Topics may include an analysis of a specific period. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 436 or CINE_V 436. Equivalency: FIST_V 436.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in Canadian Cinema
description: Topics may include an analysis of the Canadian Governmental agencies supporting Film Production. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for FIST_V 438 or CINE_V 438. Equivalency: FIST_V 438.

subject: CINE
title: Majors and Honours Seminar
description: Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 445 or CINE_V 445. Equivalency: FIST_V 445.

subject: CINE
title: Honours Essay
description: A course allowing honours students to work with a faculty member on a major research paper. Credit will be granted for only one of FIST_V 449 or CINE_V 449. Equivalency: FIST_V 449

subject: CIVL
title: Introduction to Civil Engineering
description: The design process; graphical, visualization and computational tools; civil engineering disciplines; decision-making; teamwork; conceptual design project reflecting community, economic, environmental, sustainability and technical considerations. . Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150, APSC_O 176, ENGL_O 109, ENGL_O 112. Corequisite: CIVL_V 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Technical Communication in Civil Engineering
description: Written and oral communication in civil engineering. Business correspondence, business meetings, poster presentations, oral presentations and technical reports. Restricted to students in second year of the Civil Engineering program. Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150, APSC_O 176, ENGL_O 109, ENGL_O 112. Corequisite: CIVL_V 201. Equivalency: APSC_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Fundamentals of Environmental Engineering
description: Environmental engineering issues and projects; application of scientific and engineering principles to addressing these; soil, water and air pollution, and remediation. Prerequisite: CHEM 154. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Soil Mechanics I
description: Soil classification, principle of effective stress, analysis of seepage, filter criteria, introduction to shear strength and slope stability analysis. . Prerequisite: One of CIVL_V 230, MECH_V 260, WOOD_V 276 or third-year standing in ENVE_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Fluid Mechanics I
description: Fluid properties, hydrostatics, kinematics, and fluid dynamics: energy and momentum methods with applications. Dimensional analysis, modelling, introduction to flow in pipes and forces on immersed objects. . Prerequisite: All of PHYS_V 170, MATH_V 101. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Solid Mechanics
description: Stress and strain, Hooke's law, axially loaded members, torsion, shear forces and bending moments in beams, bending and shear stresses in beams, composite members, introduction to inelastic and statically indeterminate problems. . Prerequisite: All of PHYS_V 170, MATH_V 101. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Structural Mechanics
description: Deflection of beams and structural systems; analysis of determinate structures; combined axial load and bending; beam- columns; buckling (stability); biaxial stresses and strains; construction and testing of model structures. . Prerequisite: All of MATH_V 152, CIVL_V 230. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Plane Surveying
description: Theory and application of plane surveying methods. Introduction to and use of compass, transit, tape, and level. Construction and topographic surveys. Reduction of field data and construction of drawings. Demonstration of modern instruments, remote sensing methods and geographical information systems (GIS). This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Engineering and Sustainable Development
description: Implications of a finite biosphere and the complexities inherent in environmental decision-making. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Construction Engineering and Management
description: Project delivery systems: traditional; construction management; turnkey; project management. Network planning methods. Activity planning, including construction methods selection. Estimating, bidding and bonding. Project control tools and procedures. Human resources, including equity considerations; occupational health and safety and quality control. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Modelling and Decision-Making in Civil Engineering
description: Introduction to systems engineering; applications of decision-making, modelling, and programming, including probabilistic analyses and optimization, to civil engineering projects; review of numerical methods. Prerequisite: All of MATH_V 152, CIVL_V 201, STAT_V 251. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Civil Engineering Impacts
description: The social and biophysical context of infrastructure and the impact of civil engineering on people, the economy, and the environment. Specific topics vary from year to year. Prerequisite: CIVL_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Computational Tools in Civil Engineering
description: Computational and numerical solutions to civil engineering problems; application to a civil engineering design project that reflects community, economic, environmental and technical considerations. Prerequisite: All of CIVL_V 201, MATH_V 256. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Water, Society and Environmental Engineering
description: Environmental systems, risk and resilience, and the dynamics of water availability, management, and treatment within responsible and sustainable stewardship frameworks. Prerequisite: CIVL_V 204 or third-year standing or higher in IGEN. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Soil Mechanics II
description: One-dimensional compression and stress-strain response of soils with application to estimation of the settlements and capacities of foundations and of retaining walls. Prerequisite: CIVL_V 210 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Fluid Mechanics II
description: Two-dimensional flow around immersed objects; velocity and pressure fields; lift and drag on cylinders and aerofoils; fluid loads on structures and structural response; pumps and turbines; analysis and design of pipeline systems; unsteady flow in pipes; frictionless water hammer analysis. . Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 201, ENVE_V 201, CIVL_V 203 and all of CIVL_V 215, MATH_V 256. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Hydrology and Open Channel Flow
description: Introduction to open channel hydraulics, engineering hydrology, and water resource systems; estimation of design discharge; flood statistics; nonuniform steady open channel flow; energy and momentum principles, backwater analysis; culvert and bridge hydraulics. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 215 and one of APSC_V 201, CIVL_V 203, ENVE_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Civil Engineering Materials
description: The structure and properties of common Civil Engineering materials: aggregates, Portland cement, concrete, wood, steel and other construction materials. The emphasis is on the relationship between the structure of materials and their mechanical and durability properties. Prerequisite: All of APSC_V 278, APSC_V 279. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Steel and Timber Design
description: Introduction to limit states design of steel and timber structures: design objectives, design loads and load combinations, structural safety, material properties, design of tension and compression members, beams, columns, and connections. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 231. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Structural Analysis
description: Introduction to indeterminate structural analysis; approximate analysis of structures; calculation of displacements using virtual work; flexibility (force) method; stiffness method for frames; moment distribution method; influence lines, introduction to structural dynamics. . Prerequisite: All of CIVL_V 231, MATH_V 152. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Transportation Engineering I
description: The analysis and design of transportation facilities; vehicle motion and vehicle/pavement interaction; geometric design of roadways; traffic flow analysis and level of service; fundamentals of intersection design; traffic safety. Prerequisite: STAT_V 251. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Professionalism and Law in Civil Engineering
description: The Professional Governance Act; professional ethics, conflicts of interest, confidentiality and accountability; health and safety; sustainable development and environmental stewardship; equity considerations; design and construction contracts, specifications and tendering; labour and employment law; dispute resolution; evidence and expert witnesses; torts and legal liability. Third-year standing or higher in B.A.Sc. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Engineering Economic Analysis
description: Time value of money; cash flow analysis; comparing options; depreciation, taxes, and inflation; financial accounting; company structures; public sector projects; decision-making. Third-year standing or higher in B.A.Sc. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Introduction to Solid Waste Management
description: Characteristics of solid wastes; solid waste collection, treatment, and disposal; evaluation and analysis of landfills, composting, combined treatment, recycle, and re-use. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 204. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Water Treatment and Waste Management
description: Processes used in water and wastewater treatment. Conditions which necessitate treatment of water or wastewater, water and wastewater treatment processes and plant design. Municipal services required and associated with solid waste management. Credit will be granted for only one of CHBE_V 373 or CIVL_V 406. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 305. or third-year standing in ENVL program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Environmental Laboratory Analysis
description: Testing procedures used in water quality studies and in the operation of water and wastewater treatment plants. Prerequisite: CHEM_V 154. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Geo-Environmental Engineering
description: Environmental contamination, regulatory requirements, site investigation, migration of contaminants, containment systems, site remediation technologies, design considerations related to soil-contaminant interactions, hydrogeology, geochemistry and types of contaminants. Design and performance case histories. Prerequisite: CIVL 316 and fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Municipal Engineering
description: Design of municipal infrastructure, including streets, water supply networks, and sewers, garbage collection and solid waste management. Focus is on solutions for providing an adequate water supply, collecting and disposing of stormwater and sewage, and managing excess stormwater flow. . Prerequisite: All of CIVL_V 315, CIVL_V 316. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Foundation Engineering I
description: An introduction to the process of foundation engineering. Empirical and analytical approaches used in current professional practice. Topics include site investigation, preloading, liquefaction assessment, ground improvement, design of shallow and deep foundations, and retaining structures. The importance of geology and technical communication are emphasized. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 311. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Foundation Engineering II
description: Aspects of Geotechnical Engineering. Design considerations illustrated by case histories pertinent to BC. Topics include: site investigation, terrain analyses, in situ testing, groundwater problems, deep foundations, tie back walls and bracing, tailings impoundments, Northern construction, ground ice, dikes and dams engineering. Many case histories presented in part by prominent consulting engineers in BC. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 410. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Design of Earth Dams and Containment Structures
description: Purpose and types of dams; design criteria; construction sequence; compaction; seepage; filter design; factors influencing the design of earth dams; stability and deformation under static and earthquake loading; slope protection; field instrumentation. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 311. Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Water Resource Engineering
description: An introduction to the planning and design of water resource systems, stream systems, and municipal and hydropower engineering. . Prerequisite: All of CIVL_V 315, CIVL_V 316, STAT_V 251. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Environmental Hydraulics
description: Application of hydraulic engineering principles to problems of environmental concern. Pollutant transport and dispersion. Mixing in rivers and lakes. Theory of jets and plumes. Design of outfall diffusers. . Prerequisite: All of CIVL_V 316, MATH_V 256. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Coastal Engineering
description: Linear wave theory; wave shoaling, refraction and diffraction; random waves; wave generation; long waves, tides and currents; coastal structures; beaches and coasts; mixing processes; harbour and marinas; coastal modelling. Credit will only be given for one of CIVL_V 417 or CIVL_V 540. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 316 and one of EOSC_V 213, MATH_V 256. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Engineering Hydrology
description: Hydrologic processes - weather, precipitation, infiltration, evaporation, snowmelt and runoff generation. Emphasis on quantitative techniques including: hydrograph analysis, reservoir and channel routing, statistical methods and design floods, hydrologic modelling. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 316. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Concrete Technology
description: Physical and chemical properties and microstructure of hydrated Portland cement; construction practices; modern use of industrial by-products such as fly ash, blast furnace slag, silica fume and metakaolin; use of chemical admixtures; environmental issues; properties of hardened concrete; issues in standardized and accelerated testing, non-destructive testing. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 320. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Project Based Learning in Civil Engineering Materials
description: Some topical problems will be identified and students in groups will carry out experiments to study the materials involved. Site visits and external consultations are an integral requirement. Prerequisite: CIVL_V 320. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Case Studies of Construction Methods
description: Identification and evaluation of solutions to construction site operation problems: the relationship between design and construction; factors affecting productivity and safety; measurement of on-site performance. Credit will be granted for only one of CIVL_V 425 or CIVL_V 521. Restricted to students with fourth-year standing or higher. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Virtual Design and Construction
description: Building information modelling (BIM), 4D/5D modelling, design coordination, BIM execution and performance assessment, and integrated project delivery methods. Credit will be granted for only one of CIVL_V 426 or CIVL_V 526. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Applied Machine Learning for Construction and Facility Management
description: Introduction to classical machine learning algorithms, including linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, and neural networks, and their applications to Civil Engineering practices, such as construction safety, building energy conservation, and traffic simulation. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor. Prerequisite: CIVL 300. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Design of Concrete Structures
description: Non-linear response of reinforced concrete members subjected to axial load, bending and shear; design of simple one-way members including beams, columns, slabs and footings. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 231. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
description: Design of steel structures to resist vertical and lateral loads. Floor and roof systems including conceptual layout, floor deck, beams, joists, trusses, and columns. Stability issues and limit states design. Connections and construction aspects. Seismic design. . Prerequisite: All of CIVL_V 331, CIVL_V 332. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Advanced Concrete Design
description: Design of members subjected to shear and torsion, long columns, two-way slab systems; seismic design of low-rise concrete buildings. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 430. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Advanced Structural Analysis
description: Shear flow, shear deformation, St. Venant torsion, warping torsion, P-delta and geometric stiffness, buckling of columns and frames, cylindrical shells, beams on elastic foundation, shear wall analysis, elasto-plastic analysis. Introduction to the finite element method. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 332. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Matrix Structural Analysis and Dynamics
description: Further techniques in matrix structural analysis; non-rigid supports, temperature-shrinkage effects, computer implementation; matrix representation of structural dynamics; mode shapes, natural frequencies, continuous systems; lumped mass models, modal analysis, response spectra. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 332. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Introduction to Ship Structures
description: Structural theory and practice of ship structural design; longitudinal and transverse strength of hull girder; plates and shells; matrix analysis; introduction to classification society rules; ship section design synthesis; finite element analysis. . Prerequisite: One of CIVL_V 332, MECH_V 360. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Design of Timber Structures
description: Design of timber structural elements using limit states design principles; joints and fasteners, sawn lumber and engineered wood products, light frame systems and shear walls. Credit will be granted for only one of CIVL_V 439 or CIVL_V 516. . Prerequisite: One of CIVL_V 331, WOOD_V 386. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Transportation Engineering II
description: Traffic operations and network analysis: macroscopic traffic models and shockwaves analysis; queueing theory and gaps; advanced signalized intersection analysis and design; freeway weaving and interchange analysis; data collection including field exercises. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 340. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Transportation Planning and Analysis
description: Transportation systems planning and analysis: data needs; surveys and analysis; sampling techniques; trip generation; trip distribution; modal choice; trip assignment; traffic impact studies; system evaluation. Credit will be granted for only one of CIVL_V 441, CIVL_V 583 or PLAN_V 535. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 340. Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Civil Engineering Design Project I
description: Integration and application of previously acquired knowledge and skills to find design solutions for a multi-disciplinary civil engineering project. Focus on conceptual and preliminary design. Prerequisite: CIVL_V 303 and fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Civil Engineering Design Project II
description: Integration and application of previously acquired knowledge and skills to find design solutions for a multi-disciplinary civil engineering design project. Focus on detailed design. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 445. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Emerging Contaminants in Water Systems
description: Emerging contaminants in water systems. Organic contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and other chemicals used in consumer products and industrial processes. Partitioning of contaminants in natural water systems. Methods of water treatment. Credit will be granted for only one of CIVL_V 466 or CIVL_V 566. . Prerequisite: CIVL_V 305. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Environmental Stewardship in Civil Engineering
description: Co-evolution of human and natural environments, approaches to the design, construction and operations of interacting built, social, and ecological systems, the integrative design process and related strategies. . Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 261, APSC_V 262, APSC_V 263, CIVL_V 250, CIVL_V 302. Third-year standing in BASc program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Building Science
description: Building science concepts associated with the design of modern buildings, focusing particularly on the building envelope's role in environmental separation, controlling the movement of heat, air, and water in liquid and vapour states. . Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Directed Studies in Civil Engineering
description: Independent studies on a special topic. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CIVL
title: Topics in Civil Engineering
description: Seminar or lecture. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CLST
title: Golden Age of Athens
description: The history and culture, values, and achievements of fifth-century Athens.

subject: CLST
title: Late Republican and Early Imperial Rome
description: The history and culture, values, and achievements of Late Republican and Early Imperial Rome.

subject: CLST
title: Gods, Graves, and Goods: The Archaeology of Ancient Greece and Rome
description: A survey of the material cultures of the pre-classical and classical civilizations of Greece and Rome, illustrating the principles and techniques used to illuminate the archaeological history of these civilizations.

subject: CLST
title: Life and Society in Classical Antiquity
description: Topics in Greek and Roman life and society.

subject: CPEN
title: Computing Systems I
description: Boolean algebra; combinational and sequential circuits; organization and operation of microcomputers, memory addressing modes, representation of information, instruction sets, machine and assembly language programming, systems programs, I/O structures, I/O interfacing and I/O programming, introduction to digital system design using microcomputers. Credit will be granted for only one of CPEN_V 211, CPEN_V 312. . Prerequisite: APSC_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Computing Systems II
description: Abstractions at the hardware-software interface and their low-level implementation. Procedure invocation, dynamic dispatch, and related exploits; library linkage, virtual memory, heap management, garbage collection, and caches; interrupts, signals, and processes; threads, locks, and cache coherence; files, devices, and network topology. Credit will only be given for one of CPEN_V 212, CPSC_V 213. Prerequisite: CPEN_V 211 and one of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 223, CPSC_V 259. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Construction I
description: Design, implementation, reasoning about software systems: abstraction and specification of software, testing, verification, abstract data types, object-oriented design, type hierarchies, concurrent software design. . Prerequisite: APSC_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Design for Engineers I
description: Introduction to robust software design: static typing, procedural specifications, unit testing, black-box & white-box tests, user- defined data types (representations, invariants, abstraction functions), data abstractions, communicating design (e.g., UML). . Prerequisite: APSC_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Technical Communication
description: Written and oral communication in engineering. Technical description, report preparation, business correspondence, and oral presentation of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of Electrical and Computer Engineering programs. Credit will be granted for only one of ELEC_V 281, CPEN_V 281, BMEG_V 201 or APSC_V 201. . Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 112, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Computer Engineering Design Studio I
description: Design projects involving hardware (electronic devices and circuits, microcomputers) and software. . Prerequisite: CPEN_V 211. Corequisite: ELEC_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Special Topics in Computer Engineering
description: Lectures or projects on subjects of current interest. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Digital Systems Design
description: Advanced combinational and sequential electronic system design. Hardware specification, modelling, and simulation using hardware description languages (HDLs) and CAD tools. Design with programmable logic including FPGA's. Applications include complex state machines, microcontrollers, arithmetic circuits, and interface units. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 211, CPEN_V 312. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Digital Systems and Microcomputers
description: Data representation in digital computers; boolean algebra; the design and optimization and implementation of combinatorial and sequential circuits; modern digital circuit technologies; memory and programmable logic devices; organization and operation of microcomputers; data/address bus organization; input-output interfacing. Credit will be granted for only one of CPEN_V 312, CPEN_V 211. . Prerequisite: One of ELEC_V 201, ELEC_V 204, ELEC_V 203, MECH_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Construction II
description: Contemporary concepts and techniques for developing interactive software applications: client-server architectures; session oriented systems; security and scalability; models of application deployment.. Prerequisite: All of CPEN_V 221, CPSC_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Engineering
description: Engineering practices for the development of non-trivial software-intensive systems including requirements specification, software architecture, implementation, verification, and maintenance. Iterative development. Recognized standards, guidelines, and models. Credit will only be granted for only one of CPSC_V 310, CPEN_V 321. . Corequisite: CPEN_V 322. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Operating Systems
description: Operating systems, their design and their implementation. Process concurrency, synchronization, communication and scheduling. Device drivers, memory management, virtual memory, file systems, networking and security. Prerequisite: CPEN 212 and CPEN 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Design for Engineers II
description: Use of operating systems abstractions; real-time systems; principles of concurrent and multi-threaded programming; information structures; introduction to object oriented analysis; design, and modelling using UML; software testing. This course is not open to students in the Computer Engineering program. . Prerequisite: One of CPSC_V 259, CPEN_V 223. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Machine Learning with Engineering Applications
description: Foundations and concepts of data science and machine learning with applications to engineering problems. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 318, MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_V 321, ELEC_V 321 and one of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 223, CPSC_V 259. Credit cannot be obtained for both CPEN_V 355 and CPSC_V 340. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Computer Engineering Design Studio II
description: Design and implementation of a hardware platform and software design and implementation at the operating system and application layers. Project management skills. Effective presentations. Going-forward, credit will be given for only one of CPEN_V 291, CPEN_V 391. . Prerequisite: All of CPEN_V 212, CPSC_V 221, ELEC_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Topics in Computer Engineering
description: Lectures or projects on subjects of current interest.

subject: CPEN
title: Computer Architecture
description: Modern processors, GPUs, and memory hierarchies; quantitative principles and instruction set design; pipelining, superscalar issue, out-of-order execution, branch prediction and speculation; memory hierarchies, caches, virtual addressing, prefetching, coherence, and consistency; multicores, VLIW, on-chip networks, and other advanced architectures. Credit will be granted for only one of CPEN_V 411 or CPSC_V 313. . Prerequisite: CPEN_V 211 and CPEN_V 212. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Microcomputer Systems Design
description: Microprocessor and system buses; advanced I/O methods; priority interrupts; event/exception handling; serial I/O; computer networking; memory system design; interaction of hardware and software, microprocessor comparison, testability issues, safety critical systems. . Prerequisite: CPEN_V 311 and one of CPEN_V 211, CPEN_V 312. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Gate-Model Quantum Computing
description: A software-based introduction to gate model quantum computing algorithms. Basic elements of quantum computation; analysis and software implementation of Grover's algorithm, Shor's algorithm, quantum compilation, variational algorithms, Hamiltonian simulation, noise characterization. Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 223, CPSC_V 259, CPSC_V 221, PHYS_V 210, and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Project Management
description: Advanced project planning, cost estimation and scheduling. Project management tools. Factors influencing productivity and success. Productivity metrics. Analysis of options and risk. Tools. Case studies. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 321, CPSC_V 310. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Testing and Analysis
description: Different levels of testing including unit, integration, system, performance and regression levels. Requirements flowdown. Problem tracking. Coverage criteria. Static methods. Tools support. Specialized techniques. Assessment of correctness, reliability, safety. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 321, CPSC_V 210, CPSC_V 310. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Software Architecture
description: Software architecture as a bridge from requirements to implementation. Architectural description and patterns. Iterative development. Use of commercial off-the-shelf products. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 321, CPSC_V 310. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Design of Distributed Software Applications
description: Communications, processes, naming, synchronization, consistency and replication, fault tolerance, middleware, and security technologies for distributed applications. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 331, CPSC_V 313 and one of CPEN_V 221, CPSC_V 210. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Real-time System Design
description: Multi-tasking; interrupt-driven systems; task scheduling; schedulability analysis; inter-process communication and synchronization; resource management; performance measurement; hardware/software integration; hardware/software tradeoffs; system reliability. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 333, CPEN_V 331, CPSC_V 313. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Human Computer Interfaces in Engineering Design
description: Practical issues for interfaces for modern software. Task analysis, user modelling, usability engineering, representations, metaphors, prototyping tools. Applications: interactive multimedia systems, engineering, scientific visualization, engineering design. . Prerequisite: CPSC_V 221 and one of CPEN_V 221, CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 333. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Introduction to Cybersecurity
description: Security risks, threats, and vulnerabilities from technical perspectives; cryptography; software and web security; access control, assurance, accountability; usable privacy and security; engineering of secure systems; cryptocurrencies. . Prerequisite: One of CPEN_V 333, CPEN_V 331, CPSC_V 313. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Deep Learning
description: Fundamentals of deep learning, including architectures (e.g., MLPs, CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, and GNNs) and learning algorithms under different paradigms (supervised / unsupervised / reinforcement learning). Emphasis on design principles and motivating applications. Recommended pre-requisite: CPEN_V 355 or CPSC_V 340. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 318, MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_V 321, ELEC_V 321 and one of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 223, CPSC_V 259. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Economic Analysis of Engineering Projects
description: Time-money relationships; economic analysis of alternatives including the effects of interest rates, inflation, depreciation, taxation and uncertainty; cost estimation and budgeting; financial analysis of engineering operations. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Computer Engineering Capstone Design Project
description: Design, analysis, and implementation of solutions in response to a real-world computer engineering problem, provided by industry, research laboratories, or other suitable entities. Includes coverage of topics such as project management. or Prerequisite: All of CPEN_V 331, CPSC_V 320 and one of CPEN_V 311, CPEN_V 322; and one of CPEN_V 291, CPEN_V 391. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Research Experience in Computer Engineering
description: Directed research experience. Communication of research ideas. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: Third-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CPEN
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Project in electrical engineering or computer engineering involving design, experimental and/or computer simulation work as selected from topics supplied by faculty members. An individual project thesis is to be prepared according to specifications available from the departmental office. or . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Creative Writing
description: Techniques of and practice in multiple genres of writing, including fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, screenplay, stageplay, graphic forms, lyric forms, children's literature, and writing for new media. Manuscript submission is not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing Poetry
description: An exploration of and practice in the writing of poetry, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of poetry. Manuscript submission not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing for Children and Young Adults
description: Techniques of and practice in creating, developing and writing for children and young adults. Manuscript submission is not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing Creative Nonfiction
description: An exploration of and practice in the writing of creative nonfiction, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of creative nonfiction. Manuscript submission not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing for the Screen
description: Techniques of and practice in creating, developing, and writing a screenplay. Manuscript submission is not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing for Graphic Forms
description: Techniques of and practice in creating, developing, and writing the graphic novel, manga, and other forms of illustrated writing. The ability to draw is not required. Manuscript submission is not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing Fiction
description: An exploration of the writing of fiction, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of fiction. Manuscript submission not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Video Game Writing
description: A practical, project-based class for the creation of indie-scale, story-driven video games.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing for the New Media
description: An exploration of and practice in writing for new media, including podcasting, blogging, and writing for websites, games, and online environments. Manuscript submission is not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Short Screenplay Workshop
description: Restricted to B.F.A. Film Production students.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Creative Writing with an Indigenous Focus
description: Covers three genres from fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, radio drama, radio feature, or stageplay.

subject: CRWR
title: Introduction to Writing for Comedic Forms
description: An examination of and practice in creative writing in comedic forms, including stand-up, sketch, film, new media, and text. Manuscript submission not required for admission.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing Poetry
description: The writing of poetry in various forms using a combination of workshopping and online modules. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 201.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for Podcast
description: Exploration of and practice in writing for podcast.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing for Children and Young Adults
description: The writing of work for children and young adults in various forms using a combination of workshopping and online modules. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 203.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing of Creative Nonfiction
description: An exploration of and practice in the writing of creative non-fiction, covering four of the more basic forms of this genre: memoir, profile, commentary, and exposition. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 205.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing for the Screen
description: An exploration of and practice in writing for the screen, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of screenwriting. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 206.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing for the Stage
description: An exploration of practice in the writing of the one-act stage play, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of this genre. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 200.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing for Graphic Forms
description: The writing of graphica (comics, manga and graphic novels), using a combination of workshopping and online modules. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 208.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing Fiction
description: An exploration of the writing of fiction, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of fiction. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 209.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Video Game Writing
description: Narrative design and writing for video games. Prerequisite: CRWR_V 210.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing for Lyric Forms
description: Techniques of and practice in writing for lyric forms, including song lyrics, lyrical narratives, and libretti. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR_V 200.

subject: CRWR
title: Interactive Storytelling
description: Origin, theory and practice of interactive story forms. Exploring structural links between interactive theatre, gaming, and extended (virtual, mixed, and augmented) reality. Prerequisite: One of CRWR 213 or B.M.S. student with 3rd year standing or higher.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Writing for Television
description: Elements of episodic and serialized comedic and dramatic television writing with writing practice applied to primary formats and genres. Prerequisite: CRWR 206.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing Genre Fiction
description: Exploration and practice in writing major genres of genre fiction, including fantasy, science fiction, romance, crime, horror, and historical fiction. Prerequisite: CRWR_V 209.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Comedic Forms
description: Contemporary and historical comedic writing in a variety of forms. Emphasis on critical analysis and creative writing of comedic works, and changes in the comedic landscape. Prerequisite: CRWR_V 230.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Poetry Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing poetry. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 301.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Children and Young Adult Writing Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing for children and young adults. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 303.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Creative Nonfiction Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing of creative nonfiction. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 305.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Screenplay Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing for the screen. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 306.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Graphic Forms Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing for graphic forms. The ability to draw is not required. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 308.

subject: CRWR
title: Intermediate Fiction Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing of fiction. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 309.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing Poetry I
description: A workshop class in the writing of poetry. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for New Media I
description: An advanced workshop class in writing for new media. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for Children and Young Adults I
description: A workshop class in writing for Children and Young Adults. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for Radio I
description: A workshop class in writing for the radio. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing Creative Nonfiction I
description: A workshop class in writing creative nonfiction, which may include forms such as autobiography, rhetoric, literary journalism, and the personal essay. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for the Screen I
description: A workshop class in writing for the screen. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing of Drama for the Stage I
description: A workshop class in writing of drama for the stage. Studio work is required, and some plays may be given a live stage production in Brave New Play Rites (adjudication process involved). Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for Graphic Forms I
description: A workshop class in the writing of graphic novel, manga, and other forms of illustrated writing. The ability to draw is not required. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing Fiction I
description: A workshop class in the writing of fiction. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Video Game Writing
description: A workshop class on writing for video games. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for Lyric Forms I
description: A workshop class exploring the words that accompany music in varied forms including pop, art, musical theatre, and opera. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Workshop in Literary Translation I
description: A workshop class in literary translation. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing. Prerequisite: Proficiency in a language other than English.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing for Television I
description: A workshop class in writing for television. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Play Development Workshop
description: An interdisciplinary course, in cooperation with the Theatre program, emphasizing script development through scene work, character development and stagecraft. Prerequisite: Manuscript submission or equivalent theatre experience.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing Speculative Fiction
description: Workshop-based class focused on writing speculative fiction, including fantasy, science fiction, and horror; emphasis on reading various genres and peer feedback. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Indigenous Writing
description: Advanced study of contemporary Indigenous writing in North America across genres focusing on the production of critical and creative writing about coloniality, race, history, and identity. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Experimental Forms
description: Interdisciplinary perspectives on non-traditional forms of writing. Emphasis on combinations of poetry with prose, extra-literary structures, and visuals. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Climate Writing
description: Workshop-based class focused on writing related to climate change and environmental issues; emphasis on reading various genres and peer feedback. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing. A maximum of 6 credits is permitted between CRWR_V 425 and 525.

subject: CRWR
title: Preparation for a Career in Writing
description: Pass/Fail. Credit will be granted for only one of CRWR 430 or CRWR 530. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: CRWR
title: Writing Comedic Forms
description: A workshop class exploring comedic writing in varied forms including film and television, prose and poetry, non-fiction, and new media. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

subject: CRWR
title: Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Group projects and workshops with students majoring in other creative arts. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing. Credit will be granted for only one of CRWR_V 440, THTR_V 469, VISA_V 469, MUSC_V 469. Equivalency: THTR_V 469, VISA_V 469, MUSC_V 469.

title: Writing Poetry II

subject: DSCI
title: Introduction to Data Science
description: Use of data science tools to summarize, visualize, and analyze data. Sensible workflows and clear interpretations are emphasized. .

subject: DSCI
title: Navigating Data: Acquisition, Exploration and Management
description: Acquiring data through web scraping and generating synthetic data via simulations. Sampling and experimental designs. Reporting and visualizing data and data quality. Data privacy and ownership. Emphasis on case studies and real data sets. Prerequisite: DSCI_V 100 or DATA_O 101.

subject: DSCI
title: Discrete Mathematics for Data Science
description: Boolean algebra and logical inference, proof techniques, sets, relations and functions, regular expressions, and data filtering. Prerequisite: All of a) DSCI_V 100 or DATA_O 101; b) MATH_V 100, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, SCIE_V 001 or MATH_O 100; and c) CPSC_V 103 or CPSC_V 110.

subject: DSCI
title: Data Structures for Data Science
description: Object-oriented programming. Design and analysis of basic algorithms and data structures especially relevant to data science. Algorithm analysis methods, basic data structures, graphs and graph algorithms. Prerequisite: (a) DSCI_V 220, or (b) CPSC_V 121 and one of CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 221.

subject: DSCI
title: Reproducible and Trustworthy Workflows for Data Science
description: Data science methods to automate the running and testing of code and analytic reports, manage data analysis software dependencies, package and deploy software for data analysis, and collaborate with others using version control. Prerequisite: One of (a) DSCI_V 221, (b) DSCI_V 100 and one of CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 221, or (c) DSCI_V 100, either MATH_V 210 or ECON_V 323, and either CPSC_V 107 or CPSC_V 110.

subject: DSCI
title: Visualization for Data Science
description: Analysis, design, and implementation of static and interactive visual representations; visualization literacy; data communication; exploratory Data Analysis; application of theoretical principles to visualization development. Prerequisite: STAT_V 201 and one of CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 221, DSCI_V 221.

subject: DSCI
title: Fairness, Accountability, Transparency and Ethics (FATE) in Data Science
description: Ethical application of data science and machine learning algorithms. Application of ethical theories in real-world case studies. Data ownership, collection, and validity. Algorithm auditing, fairness and transparency. Reducing unfairness in algorithms. Deployment of predictive models and dissemination of results. Prerequisite: One of CPSC 330, CPSC 340, STAT 301, STAT 406.

subject: ENPH
title: Introduction to Instrument Design
description: Practice in engineering design and instrument development including mechanical and electrical design, and communications with sensors, actuators. Micro-controller implementation and system integration. Engineering design review process and presentations. Engineering communication in design and product release. Prerequisite: ENPH 259.

subject: ENPH
title: Heat and Thermodynamics
description: Thermometry, thermal properties of matter; heat transfer by conduction; convection and radiation; kinetic theory of gases and gas laws; heat engines; refrigeration; change of state; first and second laws of thermodynamics. Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 254, MATH 255; and either (a) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 109 or (b) one of PHYS 102, PHYS 153 or (c) all of PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 159 or (d) all of PHYS 118, PHYS 119 or (e) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 119.

subject: ENPH
title: Experimental Techniques
description: Basic experimental techniques in acquisition, analysis, and presentation and communication of data and technical results. Prerequisite: One of APSC 176, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 112, ENGL 120, ENGL 121, WRDS 150 and either (a) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 109 or (b) one of PHYS 102, PHYS 153 or (c) SCIE 001 or (d) all of PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 159 or (e) all of PHYS 118, PHYS 119 or (f) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 119.

subject: ENPH
title: Mechanics II
description: Dynamics: systems of particles, kinematics and kinetics of rigid bodies (plane motion), energy and momentum, rotating coordinates. Prerequisite: PHYS 170.

subject: ENPH
title: Laboratory Techniques in Physics
description: Some of the experiments will be based on the lecture material for PHYS 301. Other techniques and subjects will also be covered. Corequisite: PHYS 301.

subject: ENPH
title: Engineering Physics Project I
description: Engineering project planning, execution and reporting. The course involves carrying out an open-ended Engineering project to meet specific performance metrics on an industry relevant topic selected by instructors. Reporting on progress is both oral and written. . Prerequisite: All of ENPH_V 253, CPEN_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ENPH
title: Engineering Physics Project II
description: Project planning, management and reporting. This course involves writing a project proposal, carrying out an open-ended Engineering project, and reporting the results both orally and in writing. . Prerequisite: ENPH_V 253. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ENPH
title: Engineering Physics Project III
description: Projects designed to give students research development and design experience. Projects are provided by research faculty in Science and Engineering and from local industry. . Prerequisite: ENPH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ENPH
title: Engineering Physics Project IV
description: An optional course for those students wishing to continue their project work beyond the development in ENPH_V 479. . Prerequisite: ENPH_V 479. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ENPH
title: Entrepreneurial Projects I
description: A project course for students pursuing entrepreneurial training within Engineering Physics, and wishing to further develop projects resulting from ENPH_V 459. . Prerequisite: ENPH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: The Solid Earth: A Dynamic Planet
description: Earth's origin, composition, structure, and natural resources. Plate tectonics as the driving force for volcanism, mountain building, and earthquakes. Imaging Earth's interior. Environmental geoscience and sustainability. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list for the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.)

subject: EOSC
title: Laboratory Exploration of Planet Earth
description: An examination of the processes that shape and change the planet earth. This laboratory course is an appropriate complement to EOSC 110, EOSC 112, EOSC 114, EOSC 116 but can also be taken independently.

subject: EOSC
title: The Climate System
description: Introduction to Earth's climate system: radiation balance, greenhouse effect, atmosphere and ocean circulation, plate tectonics, biosphere interactions, and the carbon cycle. Applications to understand the causes of climate change, from long-term climate evolution to modern human-induced climate change. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list, within the Faculty of Science section in the Calendar.)

subject: EOSC
title: The Catastrophic Earth: Natural Disasters
description: Introduction to causes and physical characteristics of disasters such as volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, tsunamis, hurricanes, storm surge, thunderstorms, tornadoes, landslides, wind waves, meteor impacts, mass extinctions.

subject: EOSC
title: Mesozoic Earth: Time of the Dinosaurs.
description: Earth's tectonics, climate, and oceans during the time of the dinosaurs. Reading the fossil record of Earth from its earliest origins up to and including the Mesozoic, 250 - 65 million years ago.

subject: EOSC
title: Earth's Treasures: Gold and Gems
description: Origin, properties, valuation, prospecting and geology of gold, platinum, silver, diamonds, rubies, emeralds, and other precious metals and gems.

subject: EOSC
title: Earth Science for Engineers
description: Focus on the interaction between society and the geologic environment. Locating, assessing and developing natural resources; understanding and preparing for natural hazards, design of structures and waste disposal sites. Corequisite: One of CIVL 215, MINE 200.

subject: EOSC
title: Computer Methods in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences
description: Mathematical computer-based problem solving in the physical, chemical, and biological sciences. Problems drawn from studies of the earth, the oceans and the atmosphere. Credit will be granted for only one of APSC 160 or EOSC 211. Prerequisite: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001.

subject: EOSC
title: Topics in the Earth and Planetary Sciences.
description: Cutting edge problems in earth, ocean, atmospheric and planetary sciences. Topics will be introduced through discussions of the current literature. Prerequisite: Second-year standing in science or engineering.

subject: EOSC
title: Computational Methods in Geological Engineering
description: Combining basic physical principles with their mathematical description and generating computational models that describe them. Introduction to basic building blocks in modelling, simulation and parameter estimation. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 253 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and one of APSC_V 160, CPSC_V 103, CPSC_V 110, EOSC_V 211.

subject: EOSC
title: Introductory Mineralogy
description: Introduction to crystallography, physical and chemical properties of minerals. Recognition and identification of common minerals. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: One of CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, CHEM_V 154, SCIE_V 001.

subject: EOSC
title: Introductory Petrology
description: Optical mineralogy and the classification and genesis of igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks. Prerequisite: [EOSC220]

subject: EOSC
title: Geological Time and Stratigraphy
description: Measuring geological time and understanding Earth history using stratigraphic principles, paleontology and radioactive decay. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: Second-year standing in Science. One of EOSC 1**, EOSC 210, GEOB 103 is recommended.

subject: EOSC
title: Field Techniques
description: Introduction to the techniques of geological mapping and the interpretation of field data. Includes three one-day field trips on weekends plus a seven-day field school after Spring examinations. A fee is to be paid by January 31. Corequisite: EOSC 221.

subject: EOSC
title: Site Investigation
description: Theory and practice of site investigation for geological engineers, including background studies, field work, remote sensing, development of ground models, importance of geological variability and uncertainty. Impacts on design, project risk and decision making. Prerequisite: EOSC 210. Corequisite: CIVL 210.

subject: EOSC
title: Fields and Fluxes
description: Application of classical theory of scalar and vector fields to geophysical sciences. Conductive, convective and radiative energy flux, gravitation, electrostatics, and magnetostatics. Gauss' and Stokes' theorems. Prerequisite: MATH_V 200 and one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 157. One of PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 158 is recommended.

subject: EOSC
title: Earthquakes
description: Characteristics, types, plate tectonics, faults, earth stresses and strains, seismic waves, magnitude scales, instrumentation, hazard mapping, prediction, and forecasting. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157; or (b) SCIE 001.

subject: EOSC
title: Marine Ecosystems
description: Introduction to diversity of marine habitats and ecosystems; hydrothermal vent, intertidal, coral reef, estuarine, deep sea, and polar ecosystems; impacts of ecosystem change; evolution of ocean plankton; invasive species; climate change; pollution. Prerequisite: One of SCIE 001, CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141, CHEM 154.

subject: EOSC
title: The Earth and the Solar System
description: The Earth as a planet: its composition, internal dynamics, and surface evolution. Rotation, magnetic field, plate tectonics, earthquakes, volcanoes. The ocean, atmosphere, and biosphere as components of a varying geo-environment. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( https://www.eoas.ubc.ca/undergrad/degrees ). No background in science or mathematics is required. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… Prerequisite: 2nd-year class standing or higher.

subject: EOSC
title: The Earth and its Resources
description: An introduction to the Earth with emphasis on its industrial and aesthetic resources. Rocks, minerals, gold, diamonds, sediments, fossils, oil and gas, canyons, and volcanoes and the processes that create them. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( https://www.eoas.ubc.ca/undergrad/degrees ). No background in science or mathematics is required. Prerequisite: Class standing 2.

subject: EOSC
title: The Ocean Environment
description: An introduction to the oceans and the processes that have shaped them, their composition and movement, waves, tides, beaches, interactions with the atmosphere and human exploitation of the non-living resources. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( https://www.eoas.ubc.ca/undergrad/degrees ). No background in science or mathematics is required. Prerequisite: Class standing 2.

subject: EOSC
title: The Ocean Ecosystem
description: An introduction to life in the oceans, its variety and evolution; primary producers and their links to the environment, zooplankton, marine communities, living marine resources and their role in today's world.
