Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( https://www.eoas.ubc.ca/undergrad/degrees ). No background in science or mathematics is required. Prerequisite: Class standing 2.

subject: EOSC
title: Sedimentology
description: Origin, diagenesis and geochemistry of sediments and sedimentary rocks. Prerequisite: EOSC 221 and one of EOSC 210, EOSC 222.

subject: EOSC
title: Igneous Petrology
description: The origin and formation of igneous rocks. Prerequisite: EOSC 221.

subject: EOSC
title: Metamorphic Petrology
description: Deciphering lithospheric processes as recorded by the mineralogy, chemistry and textures of metamorphosed rocks. Prerequisite: EOSC 221.

subject: EOSC
title: Structural Geology I
description: Analysis and interpretation of natural deformation. Prerequisite: All of EOSC 221, EOSC 223 and one of EOSC 210, EOSC 222.

subject: EOSC
title: Principles of Physical Hydrogeology
description: Theories of storage and movement of water within groundwater systems; Groundwater-surface water interaction; Role of groundwater systems in watershed management and regulating the environmental impacts of global change; Groundwater sustainability; Impacts of climate & land use changes on groundwater resources. . Prerequisite: (a) 3rd year standing in Science, Land and Food Systems, or Forestry and Environmental Stewardship; and (b) One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: Earth and Life Through Time
description: The fossil record of adaptation and extinction emphasizing the interaction of biological and geological processes. Not for credit in Geological Sciences and Geophysics specializations. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Second-year class standing or higher. Prerequisite: Biology 12 or BIOL_V 100-level.

subject: EOSC
title: Geochemical Thermodynamics
description: Application of chemical thermodynamics to problem solving in the earth sciences. Geochemical tools are developed for: low-T aqueous geochemistry, high-T, high-P processes in the lithosphere, ore-deposit formation, and for prediction of geochemical reaction rates in all environments. Prerequisite: EOSC220 Corequisite: CHEM 205.

subject: EOSC
title: Field Geology
description: Recording and processing geological data in the field. Held within the three weeks following April examinations after third year. A special fee is to be paid by January 31. Prerequisite: All of EOSC_V 323, EOSC_V 330 and one of EOSC_V 321, EOSC_V 322.

subject: EOSC
title: Quantitative Groundwater Hydrology
description: Introduction to theory of groundwater flow; flow nets; regional groundwater resource evaluation; well hydraulics; role of groundwater in geologic processes, case studies. Prerequisite: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001.

subject: EOSC
title: Principles of Geomorphology
description: Landform development; morphological and historical analysis of landforms; applications in engineering and resource development. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Prerequisite: One of GEOB 103, EOSC 110, EOSC 210.

subject: EOSC
title: Introduction to Mineral Deposits
description: Introduction to economic geology and models related to mineral exploration. Study includes typical deposit types and their plate tectonic setting. Prerequisite: EOSC 221.

subject: EOSC
title: Tectonic Evolution of North America
description: An overview of the geology and tectonic evolution of North America; comparisons and contrasts between Precambrian rocks of the North American craton and Phanerozoic belts of the Cordilleran, Appalachian, Ouachita and Innuitian orogens; interrelations between sedimentation, deformation, metamorphism and magmatism in a plate tectonic context. Prerequisite: [EOSC323] or permission of the instructor.

subject: EOSC
title: Elemental and Isotopic Geochemistry
description: Analytical methods in geochemistry, major and trace element geochemistry, radiogenic isotopes, geochemistry of seawater, the mantle, basalts, subduction zones, sedimentary rocks, continental crust. Prerequisite: EOSC 221.

subject: EOSC
title: Climate Change: Causes and Solutions
description: Mechanisms and processes of past and future global climate change. Climate models and projected impacts. Climate solutions including carbon sequestration, adaptation and geoengineering. Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, CHEM_V 154 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 and one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 157, PHYS_O 111.

subject: EOSC
title: Climate Change: Evidence and Impacts
description: Climate science fundamentals: Energy balance, ocean and atmospheric circulation. Future climate scenarios. Processes driving spatial and temporal climate variability. Analysis of observations and climate projection data to evaluate the anthropogenic impact on climate. Prerequisite: 3rd year class standing

subject: EOSC
title: Environmental, Geotechnical, and Exploration Geophysics I
description: Principles of geophysical survey design, data acquisition, processing and interpretation with emphasis on near-surface problems. Magnetic, seismic reflection/refraction, electromagnetic and ground penetrating radar surveys. Case history analysis of environmental and geotechnical problems. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 253 and third-year standing or higher in Science or Applied Science.

subject: EOSC
title: Geophysical Continuum Dynamics
description: Introduction to tensor calculus and continuum mechanics. Stress, strain and strain-rate tensors. Mass, momentum and energy balance. Applications to problems of geophysical heat transport, elasticity and fluid dynamics. Prerequisite: One of EOSC 250, MATH 317.

subject: EOSC
title: Seismology
description: Hooke's law for isotropic continua, elastic wave equation, reflection and refraction methods for imaging the Earth's internal structure, plane waves in an infinite medium and interaction with boundaries, body wave seismology, inversion of travel-time curves, generalized ray theory, crustal seismology, surface waves and earthquake source studies. Prerequisite: [EOSC352]

subject: EOSC
title: Analysis of Time Series and Inverse Theory for Earth Scientists
description: Continuous and discrete Fourier transforms, correlation and convolution, spectral estimates, optimum least-squares filters, deconvolution and prediction, frequency-wave number filtering. A practical course on computer techniques applied to the analysis of a wide range of geophysical phenomena. Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157.

subject: EOSC
title: The Planets
description: Diversity among the planets and moons of the solar system; integrating concepts across scientific disciplines, including geology, geophysics, and atmospheric science to understand how planets evolve. Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121; and one of CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141, CHEM 154 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157.

subject: EOSC
title: Introductory Oceanography: Circulation and Plankton
description: Physical and chemical processes and their controls on the distribution of plankton in the ocean. Prerequisite: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141, CHEM 154 and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157.

subject: EOSC
title: Introductory Oceanography: Climate and Ecosystems
description: Physical, chemical, and biological processes in the ocean and their interaction with climate and marine food-webs. Prerequisite: EOSC 372.

subject: EOSC
title: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in Winter Session (Term 1) in third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: Geoscientific Data Analysis and Empirical Modelling
description: Application of data analysis and empirical modelling strategies for conducting a data-oriented research in geosciences; from setting research questions and hypothesis to delivering and interpreting results. Examples are drawn from across the Earth, ocean, atmospheric and planetary sciences. Prerequisite: One of STAT_V 200, BIOL_V 300 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 200, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, EOSC_V 250 and one of EOSC_V 211, CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210.

subject: EOSC
title: Stable Isotopes in Earth, Ocean, and Environmental Sciences
description: Principles of stable isotope geochemistry applied to environmental systems, including instrumentation, data and sample analysis, and applications to (paleo) climate, oceanographic and environmental research. Prerequisite: 3rd-year class standing or higher and either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, CHEM_V 154 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105 or MATH_V 121.

subject: EOSC
title: Volcanology
description: Field and lab-based studies in volcanology concentrating on physical and chemical aspects of volcanic processes. Prerequisite: All of EOSC_V 220, EOSC_V 221.

subject: EOSC
title: Advanced Sedimentology
description: Description and interpretation of ancient and modern sediments, with emphasis on the origin, composition, textures, structures, diagenesis and chemistry of biogenic sediments. Prerequisite: [EOSC320] or permission of instructor.

subject: EOSC
title: Structural Geology II
description: Studies of natural deformation using advanced techniques. Prerequisite: [EOSC323]

subject: EOSC
title: Advanced Mineral Deposits
description: Advanced concepts in the processes that lead to the formation of mineral deposits. Introduction to the study of ore minerals using reflected light microscopy. Prerequisite: EOSC 331.

subject: EOSC
title: Paleontology
description: Paleobiogeography in the context of plate tectonics. Mass extinction events. Fossilization and biases in the fossil record. Species concepts in paleontology. Biostratigraphy. Paleontological evidence for early life; the colonization of oceanic and terrestrial environments and; the evolution of the primates. Prerequisite: EOSC 222.

subject: EOSC
title: Fundamentals of Geomicrobiology
description: Foundational knowledge of the interactions between microorganisms and Earth's surface chemistry. . Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 111, BIOL_V 112, BIOL_V 121, CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, EOSC_V 110, EOSC_V 112. Third year standing in Science. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: Field Techniques in Groundwater Hydrology
description: Hydraulic head measurements, water-quality sampling, pump and slug testing, infiltration measurements, profiling techniques. Held over five days after spring term at the Richmond groundwater hydrology field-school site. Enrolment limitations. Prerequisite: One of EOSC 325, EOSC 329.

subject: EOSC
title: Groundwater Contamination
description: Contaminant transport processes in groundwater flow systems; aqueous and multiphase transport; mathematical models describing migration and chemical evolution of contaminant plumes; case studies. Prerequisite: One of EOSC 325, EOSC 329.

subject: EOSC
title: Aqueous Geochemistry
description: Quantitative approaches to practical aqueous geochemistry problems. Equilibrium thermodynamics, kinetics, complexation, oxidation reduction, cation exchange, sorption and partitioning of organics. Case Studies. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001. Corequisite: One of EOSC 325, EOSC 329.

subject: EOSC
title: Groundwater Remediation
description: Methods for containment and remediation of subsurface contaminants; including groundwater control, groundwater extraction, and in situ treatment. Experience with common design approaches. Prerequisite: [EOSC429]

subject: EOSC
title: Fossil Fuels
description: Origin, geochemistry and distribution of petroleum and coal in the stratigraphic record. Sedimentation of organic matter, organic diagenesis, migration and accumulation of hydrocarbons. Principles of exploration and development. Techniques for measurement of organic maturation and source rock analyses. Corequisite: EOSC 320.

subject: EOSC
title: Geological Engineering Practice I - Rock Engineering
description: Application of rock mechanics, hydrogeology, and engineering design tools in realistically complex geological environments. Influence and treatment of geological uncertainty, and use of field data, geotechnical monitoring, and numerical analyses for tunnelling, mining and rock slope engineering projects. Case histories. Prerequisite: All of EOSC 329, CIVL 210, MINE 303.

subject: EOSC
title: Geological Engineering Practice II - Soil Engineering
description: Application of geomorphology, hydrogeology, and soil mechanics to geotechnical design. Influence and treatment of geological uncertainty in geotechnical hazard and risk assessments; multi-disciplinary approaches to geotechnical engineering problems in realistically complex geological environments. Case histories. Prerequisite: All of EOSC 329, EOSC 330, CIVL 210.

subject: EOSC
title: Physical Climate Modelling
description: Understanding climate models from 1D energy balance to fully coupled atmosphereocean general circulation models. Physics and thermodynamics of radiative balance and clouds. Spatial and temporal climate variability. Run simple climate models and analyze data from complex models. Prerequisites: 3rd year class standing, and one of EOSC 211, EOSC 213, CPSC 203, CPSC 210, and MATH 200, and one of EOSC 112, ATSC 201, EOSC 340, EOSC 345, GEOS 102,GEOG 312, PHYS 333.

subject: EOSC
title: Climate Measurement and Analysis
description: Local climate time series collection and analysis. Retrieval and analysis of online climate data and model output. Prerequisite: One of EOSC 340, EOSC 345 and one of CPSC 103, CPSC 110, EOSC 211, MATH 210, PHYS 210 and one of STAT 200, STAT 201, STAT 251, BIOL 300.

subject: EOSC
title: Engineering Design Project
description: Geological engineering design project from scope definition to final design. Based on a problem from industry. [2*-3-0, 2*-3-0] Prerequisite: All of EOSC 323, EOSC 330, CIVL 316. Corequisite: All of EOSC 433, CIVL 410.

subject: EOSC
title: Thesis
description: For B.A.Sc. Topic to be approved by the Department.

subject: EOSC
title: Directed Studies
description: Investigation of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of an undergraduate advisor and of the supervising faculty member is required before registration.

subject: EOSC
title: Thesis
description: Original research work under the direction of a faculty member. Required of all honours students. Open to major students with a satisfactory standing, appropriate background courses and permission of the course instructor and the directing faculty member.

subject: EOSC
title: Interior Structure of Earth and Planets
description: Theory, application and quantitative interpretation of potential field methods for use in exploring the interior structure of Earth and planets. Topics drawn from problems in geophysical exploration, geodesy, geodynamics, geomagnetism, planetary magnetic fields, heat flow and fluid flow. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 312, MATH 316, MATH 257 and one of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 158, SCIE 001.

subject: EOSC
title: Physics of the Earth and Other Planets
description: Identification and quantitative analysis of diverse physical problems in the earth, ocean, atmospheric, and planetary sciences. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 312, MATH_V 316, MATH_V 257.

subject: EOSC
title: Applied Geophysics
description: Using geophysics to characterize the Earth's subsurface for resource exploration, engineering, or environmental applications. Data acquisition, processing, and interpretation of geophysical surveys. Inversion examples drawn from potential (electrical, magnetic, gravity) or wave field (seismic, ground penetrating radar) surveys. Prerequisite: One of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, and one of EOSC_V 211, CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, and one of MATH_V 316, PHYS_V 312, EOSC_V 350, EOSC_V 352.

subject: EOSC
title: Biological Oceanography
description: A quantitative examination of processes regulating the abundance, distribution and production of phytoplankton, zooplankton, microbes and fish. Controls of primary and secondary production, ecosystem dynamics and foodwebs. Prerequisite: One of EOSC 372, EOSC 373.

subject: EOSC
title: Waves, Currents and Ocean Mixing
description: Use of observations, theory and model results to solve physical oceanographic problems including applications to transport and mixing of pollutants or nutrients. Prerequisite: EOSC 211 and one of ATSC 201, EOSC 372, GEOB 200 and one of SCIE 001, PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157.

subject: EOSC
title: Chemical Oceanography and Marine Geochemistry
description: Controls on chemical composition and elemental distributions in seawater and marine sediments (including nutrient elements, dissolved gases, the carbonate system, marine organic matter, and trace metals); solution chemistry of seawater; isotopic tracers of rates and dates in marine systems; geochemical balance in the oceans. Prerequisite: EOSC 373.

subject: EOSC
title: Methods in Oceanography
description: Methods of data acquisition, study and analysis required in solving oceanographic problems. Includes a field school held during the mid-term break. A fee is to be paid by January 31. Open to third- and fourth-year students in Oceanography, or with permission of the Department Head. Prerequisite: One of EOSC 372, EOSC 373.

subject: EOSC
title: Marine Pollution
description: An interdisciplinary study of pollution, with examples drawn from coastal and oceanic environments, including areas of local interest. Intended for third and fourth-year students with a background in the sciences. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in Science.

subject: EOSC
title: Marine Microbiology
description: Advanced biology, ecology and diversity of marine microbes. Emphasis on the roles of bacteria and viruses in marine foodwebs and geochemical cycles. Prerequisite: A minimum of 6 credits of third-year level life science courses.

subject: EOSC
title: Introduction to Fisheries Science
description: An introduction to the ecology and management of freshwater and marine fisheries. Topics include: population dynamics, species interactions, communities, environmental influences, stock assessment, economics and sociology of fisheries. Laboratories will consist of numerical analyses and simulations.

subject: EOSC
title: Student Directed Seminars in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies in earth, ocean and atmospheric sciences, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Prerequisite: Third-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university of government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: EOSC
title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNH
title: Integrated Physiology for Human Nutrition I
description: Basic principles in human physiology, including function of the nervous, endocrine, musculoskeletal and digestive systems, integration across systems, maintenance of homeostasis, and application to human nutrition. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 11, CHEM 12, CHEM 100, CHEM 110, CHEM 111 and one of BIOL 11, ATPH 12, BIOL 12, BIOL 111. FNH 160 and 161 together are credit-excluded with BIOL 153 and 155.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Integrated Physiology for Human Nutrition II
description: Basic principles in human physiology, including function of the cardiovascular, immune, respiratory, urinary and reproductive systems, integration across systems, maintenance of homeostasis, and application to human nutrition. Prerequisite: FNH 160. FNH 160 and 161 together are credit-excluded with BIOL 153 and 155.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Exploring Our Food
description: Chemical and physical properties of foods; issues pertaining to safety, nutritive value and consumer acceptability; government regulations pertaining to food safety, quality and additives; preservation techniques and transformation of agricultural commodities to food products; foods of the future. Prerequisite: At least second year standing required.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrition Concepts and Controversies
description: Fundamental concepts and principles of human nutrition applied to current nutrition issues. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of FNH 160, FNH 161 or (b) one of BIOL 111, BIOL 112, BIOL 153, BIOL 155 or (c) all of KIN 131, KIN 132. At least second-year standing required.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Introductory Topics in Food, Nutrition, and Health
description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in food, nutrition, and health. Topics will vary from year to year.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Engineering
description: Units and dimensions, mass balance, energy balance, steady state and transient heat flow, fluid handling and measurement. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Chemistry
description: Chemical and physical properties and reactions of food constituents, including water, carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, minerals and vitamins. Prerequisite: Either CHEM_V 203 or CHEM_V 233.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Analysis
description: Principles of and procedures for analysis of the chemical and physical properties of food; proximate analysis; introduction to instrumental analysis; reporting and analysis of data. Prerequisite: Either (a) CHEM_V 205, (b) CHEM_V 210, or (c) CHEM_V 211; and either (a) CHEM_V 203 or (b) CHEM_V 233.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Product Development
description: Introduction to and application of concepts involved in food product formulation and development. Prerequisite: One of LFS 252, BIOL 300, EPSE 482, FRST 231, STAT 200. FNH 301 recommended.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Processing
description: Preservation of tissue and fluid food systems by selected physical and chemical treatments with emphasis on product-process interactions. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100, PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Microbiology
description: Roles of microorganisms in food production, preservation, spoilage, and foodborne disease; factors affecting growth, survival and inactivation of microorganisms in foods; methods for identifying, enumerating, and eliminating microorganisms in food-production environments. Prerequisite: BIOL 112. third-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Science Laboratory I
description: Laboratory techniques used in food chemistry, microbiology and processing; statistical analysis and presentation of experimental data; scientific report writing. Enrolment restricted to Food Science students. Prerequisite: FNH 200. Corequisite: All of FNH 301, FNH 309, FNH 313.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Science Laboratory II
description: Laboratory techniques used in food analysis, food processing, sensory science and product development; statistical analysis and presentation of experimental data; scientific report writing. Enrolment restricted to Food Science students. Prerequisite: FNH 325. Corequisite: All of FNH 302, FNH 303.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Introduction to Wine Science I
description: Principles of viticulture, enology, and wine microbiology and chemistry; marketing, regulation and classification of wines from selected regions of the world; social, economic and health aspects of wine consumption; wine appreciation. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Introduction to Wine Science II
description: Review of diverse styles of wine with consideration of classic wine-producing areas. Concepts in wine microbiology/chemistry; overview of steps in grape processing for diverse wine styles. Comparison of regulations for Canadian VQA systems with international systems. Wine sensory analysis. Prerequisite: FNH 330. and third-year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Theory and Applications
description: Principles of food preparation based on the physical and chemical properties of food, and experimental and practical applications to food preparation. Prerequisite: FNH_V 200 and either (a) all of CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 113 or (b) all of CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 123. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Critical Perspectives on Consumer Food Practices
description: Personal, collective, and policy factors affecting food choices, including perceptions of healthy eating, gender, identity, family structures, and economic, sociocultural, and political forces. Prerequisite: At least third year standing required.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Counselling Skills in Dietetics
description: Counselling in dietetics: communication theory and foundational counselling skills. Prerequisite: FNH_V 370. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Fundamentals of Nutrition
description: Fundamentals of energy and macronutrient metabolism. Prerequisite: FNH_V 250 and one of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Vitamins, Minerals, and Health
description: Vitamin and mineral nutrition and their role in maintaining and promoting health. Prerequisite: FNH_V 250 and one of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: International Nutrition
description: Conceptualization and scientific analyses of global problems in food and nutrition; complexities of food habits and malnutrition in various cultures around the world.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrition Assessment
description: The use of dietary, anthropometric, biochemical, and related information for the assessment of nutritional status of individuals and populations. Prerequisite: FNH 250.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Human Nutrition Over The Life Span
description: Nutritional requirements and dietary patterns of healthy individuals throughout the life span. Prerequisite: FNH 250.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrition Care I
description: Fundamentals of nutrition care: the nutrition care process (NCP), documentation, nutritional risk and nutritional status assessment, metabolic stress, supplements, pharmacology, and body weight. NCP applied to food allergies and intolerances, gastrointestinal symptoms. Introduction to chronic diseases. Restricted to students in year 3 of the dietetics major. Prerequisite: All of FNH_V 350, FNH_V 370 and either (a) one of BIOL_V 153, BIOL_V 155, CAPS_V 301 or (b) all of FNH_V 160 and FNH_V 161. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Professional Dietetic Practice I
description: Introduction to the profession of dietetics in Canada. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Dietetics Major. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement I
description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Prerequisite: All of FNH_V 375, FNH_V 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Research Methods in Human Nutrition
description: Process of research; principles and processes in utilizing research. Restricted to students in majors in the FNH program. Prerequisite: FNH 250 and either (a) LFS 252 or (b) BIOL 300 or (c) EPSE 482 or (d) FRST 231 or (e) STAT 200.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Advances in Plant and Cell-Based Foods
description: Examination of meat, egg, fish, and dairy analogues made using plants, recombinant proteins, and cell cultures, from the molecular to the macroscopic level. Relation of molecular details to physical and sensory properties. Health and sustainability impacts. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203, CHEM_V 203 or CHEM_V 233. 3rd-year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Functional Foods
description: Functional food concepts related to efficacy and safety; examples of bioactive component-disease relationships; natural health products; approval of functional food and health claims; the importance of clinical studies in support of efficacy for health claims; market determinants of functional foods. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203, and third-year standing. Equivalency: PHAR_V 431
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Laws, Regulations and Quality Assurance
description: Canadian and international laws governing food composition, grading, quality and safety; hazard analysis critical control points; statistical quality assurance. Prerequisite: One of LFS_V 252, STAT_V 200, FRST_V 231, BIOL_V 300, EPSE_V 482, or equivalent background in statistics.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Safety and Quality Management
description: Food production plant sanitation, environmental monitoring, global food safety standards, and food plant internal audits. Prerequisite: FNH 403.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Microbiology of Food and Beverage Fermentation
description: Fermentation methods, mechanism and microbiology of nonalcoholic fermented foods and alcoholic fermented beverages (beer, cider, sake). Prerequisite: One of MICB_V 211, MICB_V 212, BIOL_V 201, BIOL_V 203, BIOC_V 202, BIOC_V 203. Third-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Safety
description: Microbial and chemical factors that underlie public health challenges in the food supply chain; prevalence and nature of organisms which cause foodborne diseases; approaches and technologies for improvement of food safety. Prerequisite: One of MICB_V 211, MICB_V 212, CHEM_V 233, FNH_V 313.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Sustainability in the Food Industry
description: Regenerative sustainability and the sustainability nexus; health and environmental impacts of the food industry; environmental performance indicators and management systems; approaches to enhance sustainability in the food industry. Prerequisite: One of FNH 309, FNH 313.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Business Concepts in Food, Nutrition, and Health
description: Introduction to and application of business activities in food, nutrition, and health settings. Credit will only be granted for only one of FNH 415, FOOD 515, or FRE 515. Prerequisite: At least third-year standing in the Faculty of Land and Food Systems.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Interfacial Phenomena
description: Outline of the physics and chemistry of interfaces; discussion of the part played by surface effects in technical processes. Credit will be granted for only one of FNH 419 and FOOD 519. Prerequisite: FNH 300. or equivalent. Equivalency: CHBE 487
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Science Laboratory III
description: Integrated course designed to illustrate principles of research and product development in the food industry. Prerequisite: All of FNH 325, FNH 326.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Enology and Wine Biotechnology
description: Yeasts and bacteria involved in wine making, metabolic pathways leading to the production of flavour and spoilage compounds, genetic improvement of wine yeasts, and red and white wine fermentations. Approaches and technologies for the improvement of wine safety. Sensory evaluation of wines. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 335, MICB 325, FNH 313, BIOC 302.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Integrated Functional Genomics
description: Global transcript, protein and metabolite profiling technologies, their integration, application, and furtherance of our understanding of how higher organisms function in general. Prerequisite: BIOL 335. Equivalency: BIOL436
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Food Service Systems Management
description: Management responsibilities in quantity food production with emphasis on menu planning, purchasing and service. Includes planning and equipping food services. Restricted to students in the Dietetics major. Note: Course registrants are required to possess a Foodsafe II certificate. Prerequisite: FNH_V 340. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrient Metabolism and Implications for Health
description: Integration of nutrient and energy metabolism on a whole-body and individual tissue basis and the implication for health. Emphasis will be on regulation of nutrient metabolism. Prerequisite: FNH_V 350, one of BIOC_V 302 or BIOC_V 303, and either (a) one of BIOL_V 153, BIOL_V 155, CAPS_V 301 or (b) all of FNH_V 160 and FNH_V 161.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Fish Nutrition
description: Physiology of digestion and excretion, nutrient requirements, sources of nutrients, diet formulation, feeding management. Prerequisite: [FNH 350]
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Applied International Nutrition
description: Applying nutrition concepts and principles in addressing problems of malnutrition and food insecurity in international settings. Basics of developing culturally acceptable, sustainable nutrition intervention programs. Prerequisite: FNH_V 355. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrition Care II
description: Enteral nutrition, parenteral nutrition, and the nutrition care process are applied to select diseases or conditions, including trauma, surgery, critical care, respiratory diseases, gastrointestinal diseases, liver diseases, and diseases of the gallbladder and exocrine pancreas. Restricted to students in year 4 of the dietetics major. Prerequisite: All of FNH_V 371, FNH_V 375. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Maternal and Fetal Nutrition
description: Metabolic adaptations, nutrient metabolism, and special issues during pregnancy that may influence the maternal-fetal nutritional supply. Corequisite: FNH 350. Third-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Applied Public Health Nutrition
description: Theory and methods in public health nutrition and health promotion program planning to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate nutrition-related programs for communities and populations. Considers factors affecting behavior and the social determinants of health. Prerequisite: FNH 250 and fourth-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Sport Nutrition
description: Nutritional needs of athletes, including energy, carbohydrate and protein; hydration; pre-and post-event nutrition, weight management and body composition issues; ergogenic aids; sports-specific guidelines; and special athlete populations. Prerequisite: All of FNH 350, FNH 351.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrition Care III
description: Nutrition care process applied to select diseases and conditions including dysphagia, cancer, neurological conditions, metabolic syndrome, eating disorders, cardiovascular diseases, endocrine diseases, and renal diseases. Restricted to students in year 4 of the dietetics major. Prerequisite: All of BIOC_V 302, FNH_V 470. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
description: Evidence-based examination of the role of nutrition in the prevention of chronic disease. Prerequisite: FNH 398.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Professional Dietetic Practice II
description: Skill development and application for practice education placements and dietetic practice settings. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Prerequisite: All of FNH_V 380, FNH_V 381. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement II
description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: All of FNH_V 380, FNH_V 381, FNH_V 480. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement III
description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: FNH_V 481. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Dietetics Practice Education Placement IV
description: Practice education placements in settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Dietetics Major. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: FNH_V 482. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Advanced Topics in Food, Nutrition, and Health
description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in food, nutrition and health. Prerequisite: 3rd year standing or higher.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Directed Studies in Food, Nutrition and Health
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNH
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Design and execution of an experimental/analytical research project leading to preparation of a thesis. Prerequisite: Approval of a program advisor; consult before the end of classes in third year.
faculty_school: Faculty of Land and Food Systems

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Foundations
description: The historical, cultural, political, economic and legal issues that inform the experiences of Indigenous peoples in Canada, examined from both Indigenous and non-Indigenous perspectives. Credit will be granted for only one of FNIS 100, FNSP 100, or FNSP 200. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Politics and Self-Determination
description: The cultural, historical, political, economic, and gender dynamics that structure the relationship between Indigenous peoples and the state in Canada; Indigenous self-determination struggles in relation to constitutional recognition, self-government, land claims, and economic development. Credit will be granted for only one of FNSP 200, FNIS 210, or FNSP 210. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Recommended pre-requisite: FNIS 100.

subject: FNIS
title: Representation and Indigenous Cultural Politics
description: Representation, identity, and cultural politics through Indigenous literature, film, and the visual arts; the relationship between these sites of cultural production and the self-determination struggles of Indigenous peoples. Credit will be granted for only one of FNSP 200, FNIS 220, or FNSP 220. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Recommended pre-requisite: FNIS 100

subject: FNIS
title: Applied Learning: Collaborative Place-Based Research
description: Topic and community/location of instruction will vary from year to year. Applied, intense delivery experiential learning course designed and implemented in collaboration with faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). Examines the importance of Indigenous place-based research and learning for student and community empowerment. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: Permission of the Instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Writing First Nations
description: writing-intensive course examining approaches to writing Indigenous research: Representation & the Other; Indigenous critiques of research & representation; Indigenous, feminist and cultural studies approaches to writing ethnography, oral history, and related research methods. Credit will be granted for only one of FNIS_V 300 or FNSP_V 300. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of FNIS_V 210, FNIS_V 220 or (b) one of FNSP_V 210, FNSP_V 220. Equivalency: FNSP_V 300. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Critical Indigenous Theory Seminar
description: Adapting and integrating current conceptual paradigms in the humanities, social sciences, performing arts, and Indigenous studies into approaches in First Nations/Indigenous Studies, including identity construction, political and cultural self-determination, representation, essentialism/authenticity, ethics, and decolonization. Credit will be granted for only one of FNIS_V 310 or FNSP_V 310. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: Either (a) FNSP_V 200 or (b) all of FNIS_V 210, FNIS_V 220 or (c) all of FNSP_V 210, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Critical Indigenous Methodologies and Ethics
description: Responsible and community-based research from a critical Indigenous perspective; methods for identifying and assessing research materials, critical analysis, oral history/qualitative research interviewing and analysis, and research ethics in the design and implementation of community-based student research projects. Credit will be granted for only one of FNIS_V 320 or FNSP_V 320. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: Either (a) FNIS_V 310 or (b) FNSP_V 310. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Applied Learning: Collaborative Place-Based Research
description: Topic and community/location of instruction will vary from year to year. Applied, intense delivery experiential learning course designed and implemented in collaboration with faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). Examines the importance of Indigenous place-based research and learning for student and community empowerment. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. And Permission of the Instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Practicum/Advanced Research Seminar
description: Applied research/community oriented project designed and implemented in collaboration with student, faculty and Aboriginal community organization. Emphasis on examining ethical issues and developing culturally respectful and academically rigorous forms of research. Credit will be granted for only one of FNIS_V 400 or FNSP_V 400. Restricted to Majors in First Nations and Indigenous Studies. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of FNIS_V 310, FNIS_V 320 or (b) all of FNSP_V 310, FNSP_V 320. Students must pass FNIS_V 320 or FNSP_V 320 with a B- or higher or request program approval. Equivalency: FNSP_V 400. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Special Topics
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website: http://fnsp.arts.ubc.ca . Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS 100, FNSP 200, FNIS 210, FNSP 210, FNIS 220, FNSP 220.

subject: FNIS
title: Directed Study
description: Restricted to Undergraduate Students.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Feminisms
description: The historical, cultural, political, and activist roots of contemporary Indigenous feminisms. Indigenous feminist methodologies, theory, and praxis in relation to contemporary Indigenous politics and social justice movements. Credit will be granted for only one of FNSP_V 401D, FNIS_V 451, or FNSP_V 451. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Social Movements
description: Draws on Indigenous and non-Indigenous intellectual traditions to explore the theoretical, cultural, political, economic, and historical bases of Indigenous peoples decolonization struggles in Canada. Credit will be granted for only one of FNSP_V 401A, FNIS_V 452, or FNSP_V 452. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Legal Traditions
description: Socio-historical, political and cultural context of Indigenous legal traditions and strategies for ethical engagement within state and Indigenous polities. Methods include oral history analysis, legal theory, literary/narrative studies, and philosophy from an Indigenous studies perspective. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous New Media
description: New media and digital storytelling works designed and implemented by Indigenous artists, authors, and programmers. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Geographies: Our Home on Native Land
description: Indigenous people's place-based relations, colonial processes of de-territorialization, and spatial negotiations of settler colonialism. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FNIS
title: Indigenous Two-Spirit and Queer Studies
description: Cultural contexts, scholarship, literature, and artistic expressions of Queer, LGBTI, and Two-Spirited Indigenous people, both as an academic area of study and as lived experience and relationship. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Prerequisite: One of FNIS_V 100, FNIS_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 200, FNSP_V 210, FNSP_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: FRST
title: Sustainable Forests
description: An overview of forests and forestry. Survey of the disciplines, areas of study, and values that frame sustainable management of forests in BC and the world. Assignments focus on critical thinking and written communication skills.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Principles of Microeconomics for Forestry and Land and Food Systems
description: Principles of microeconomics and their applications in forestry and land and food systems. The basic concept of the economy to focus on private and social decision making related to the use of land, especially in agriculture, forestry, and conservation. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST 101, ECON 101, or LFS 101. Equivalency: LFS101, ECON101
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Introduction to Forestry Co-op
description: An introduction to Forestry Co-op including: completion of preemployment workshops, career skills toolkits, networking opportunities, interview training, individual coaching sessions, and job search skills. Restricted to students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship Co-operative Education Program. Pass/fail. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Land One: First-year Integrative Seminar
description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both First Nations and Western perspectives. Equivalency: LFS_V 110, NRES_V 110. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Forestry
description: Communicating concepts of forestry and links to human and environmental activities through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES_V 150, FRST_V 150, or LFS_V 150. Equivalency: LFS_V 150, NRES_V 150. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Plant Biology I
description: The structure, diversity and development of trees and other plants, with emphasis on the angiosperms. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 200 or FRST 200. Prerequisite: BIOL 121. Equivalency: NRES 200
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Ecology
description: The structure and function of forest ecosystems, including: energetics; productivity; nutrient, carbon and water cycling; soils; the physical environment; population and community ecology; disturbance ecology; ecological succession; biological diversity and ecological resilience. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 201 or FRST 201. Equivalency: NRES 201
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Ecology
description: The Ecosystem concept; energy biomass and nutrient cycling; the physical environment; population and community ecology; succession, Biogeoclimatic classification and some coastal ecosystems. Available only through Distance Education.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Silvics of Forest Trees of Western Canada
description: Ecological and silvical characteristics of forest trees; assessment of ecological site quality and biogeoclimatic classification; application of silvics in silviculture. A plant herbarium of at least 50 species is required. Only available through Distance Education. Prerequisite: FRST202
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Plant Biology II
description: The functional biology of trees and other forest plants in their environment, with an emphasis on gymnosperms. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 210 or FRST 210. Prerequisite: One of FRST 200, NRES 200. Equivalency: NRES 210.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Classification and Silvics
description: Forest classification and the application of silvics in forest management, including world forest classification systems, the Biogeoclimactic Ecosystem Classification system, and ecosystem diagnosis in the field. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 211 or FRST 211. Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201. Equivalency: NRES 211
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Introduction to Biometrics
description: Basic theories of probability and statistics. Sampling distribution, methods of estimation and hypothesis testing; goodness of fit and tests for independence; analysis of variance, regression and correlation. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 231 or FRST 231. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 180, MATH 184, MATH 190. Equivalency: NRES 231
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Computer Applications in Forestry
description: Techniques involved in solving forestry problems with microcomputers using word processing, spreadsheet, procedural language, and database management tools. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 232 or FRST 232. Equivalency: NRES 232
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Tree and Stand Level Measurements
description: An introduction to measurement of individual trees and stands; use of aerial photographs, maps, and various measurement instruments. Prerequisite: One of FRST 231, NRES 231 and one of FRST 232, NRES 232.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement.
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Orientation workshops required. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Genetics
description: Population genetics and conservation of genetic resources; principles of genetics and their application to forestry.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Into the Woods: An Introduction to Forest Science
description: Introduction to growth of trees and forests with emphasis on evolutionary, ecological and environmental aspects. Not available for credit to undergraduate students in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Stewardship in a Changing Climate
description: Forests can provide natural solutions to climate change and social well-being through innovative management and restoration including protection of mother trees and soils, carbon and conservation financing, and emergence of value-added industries. For students without strong science backgrounds. Not available for credit to Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship students.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Silviculture
description: Silviculture concepts and principles; stand dynamics; artificial and natural regeneration; cultural techniques for forest stand establishment and stand tending; silvicultural systems; decision making and development of prescriptions; connections to forest planning. Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201 and one of FRST 350, FRST 351, UFOR 400.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Biotic Disturbances
description: Concepts of disturbance ecology with special reference to insects and diseases in the forests of British Columbia; forest health problems in the biogeoclImatic zones of BC; present management strategies and future potentials in a scenario of climate change. Prerequisite: One of FRST 210, NRES 210 and one of FRST 211, NRES 211.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Entomology
description: An introduction to insects that cause damage to forests and forest products; how insects live; life cycles and attack symptoms of representatives of major groups of insects; principles for control and management. Available only through Distance Education.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Pathology
description: Biology and management of forest tree diseases. Available only through Distance Education.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Soil Biology
description: The diversity and interactions of soil organisms (bacteria, protozoa, fungi, animals, plants) in natural and managed ecosystems; roles in primary production, nutrient cycling, decomposition and reclamation; responses to environmental change. Prerequisite: BIOL 121. Equivalency: APBI342
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Plant Physiology I
description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants. CHEM 203, CHEM 213, or CHEM 233 and CHEM 235 is recommended. Equivalency: BIOL351, APBI351
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest and Conservation Economics
description: Practical problem solving of economic issues related to forestry and conservation, touching on investment analysis, capital budgeting, non-timber economics, ecosystem services, and forest certification. Completion of FRST_V 232 or NRES_V 232 or intermediate knowledge of MS Excel essential. Prerequisite: One of ECON_V 101, FRST_V 101, ECON_O 101.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Principles of Forestry Economics
description: Introduction to the economics of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services produced by, and dependent on, the forest resource. Available only through Distance Education.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Abiotic Disturbances: Fire and Climate
description: Ecological effects of fire and climatic (wind, temperature, and snow) disturbances; fire danger rating, principles of fire management and prescribed fire use; windthrow risk modelling and management. Prerequisite: One of FRST 210, NRES 210 and one of FRST 211, NRES 211.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Level Measurement and Productivity
description: Obtaining and forecasting information for stands and forests. Prerequisite: FRST 239.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement.
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement.
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Foundational Field School
description: Field study concentrating on outdoor skills, forest measurements, site diagnosis, and an integrated overview of the ecological, social and economic basis for forest management. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST_V 350 or 351. Prerequisite: FRST_V 211 or NRES_V 211; FRST_V 201 or NRES_V 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Interior Field School
description: Field study at an interior BC location concentrating on land use, management and silviculture. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Students with FRST_V 351 and FRST_V 350 can only count 3 credits toward their program requirements. Prerequisite: FRST_V 210 or NRES_V 210. Corequisite: FRST_V 211 or NRES_V 211.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Community Forests and Community Forestry
description: Community forests and community forestry throughout the world, with special attention to participation by aboriginal peoples; emphasis is on forms of governance, public participation, and adaptive learning.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Watershed Hydrology
description: Measurement and analysis of hydrological processes in response to forest management activities. Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Aquatic Ecosystems and Fish in Forested Watersheds
description: Effects of forest management activities on fish and aquatic ecosystems. Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing in Forestry, Science, Applied Science or Applied Biology.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
description: Ecology, management, and conservation of terrestrial vertebrate wildlife, focusing primarily on socio-economically important, forest-dwelling species of mammals, birds, amphibians and reptiles. Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, BIOL 230, BIOL 306.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Introduction to Research Methods
description: Lectures and seminars in research philosophies and the scientific method, with special emphasis on field research. Prerequisite: One of FRST 150, LFS 150, NRES 150, WRDS 150, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, WOOD 225, NRES 225.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Living Language: Science and Society
description: Multi-disciplinary course in which students, individually and in groups, examine, integrate and apply subject-specific knowledge through the lens of language and the framework of the language sciences, with a focus on themes of real-world importance. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor. Equivalency: APSC402, ASTU402, LFS 402, LLED402, PHAR402
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: The Sustainability of Production in Managed Forest Ecosystems
description: Study of the functional and dynamic characteristics of forest ecosystems and their response to forest management using ecosystem-level microcomputer simulation models. Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Advances in Silviculture
description: Fundamental silvicultural problems; the application of research findings to the practice of silviculture. Prerequisite: FRST 305.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Advanced Forest Pathology
description: Hereditary, physiological, anatomical, environmental, and microbiological factors influencing forest tree diseases. Given in alternate years.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Advanced Forest Insect Ecology
description: Role of climate and climate change in the population dynamics, outbreak potentials and resultant impacts to forest ecosystems associated with herbivorous forest insects. Prerequisite: One of FRST 307, APBI 327, BIOL 327.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Introduction to Landscape Ecology and Management
description: Current concepts, methods, and applications of landscape ecology with emphasis on spatial patterning, spatial heterogeneity, and dynamics; problem-solving approaches to natural resource issues through the application of landscape ecological principles and tools. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Complex Adaptive Systems, Global Change Science, and Ecology Sustainability
description: Concepts of complex adaptive systems (CAS); exploration of how CAS can be used to manage natural and social environments for multiple goals under changing climatic and socio-economic conditions. Prerequisite: Third-year standing
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Ecological Plant Biochemistry.
description: The structure, biosynthesis, distribution and biological function of secondary plant metabolites. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 201 and one of BIOL 209, BIOL 210; or (b) one of FRST 200, NRES 200 and one of FRST 210, NRES 210. Equivalency: BIOL462
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Sustainable Forest Policy
description: The development, implementation, and analysis of forest policy. Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Quantitative Forest Management
description: Introduction to the quantitative tools necessary in forest management. Available only through Distance Education.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Mathematical Modelling in Forest Resource Analysis
description: Modelling techniques used in strategic and tactical forest resources analyses. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in the BSF degree.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Management Planning
description: Forest management designs to identify and integrate economic, social, and environmental objectives across a forested landscape both strategically and tactically. Prerequisite: FRST 422.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Planning
description: Analyze and interpret existing management plans, prescribe solutions for achieving specific forest management goals at multiple scales, use basic tools to evaluate the financial implications of such solutions, and create a forest management plan for a virtual forest. Offered entirely online. Students in any of the Forestry programs requiring FRST 423 (6 cr) in order to graduate will not be granted the 3 cr of FRST 425 toward degree completion.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Advanced Biometrics
description: Analysis of variance, multiple regression and analysis of covariance. Design and analysis of experiments. Prerequisite: One of FRST 231, NRES 231, BIOL 300, STAT 200. And FRST 399 or equivalent. Restricted to students with 4th year standing or by permission of instructor.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Ecological Genomics
description: The genomic basis of adaptation to environments. Topics progress through community structure, life history patterns, stress responses, and variation and adaptation.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Growth and Yield
description: Techniques of growth and yield projection and discussion of modelling approaches. Exploration of stand dynamics, quantitative implications of management treatments and environmental limitations to tree and stand growth. Prerequisite: FRST339
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: International Forestry
description: The socio-economic, biological and technological aspects of forestry within the international frame, in both the developed and developing world. Regional studies and the role of national and international agencies.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Remote Sensing for Ecosystem Management
description: Basic biological concepts related to interpretation of remote sensing data for land management, including the use of films and filters, and interpretation of air photographs, and other imagery.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Agroforestry
description: Ecological, economic and social benefits of incorporating trees into agricultural landscapes. Lectures and groupwork designing agroforestry systems in temperate and tropical contexts. Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201, APBI 260. Equivalency: APBI444
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement.
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement.
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Co-operative Work Placement.
description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Directed Studies in Forestry
description: In special cases and with the approval of the instructor concerned, a student may carry on directed studies of specific problems in forestry.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Coastal Field School
description: Site diagnosis and preparation of management options in coastal forests. Extrasessional course; fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Prerequisite: FRST_V 350 or 351; FRST_V 305; Third- or fourth-year standing in the B.S.F. program, or Forest Management major or Forest Operations major in B.Sc. in Natural Resources program.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: The Role of Natural and Planted Forests in the Global Bioeconomy
description: (Go Global Seminar Series) An intensive one-month field school in Chile focused on fast-growing industrial forest plantations, innovative wood products, land use strategies for natural and planted forests, and their impact on society. Prerequisite: Third-year standing
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forests and Society
description: Social aspects of forestry and forest communities. Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Indigenous Ecologies
description: Application of Indigenous worldviews and knowledges to ecology. Colonial history of modern ecology, foundations and examples of Indigenous ecologies, restoration applying multiple worldviews, and Indigenized, culturally appropriate ecological research and decision-making processes. Prerequisite: One of BEST_V 203, BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201, APBI_V 260, GEOS_V 207. And third-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Forest Watershed Management
description: Effects of land management on quality, quantity and timing of water flow. Prerequisite: FRST385
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Visual Resource Management and Planning for Aesthetics
description: Methodologies for visual analysis, perceptions, planning & management of urban, natural and working landscapes, and implications for sustainable land-use management & community engagement. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST 490 or FRST 551. Prerequisite: Third-year standing. Equivalency: LARC542
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Visualization and Forest Design
description: GIS-based spatial planning and 3D landscape visualization for forest management. Prerequisite: Third- or fourth-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Environmental Perception
description: How individuals perceive their environment. Emphasis will be given visual perception in the context of natural resource issues and the effects of those perceptions on individuals including issues of human wellbeing. Prerequisite: Third-year standing
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Biological Diversity and Conservation
description: Principles, problems, and practices of managing natural habitats for biological diversity; current issues in biological diversity important to researchers, policymakers, and the general public. . Prerequisite: One of FRST_V 201, NRES_V 201 and FRST_V 395. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: Communications and Professionalism
description: Preparing professional reports and presentations; professionalism and professional ethics. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: B.Sc. Thesis in Forestry
description: An independent study or research project of a subject of special interest to the student under the direction of a staff member. Available only to students in the BSFS Honours specialization.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: FRST
title: B.S.F. Thesis
description: An independent study or research project on an approved topic, developed under the guidance of a Faculty member. Available only to students in their graduating year.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: GEOS
title: Our Changing Environment: Climate and Ecosystems
description: Energy and water in the Earth-Atmosphere system, global climates and climate change, ecosystem properties and processes, human impacts. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 102 or GEOS_V 102. Equivalency: GEOB_V 102.

subject: GEOS
title: Our Changing Environment: Water and Landscapes
description: Physical processes acting at the Earth's surface; water cycle; landforms; human impacts. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/facult… . Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 103 or GEOS_V 103. Equivalency: GEOB_V 103.

subject: GEOS
title: Introduction to Atmospheric Environments
description: Physical principles underlying weather and climates. Thermal, moisture and wind climates from the scale of plants and animals to the globe. Daily weather systems and climate change. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOS_V (or GEOB_V) 200, GEOS_V (or GEOB_V) 204, or APBI_V 244. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOS_V 102, GEOB_V 102, or second-year standing in science. Equivalency: APBI_V 244 and GEOB_V 200.

subject: GEOS
title: Introduction to Biometeorology
description: Basic principles and processes of climatology. Energy and water balance concepts. Weather systems and climate change, microclimate of soils, crops, forests, and animals. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOS_V (or GEOB_V) 200, GEOS_V (or GEOB_V) 204, or APBI_V 244. Equivalency: GEOB_V 204.

subject: GEOS
title: Landscapes: Introduction to Geomorphology
