description: Earth surface processes shaping the landscape; identification of hazards and hazardous areas associated with these processes; introduction to techniques for measurement and analysis at various spatial and time scales; field trips are required. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB_V 103, GEOS_V 103, EOSC_V 110, PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 157, SCIE_V 001. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 206 or GEOS_V 206. Equivalency: GEOB_V 206

subject: GEOS
title: Introduction to Biodiversity
description: Geographical ecology emphasizing contemporary species distributions at local to global spatial scales, population and community dynamics, and human impacts. Labs emphasize collecting data (sometimes outdoors) and interpreting results. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB_V 102, GEOS_V 102. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 207 or GEOS_V 207. Equivalency: GEOB_V 207

subject: GEOS
title: Geographic Information Science
description: Computer-based graphical methods of data input and analysis. Emphasis on data visualization techniques such as cartographic modelling and exploratory data analysis. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 270 or GEOS_V 270. Equivalency: GEOB_V 270.

subject: GEOS
title: Microscale Weather and Climate
description: Meteorology and climatology at the micro-, local, and meso-scales. Interactions between land surfaces and atmosphere. Basics of atmospheric turbulence and transfer processes. Microclimates on scales of a leaf to those of a large valley. Recommended prerequisites: one of GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, GEOB_V 204, GEOS_V 204, ATSC_V 201. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 300 or GEOS_V 300. Equivalency: GEOB_V 300.

subject: GEOS
title: Tropical Ecosystems in a Changing World
description: Biogeography and ecology of tropical systems, including patterns of species diversity, forest dynamics, plant-animal interactions, carbon and nutrient cycling. Impacts of global environmental change and conservation strategies for tropical ecosystems. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB_V 207, GEOS_V 207, GEOS_V 307, BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 303 or GEOS_V 303. Equivalency: GEOB_V 303.

subject: GEOS
title: Synoptic Meteorology and Climatology
description: Analysis of meteorological fields, diagnostic analysis of synoptic weather systems, applications of synoptic meteorology. Requires participation in weekly weather map discussion. Recommended prerequisites: one of GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, ATSC_V 201. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 304 or GEOS_V 304. Equivalency: GEOB_V 304.

subject: GEOS
title: Introduction to Hydrology
description: Principles of hydrology at site, watershed, and larger regional scales. Introduction to techniques of measurement and analysis. Emphasizes surface water hydrology of western North America. Recommended prerequisites: one of GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, GEOB_V 204, GEOS_V 204, APBI_V 244, ATSC_V 201, and one of PHYS_V 100-level or CHEM_V 123. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 305 or GEOS_V 305. Equivalency: GEOB_V 305.

subject: GEOS
title: Paleoecology: Lessons from Ancient Earth
description: Paleoecology of terrestrial ecosystems, particularly during the Quaternary, application of historical context to inform contemporary policy and management dilemmas, and including a foundation in relevant ecosystem and ecological concepts. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB_V 102, GEOS_V 102, GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, GEOB_V 204, GEOS_V 204, GEOB_V 207, GEOS_V 207, GEOS_V 307, GEOG_V 211, BIOL_V 230 or EOSC_V 340.

subject: GEOS
title: Biogeography and Global Change
description: Biogeographic concepts in understanding responses in ecosystems to environmental change at global, regional, and local scales. Conservation issues such as the loss of biodiversity and endangered species. This course is recommended for students who have credit in one of BIOL_V 121, BIOL_V 230, GEOS_V 102, GEOB_V 207, GEOS_V 207, FRST_V 201. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 307 or GEOS_V 307. Equivalency: GEOB_V 307.

subject: GEOS
title: Earth's Recent Past: Climate Change, Glaciers and Landforms
description: Quaternary landscape development emphasizing the history of glaciation with special reference to western North America; applications of geomorphology in resource development and land management; interpretation of Quaternary materials. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of EOSC_V 320, EOSC_V 330, GEOB_V 206, GEOS_V 206. Credit will only be granted for one of GEOB_V 308 or GEOS_V 308. Equivalency: GEOB_V 308.

subject: GEOS
title: Geographical Sciences Field Course
description: Field sampling, instrumentation, surveying, mapping techniques, and data analysis; mandatory multi-day field camp in May or June. Special fees and liability insurance are required. This course is recommended for students who have credit in GEOS_V 206, and one of BIOL_V 230, GEOB_V 207, GEOS_V 207, GEOS_V 307, and one of GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, GEOB_V 204, GEOS_V 204. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 309 or GEOS_V 309. Equivalency: GEOB_V 309. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: GEOS
title: Advanced Geographic Information Science
description: Theoretical and practical aspects of Geographic Information Systems, including cartographic modelling, digital terrain models, management issues, and spatial interpolation. Recommended prerequisites: Third-year standing in ENSC, GEOG, ENST, URST, or GEOS (or GEOB) specializations, with some introductory knowledge of GIS. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 370 or GEOS_V 370. Equivalency: GEOB_V 370.

subject: GEOS
title: Cartography
description: Cartographic methods: development of cartography; projections; data ordering, compilation and symbolization; cartographic design, map reproduction. Recommended prerequisites: one of GEOB_V 102, GEOS_V 102, GEOB_V 103, GEOS_V 103. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 372 or GEOS_V 372. Equivalency: GEOB_V 372.

subject: GEOS
title: Remote Sensing: Monitoring Earth's Surface from Afar
description: Aerial photography; measurement from aerial photographs; photo-interpretation in geographic analysis; remote sensing of the earth's surface and atmosphere. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB_V 270, GEOS_V 270, or third-year standing in ENSC or GEOS (or GEOB) specializations. Credit will only be granted for one of GEOB_V 373 or GEOS_V 373. Equivalency: GEOB_V 373.

subject: GEOS
title: Global Change Science
description: Processes controlling the planetary cycles of elements like carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus, the human perturbation of these biogeochemical cycles, and the consequences for the atmosphere, terrestrial ecosystems, and aquatic ecosystems. Recommended prerequisites: either (a) SCIE_V 001 or b) BIOL_V 121 and one of CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141. Fourth-year standing is also required. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 400 or GEOS_V 400. Equivalency: GEOB_V 400.

subject: GEOS
title: Urban Meteorology
description: The impact of urbanization upon atmospheric processes and climates. The energy and water balances of cities. Meteorological effects (urban heat island, precipitation modification, etc.) and their significance. Models of the urban atmosphere. Prerequisite: One of GEOB_V 204, GEOS_V 204, GEOB_V 300, GEOS_V 300, AGRO_V 244, APBI_V 244. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 401 or GEOS_V 401. Equivalency: GEOB_V 401.

subject: GEOS
title: Air Pollution Meteorology
description: The nature of atmospheric pollutants. The ability of the atmosphere to disperse, transform, and remove pollutants. Air pollution dispersion models. Air quality monitoring, criteria, and standards. Prerequisite: One of GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, GEOB_V 300, GEOS_V 300. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 402 or GEOS_V 402. Equivalency: GEOB_V 402.

subject: GEOS
title: Catchment Hydrology
description: Hydrometeorology; runoff processes; streamwater chemistry in relation to runoff processes; effects of climate variations and land cover change on streamflow regimes; models of catchment hydrology. Prerequisite: One of GEOB_V 200, GEOS_V 200, GEOB_V 204, GEOS_V 204 and one of GEOB_V 305, GEOS_V 305, FRST_V 385 and one of STAT_V 200, FRST_V 231, BIOL_V 300. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 403 or GEOS_V 403. Equivalency: GEOB_V 403.

subject: GEOS
title: Rivers and Landforms: Fluvial Geomorphology
description: Introduction to open channel flow and sediment transport. River morphology and channel types. Palaeohydrology. The development of channel networks. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of EOSC_V 320, EOSC_V 330, GEOB_V 206, GEOS_V 206. Credit will only be granted for one of GEOB_V 405 or GEOS_V 405. Equivalency: GEOB_V 405

subject: GEOS
title: Watershed Dynamics and Morphology
description: Hillslope and stream channel processes and their rates of operation. Analysis and modelling geomorphic processes and associated hazards at the watershed scale. Applications in geoscience and engineering. This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB_V 206, GEOS_V 206, EOSC_V 330. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 406 or GEOS_V 406. Equivalency: GEOB_V 406.

subject: GEOS
title: Vegetation Dynamics: Disturbance, Climate and Human Impacts
description: Investigation of vegetation dynamics integrating theory and research to address contemporary issues of global environmental change. Students will conduct fieldwork and learn to analyze data and interpret results. Prerequisite: One of BIOL_V 230, GEOB_V 207, GEOS_V 207, FRST_V 201. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 407 or GEOS_V 407. Equivalency: GEOB_V 407.

subject: GEOS
title: The Changing Cryosphere: Snow, Ice and Climate Change
description: Formation of ice masses and their evolution including snowpacks, glaciers, and ice sheets. Relationships between ice and climate including records of climate change, glacier dynamics and ice-related hazards. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 157, SCIE_V 001, and one of GEOB_V 206, GEOS_V 206, GEOB_V 305, GEOS_V 305, GEOB_V 308, GEOS_V 308. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB _V 408 or GEOS _V 408. Equivalency: GEOB_V 408.

subject: GEOS
title: Advanced Field Studies in Geographical Sciences
description: Advanced research design, field sampling methods, instrumentation, surveying, mapping techniques, data analysis and management; self-directed field-based research. Prerequisite: One of GEOB_V 309, GEOS_V 309. Third-year standing in Geographical Sciences, Environmental Sciences or Major in Geography (Environmental and Sustainability). Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 409 or GEOS_V 409. Equivalency: GEOB_V 409.

subject: GEOS
title: River Restoration: Science and Society
description: Projects designed to give students research development and design experience. Projects are provided by research faculty in Science and Engineering and from local industry. Recommended prerequisites: one of GEOB_V 206, GEOS_V 206, GEOB_V 305, GEOS_V 305, GEOB_V 405, GEOS_V 405, GEOB_V 406, GEOS_V 406, EOSC_V 325, EOSC_V 329, EOSC_V 330. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 415 or GEOS_V 415. Equivalency: GEOB_V 415.

subject: GEOS
title: Directed Studies in Geographical Sciences
description: For fourth-year students in Geography to permit investigation of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of the department head and of a supervisory faculty member is required. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 448 or GEOS_V 448. Equivalency: GEOB_V 448.

subject: GEOS
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Original research on an approved topic, developed under the guidance of a faculty member. Open to 4th year students in Geographical Sciences with appropriate background courses related to the research topic, and permission of the directing faculty member. The 3-credit option is only available to students who complete GEOS_V 449 in tandem with GEOS_V 409. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 449 or GEOS_V 449. Equivalency: GEOB_V 449.

subject: GEOS
title: Research in Cartography
description: Use of cartography in primary research applications. Discussion of contemporary topics in cognitive, social, and technical cartography and data visualization. Recommended prerequisites: one of GEOB_V 270, GEOS_V 270, GEOB_V 372, GEOS_V 372. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 472 or GEOS_V 472. Equivalency: GEOB_V 472.

subject: GEOS
title: Research in Geographic Information Science
description: Students use GIS in primary research applications in conservation biology, crime analysis, and health geography; theoretical and practical aspects considered in a hands-on environment. Prerequisite: One of GEOB_V 370, GEOS_V 370. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 479 or GEOS_V 479. Equivalency: GEOB_V 479.

subject: GEOS
title: Student Directed Seminar in Geographical Sciences
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies in physical geography, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. This course carries science credit. Credit will be granted for only one of GEOB_V 490, GEOS_V 490 and GEOG_V 442. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in Geographical Sciences. Equivalency: GEOB_V 490.

subject: GRSJ
title: Introduction to Social Justice
description: An overview of intersectional feminist debates and theoretical traditions.

subject: GRSJ
title: Global Issues in Social Justice
description: Intersectional feminist theory and practice, focusing on contemporary issues in a transnational context.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender and Environmental Justice
description: An interdisciplinary and cross-cultural overview of contemporary environmental issues, as they relate to gender equality and social justice challenges and initiatives that respond to ecological crises. Recommended: GRSJ 101.

subject: GRSJ
title: Connecting with Computer Science
description: Fundamentals of computer science and their connections with the arts, psychology, and biology. Historical, cultural, and gender perspectives of important contributions to the field will be discussed. No prior computing background required.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race and Colonialism in Canada
description: The historical foundations of colonialisms in Canada from just prior to the establishment of New France to the end of World War One.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race and Colonialism in the Americas
description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the ways gender, class, sexuality and race shape modern histories in Canada, and transnationally, from 1920 to the present.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Social Justice in Literature
description: Techniques of literary study, with emphasis on intersectionality and the ways in which gender is represented in literature and contributions of feminism and gender studies to literary studies.

subject: GRSJ
title: Youth Activism and Social Justice
description: A critical engagement with major issues, debates, and politics in feminist and social justice scholarship through an exploration of youth movements with a focus on activists, popular culture, digital activism, fan cultures, and literature by and for youth.

subject: GRSJ
title: Human Rights and Artistic Expression: Thinking Beyond the Legal
description: How human rights are expressed in the Arts. Critical engagement with feminist, race and social justice scholarship, and activism.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Representation in Modern Asia
description: The complex relationships between mechanisms of power, gender, and representation in Asia in different spaces examined through an interdisciplinary lens.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Social Structures in Modern Asia
description: Situates Asia in a global context and explores the complex relationships between gender, social structures, and social change.

subject: GRSJ
title: Topics in Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Social Justice
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website or contact the GRSJ undergraduate program for details.

subject: GRSJ
title: Intersectional Approaches to Thinking Gender
description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the multiple intersections between gender and (neo)colonialism, racism, poverty, ableism, and heterosexism in a globalized world; historical and cross-cultural aspects, and the social construction of sex and gender, masculinity and femininity.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race and Indigeneity in Canada
description: Gender and indigeneity in the documented histories and narrated lives of Indigenous people in Canada. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102, or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Pedagogies of Social Justice
description: The intersections of gender, education, and work using sociological and economic frameworks. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race, Social Justice and the Law
description: A survey of feminist legal thought and recent developments in feminism and law, with a focus on Canada. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gaming the System: Digital Media, Social Justice, and Video Games
description: Emerging technology in the areas of digital affect theory, cyborg feminism, critical digital humanities, critical race studies, surveillance studies, and queer game studies.

subject: GRSJ
title: Social Justice Issues in Community and International Organizing
description: Critical examination and practical applications of concepts, theories, methods, and strategies of gender-aware organizing at the community and international levels. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Globalization and Social Justice: Gender, Race, and Sexuality in International Politics
description: Critical examination of the gender dimension of globalization and the theories, discourse, and practices in international politics using gender analysis. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Popular Culture
description: Critical examination of mainstream and alternative media images of gender, race, and sexuality in the context of networked social media, film, music, and television. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Creativity from the Margins
description: Critical engagement with the creative process of marginalized peoples and the intersection of creative writing, social justice, and anti-racist feminism. Emphasis on how historical and social context are crucial to acts of creative writing and reading. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102, or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Gender, Race, Social Justice and Health
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to gender and health issues using selected theoretical frameworks. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: African/Black Women in the Americas
description: An interdisciplinary survey of gender studies and histories of African/Black women in the Americas from the beginning of the slave trade to the present. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Critical Racial Theories
description: Critical theories of racial and cultural difference. Initial formulations of theses against scientific racism and their later transformation by historical, social, and global-historical accounts of racial subjugation.

subject: GRSJ
title: Queer and Trans of Colour Theorizing
description: The intellectual and political interventions of queer of colour theorizing in the gender and sexual politics of racial and imperial projects, including its engagements with women of colour feminisms, settler colonial and indigenous studies, and immigration and diaspora studies.

subject: GRSJ
title: Feminist Anti-Racist Pedagogies
description: Feminist pedagogies and feminist debates about pedagogy in formal, nonformal, and informal educational settings. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Anti-colonial and Feminist Qualitative Methodologies
description: Data collection techniques, the politics of interpretation, and the formulation of a research proposal using a feminist, anti-racist framework. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

subject: GRSJ
title: The Politics of Gender, Families, and Nation-Building
description: Investigation of historical and contemporary scholarship on the diversity of families, focusing on differences of gender, sexuality, race/ethnicity, and social class within and across national borders. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

subject: GRSJ
title: Theories of Representation and Difference
description: Feminist scholarship emphasizing languages and processes of representation and the construction of difference in cultural discourses and institutions. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

subject: GRSJ
title: Theories of Subjectivity
description: How feminist scholarship has shaped and reinterpreted accounts of the subject, drawing on such traditions as structuralism, poststructuralism, psychoanalysis, postcolonialism, postmodernism, and Queer Theory. Recommended pre-requisites: All of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

subject: GRSJ
title: Topics in Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Social Justice
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website or contact the GRSJ undergraduate program for details. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to third-year standing or above

subject: GRSJ
title: Body, Gender and Society
description: An interdisciplinary examination of the body, exploring how social relations and space are implicated in the constitution and experience of gendered bodies and identities, with an emphasis on feminist analyses of body-societal relations. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Religious Feminisms
description: Examines religious feminisms from three Abrahamic traditions. An in-depth study of challenges various doctrinal discourses and practices pose for feminist projects. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102.

subject: GRSJ
title: Critical Racial and Anti-Colonial Feminist Approaches
description: Critical anti-colonial and feminist analyses of colonial and racial subjugation, as well as the many modalities of indigenous and minority resistance.

subject: GRSJ
title: Advanced Research Seminar
description: Critical theories, methodologies, ethics and practices appropriate for advanced feminist research. Recommended pre-requisite: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors with fourth-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Special Topics in Gender, Race, and Sexuality
description: Examination in depth of selected topics in gender, race, and sexuality. Consult the Student Service Centre course schedule for course offerings. May be repeated for credit. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

subject: GRSJ
title: Directed Studies
description: General reading and/or a research undertaking, with the agreement, and under supervision of, a faculty member selected by the student and approved by the GRSJ Undergraduate Advisor. A written paper or equivalent will be required. Open to GRSJ majors or minors.

subject: GRSJ
title: Decolonizing Praxis: A Practicum in Social Justice
description: Connects feminist and critical race theory and practice through placement in a community organization. As is the case with all UBC practice-related courses, this course requires a Criminal Record Check. Open to GRSJ Majors. This course is graded for Pass/Fail. Restricted to GRSJ Majors with fourth-year standing. Prerequisite: All of GRSJ_V 101, GRSJ_V 102 and two of GRSJ_V 325, GRSJ_V 326, GRSJ_V 327, GRSJ_V 328. Consult the department. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: HESO
title: Directed Studies
description: Investigation of readings and research undertaking topics of health and society, under the supervision of a faculty member with relevant expertise and experience. Restricted to students enrolled in the Minor in Health and Society program and with approval from the HESO Chair. Prerequisites: One of SPPH_V 301 or SOCI_V 284. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: HESO
title: Sociocultural Determinants of Health
description: Methods for analyzing population health data and medical research reporting.

subject: HESO
title: Directed Studies
description: Advanced research undertaking topics of health and society, under the supervision of a faculty member with relevant expertise and experience. Restricted to students enrolled in the Minor in Health and Society program and with approval from the HESO Chair. Prerequisites: One of SPPH_V 301 or SOCI_V 284. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ISCI
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
description: Critical analysis of recent scientific literature that combines disciplines that students are integrating in their Integrated Sciences Curriculum. . Prerequisite: Registration in Integrated Sciences Program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ISCI
title: The Size of Things
description: Scaling as a general approach to laws governing the geometry, kinematics and dynamics of systems. Dimensional analysis, isometry and allometry applied to topics from Biology, Physics, Earth Science and Economics. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Symmetry
description: Recognizing symmetry; point groups in 2D and 3D; plane groups in 2D; space groups in 3D; the role of symmetry in the natural and human world. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Research Development Project
description: Retreat to develop skills in writing scientific research proposals. Emphasis on formulating and testing hypotheses to explain observations. Course location will vary; fee payable prior to retreat. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Science of Measurement and Instrumentation
description: Interactive course integrating diverse aspects of science: semi-quantitative overview of physical principles underlying modern measurement technology; philosophy of measurement; accuracy and limits to measurement, and resultant scientific, sociological and economic consequences. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Topics in Integrated Sciences
description: Interactive examination of a theme common to all areas of science. Themes will change from year to year. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

subject: ISCI
title: Theory and Practice of Games in Economics and Evolution
description: Exploration of human and animal interactions: integrating evolutionary and economic perspectives to investigate individual and social behaviour. Credit will be granted for only one of ECON 221 or ISCI 344. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

subject: ISCI
title: Integrative Bioinformatics
description: Storage and processing of information in biological systems. Computational methods for recovering and interpreting stored genetic information. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Darwinian Medicine
description: Using the Darwinian theory of natural selection to explore explanations of infectious diseases, allergies, cancer, mental illness, and other human diseases. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: www.vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-sc… Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science. Equivalency: BIOL 350

subject: ISCI
title: Why the Big Brain? The Evolution of Human Cognition
description: Evolutionary causes, consequences and constraints of human cognition; enhanced encephalization and mentalizing capabilities throughout the Primate Order, and the emergence of cognitive faculties that define the human species. Prerequisite: Third-year or higher standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Application of systems science encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems approaches to study regional sustainability. Prerequisite: Third-year or higher standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Field Course: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Systems science approaches encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems to investigate a selected region of the world. Course location will vary; fee payable prior to field course.

subject: ISCI
title: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Normally taken in Winter Session of third year or Summer Session after third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students in the ISP Co-op program. Prerequisite: One term in ISP.

subject: ISCI
title: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 398.

subject: ISCI
title: Integrated Sciences Graduating Seminar
description: Reflection of Integrated Sciences degree experience, development of professional skills, and a showcase of degree integrations to the community. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in the Integrated Sciences specialization. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ISCI
title: Models in Science
description: Meaning, nature, use, strengths and limitations of models as investigative tools in all scientific disciplines. Detailed investigation of selected model systems from different scientific disciplines. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Ethical Issues in Science
description: Theoretical and practical consideration of ethics in the practice, reporting, public impact and accountability of science. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in any faculty.

subject: ISCI
title: Non-Animal Methods in Biomedical Science
description: Interdisciplinary non-animal methods (e.g., organoids, organ-on-a-chip, 3D bioprinting) for research, testing, and education; the regulatory landscape. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

subject: ISCI
title: Directed Studies
description: Permission of the Director is required.

subject: ISCI
title: Interdisciplinary Honours Thesis
description: Original research work under the guidance of a faculty member. Registration by approval of the Integrated Sciences Director. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: ISCI
title: Comparative Field Research Course: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Systems science approaches encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems to investigate, analyze and research two unique regions of the world. Course location may vary; course location must be different than ISCI 361; fee payable prior to field course. Prerequisite: ISCI 361.

subject: ISCI
title: Student Directed Seminars
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.

subject: ISCI
title: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 399.

subject: ISCI
title: Co-Operative Work Placement IV
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 498.

subject: JAPN
title: Beginning Japanese IA
description: An introduction to modern spoken and written Japanese with emphasis on both form (grammar and syntax) and functions (Non-intensive). Not available for credit to students with JAPN 11 and/or JAPN 12. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 100 or JAPN_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Beginning Japanese IB
description: Continuation of JAPN_V 100 (Non-intensive). Not available for credit to students with JAPN 12. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 101 or JAPN_V 160. Recommended pre-requisite: JAPN_V 100. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intensive Beginning Japanese I
description: An introduction to modern spoken and written Japanese with emphasis on both form (grammar and syntax) and functions. Offered in Term 1. Not available for credit to students with JAPN 12. Students are recommended to complete JAPN_V 160 and 260 in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 160 or JAPN_V 150 or both JAPN_V 100, JAPN_V 101. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Beginning Japanese II A
description: Continuation of JAPN_V 101 (Non-intensive). Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 200 or JAPN_V 102 or JAPN_V 260. Recommended pre-requisite: one of JAPN_V 101, JAPN_V 150, JAPN_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Beginning Japanese II B
description: Continuation of JAPN 200 (Non-intensive). Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 201 or JAPN_V 103 or JAPN_V 260. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 102, JAPN_V 200. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Basic Japanese Grammar
description: Emphasis on grammar, writing and reading Intended for students with a background in spoken Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 204 or JAPN_V 104. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intensive Beginning Japanese II
description: Continuation of JAPN_V 160. Offered in Term 2. Students are recommended to complete JAPN_V 160 and 260 in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 260 or JAPN_V 151 or both JAPN_V 102, JAPN_V 103 or both JAPN_V 200, JAPN_V 201. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 101, JAPN_V 150, JAPN_V 160. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Enriched Summer Intensive Beginning Japanese
description: An integrated language course developing communicative competence in speaking, listening to, reading, and writing modern Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 261 or JAPN_V 161. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intermediate Japanese I A
description: Integrated coverage of topics on culture and cross-cultural communication designed to develop competencies in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. It is strongly recommended that JAPN_V 320 and JAPN_V 321 be taken in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 320 or JAPN_V 210 or JAPN_V 360. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 103, JAPN_V 151, JAPN_V 201, JAPN_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intermediate Japanese I B
description: Continuation of JAPN_V 320. It is strongly recommended that JAPN_V 320 and JAPN_V 321 be taken in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 321 or JAPN_V 211 or JAPN_V 360. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 210, JAPN_V 320. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intermediate Japanese II A
description: It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 322 and JAPN_V 323 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 322 or JAPN_V 212 or JAPN_V 361. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 211, JAPN_V 250, JAPN_V 321, JAPN_V 360. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intermediate Japanese II B
description: A continuation of JAPN_V 322. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 322 and JAPN_V 323 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 323 and JAPN_V 212 or JAPN_V 361. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 212, JAPN_V 322. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Reading Course in Japanese for Honours Students

subject: JAPN
title: Intensive Intermediate Japanese I
description: Integrated coverage of topics on culture and cross-cultural communication designed to develop competencies in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. Offered in Term 1. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 360 and JAPN_V 361 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 360 or JAPN_V 212 or both JAPN_V 210, JAPN_V 211 or both JAPN_V 320, JAPN_V 321. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 103, JAPN_V 151, JAPN_V 201, JAPN_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Intensive Intermediate Japanese II
description: Continuation of JAPN_V 360. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 360 and JAPN_V 361 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 361 or JAPN_V 251 or both JAPN_V 212, JAPN_V 213 or both JAPN_V 322, JAPN_V 323. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 211, JAPN_V 250, JAPN_V 321, JAPN_V 360. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Advanced Modern Japanese: Reading and Writing I
description: Selected texts covering various aspects of Japanese cultural history and contemporary Japanese culture/society; emphasis on grammatical analysis and development of advanced competencies for reading and writing. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 400 and JAPN_V 401 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 400 or JAPN_V 300. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 213, JAPN_V 251, JAPN_V 323, JAPN_V 361. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Advanced Modern Japanese: Reading and Writing II
description: Continuation of JAPN_V 301. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 400 and JAPN_V 401 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 401 or JAPN_V 301. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 300, JAPN_V 400. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Advanced Modern Japanese: Conversation and Composition I
description: Improvement of speaking and writing skills through readings and discussions on a variety of social and cultural issues; emphasis on appropriate language use in formal situations. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 402 and JAPN_V 403 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 402 or JAPN_V 302. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 213, JAPN_V 251, JAPN_V 323, JAPN_V 361. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Advanced Modern Japanese: Conversation and Composition II
description: Improvement of speaking and writing skills through readings and discussions on a variety of social and cultural issues; emphasis on the development of formal presentation skills. It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN_V 402 and JAPN_V 403 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 403 or JAPN_V 303. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 302, JAPN_V 402. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Classical Japanese I
description: The grammar, orthography, and literary style of pre-modern Japanese (bungo). It is strongly recommended that students have 12 credits of JAPN, or equivalent, prior to registration. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 422 or JAPN 311.

subject: JAPN
title: Classical Japanese II
description: A continuation of JAPN 422. Focus on reading pre-modern primary sources and producing English translations. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 423 or JAPN 312. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 311, JAPN 422.

subject: JAPN
title: Japanese for Professional Life I
description: Technical Japanese as it is used in business, commerce, industry, etc. Emphasis on specialized current vocabulary and on the development of communicative competence relevant for workplaces in these fields. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 424 or JAPN 314. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 213, JAPN 251, JAPN 323, JAPN 361.

subject: JAPN
title: Japanese for Professional Life II
description: Continuation of JAPN 424. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 425 or JAPN 315. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 314, JAPN 424.

subject: JAPN
title: Advanced Oral Communication I
description: Oral communication skills appropriate for studying and working in a Japanese-speaking environment either formal or informal. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 450 or JAPN_V 410. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 300, JAPN_V 400 and one of JAPN_V 302, JAPN_V 402, JAPN_V 314, JAPN_V 424. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Advanced Oral Communication II
description: A continuation of JAPN_V 450. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 451 or JAPN_V 411. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 410, JAPN_V 450. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Readings in Modern Japanese Essays
description: Advanced reading and analysis of scholarly texts in modern Japanese drawn from history, sociology, economics, etc. Advanced conversation, composition, and practice in the use of standard reference tools as preparation for independent research in Japanese. Students are recommended to complete JAPN_V 403 prior to taking JAPN_V 452. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 452 or JAPN_V 406. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 301, JAPN_V 401. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Readings in Modern Japanese Literature
description: An advanced course in the reading and analysis of literary texts in modern Japanese. Advanced conversation, translation into English and practice in the use of standard reference tools as preparation for advanced research in Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 453 or JAPN_V 408. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 301, JAPN_V 401. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Newspaper Japanese I
description: Developing fluency in reading contemporary Japanese newspapers; concentration on current and emerging vocabulary, evolving grammatical features, and style of presentation. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 456 or JAPN_V 416. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 301, JAPN_V 401 and one of JAPN_V 302, JAPN_V 402, JAPN_V 314, JAPN_V 424. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Newspaper Japanese II
description: A continuation of JAPN_V 456. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 457 or JAPN_V 417. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN_V 416, JAPN_V 456. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: JAPN
title: Topics in Japanese Language, Culture, and Society
description: Advanced Japanese language course combined with analysis of various media in literary, journalistic, and popular genres drawn from history, sociology, cultural studies, etc. Practice in the use of standard reference tools prepares students for independent research in Japanese. Students are recommended to complete JAPN 403 prior to JAPN 459. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 459 or JAPN 419. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 301, JAPN 401; and permission from instructor.

subject: JAPN
title: Grammatical Analysis of Japanese I
description: Analysis of the grammatical structure of modern Japanese. Contrastive analysis of Japanese and English as well as error analysis. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 460 or JAPN 420. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 301, JAPN 401 and one of JAPN 303, JAPN 403.

subject: JAPN
title: Grammatical Analysis of Japanese II
description: A continuation of JAPN 460. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 461 or JAPN 421. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 420, JAPN 460.

subject: JAPN
title: Researching Modern Japanese Religions
description: Research tools and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of modern Japanese religions (nineteenth century to the present) including state-of-the-field works in English, and locating primary and secondary materials in Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 462 or JAPN 452. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 200- or 300-level courses in Asian religions; 3 credit writing-intensive course in Asian Studies; ability to read modern Japanese or 18 credits of Japanese language courses and permission of instructor.

subject: JAPN
title: Japanese Media and Translation
description: Emphasizing the development of translingual and transcultural literacies in Japanese popular media with a primary focus on film. This course is recommended for students with credit for JAPN_V 401 and JAPN_V 402, or placement with native or near-native proficiency in Japanese.

subject: JAPN
title: Supervised Study in the Japanese Language
description: Primarily for graduate students. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN_V 470 or JAPN_V 440.

subject: JAPN
title: Tutorial in Japanese for Honours Students
description: This course will require the presentation of at least one research paper. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 472 or JAPN 442.

subject: LARC
title: Trees and Shrubs in Landscape
description: Culture and identification of landscape materials with emphasis on woody plants. Elementary principles of landscape composition. Suitable for students of other faculties and departments interested in landscape materials and their uses, but priority given to Agroecology and Landscape Architecture students.

subject: MECH
title: Technical Skills Practicum
description: Engineering graphics, spatial visualization, CAD, equation solvers, machine shop practice, electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting, elements of engineering science. . Prerequisite: All of APSC_V 160, MATH_V 100, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 157, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170 and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159 and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150. Corequisite: MECH_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering Science I
description: Rigid body kinetics and kinematics, basic electrical circuits, work and power, stress and strain, torsion, bending, engineering materials, probability and statistics. This course includes the content of ELEC_V 203. Prerequisite: All of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 157, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170; and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150. Corequisite: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 224. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering Science II
description: Fluid properties, equations of state. Pressure, buoyancy, hydrostatic forces. Conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. Work and heat; internal energy and enthalpy. Bernoulli's equation. Dimensional analysis, modelling. Turbulent flow in pipes; turbomachinery. Second law and the Carnot cycle; entropy; first and second law analysis of systems. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 220. Corequisite: MECH_V 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process
description: Design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Design projects representing both mechanical mechanism design and thermofluid systems. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Integration of Engineering Concepts I
description: Integration of the theory and practice of Mechanical Engineering to illustrate the commonality and conceptual connectivity of seemingly different technical areas. Emphasis on dynamics, solid mechanics, materials, electronics, and mathematics. . Corequisite: MECH_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Integration of Engineering Concepts II
description: Integration of the theory and practice of Mechanical Engineering to illustrate the commonality and conceptual connectivity of seemingly different technical areas. Emphasis on thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and mathematics. . Corequisite: MECH_V 222. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Technical Communication for Mechanical Engineers
description: Written and oral communication. Preparation of design reports, business correspondence, verbal, online, and visual presentation of technical material. Restricted to students in the second year of Mechanical Engineering. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 226 or MECH_V 227. Prerequisite: ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150, or APSC_O 176. Corequisite: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 221, MECH_V 222, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Approaches to Technical Communication for Mechanical Engineers
description: Written and oral communication. Preparation of design, business correspondence, verbal, online and visual presentation of technical material. Focus on the linguistic structure and style of technical communication. Restricted to students in Mechanical Engineering. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 226 or MECH_V 227. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 220 and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Technical Skills Practicum I
description: Engineering graphics, spatial visualization, CAD, equation solvers, elements of engineering science. . Prerequisite: All of APSC_V 160, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170; and one of APSC_V 100, APSC_V 150, APSC_V 151; and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150. Corequisite: MECH_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Technical Skills Practicum II
description: Machine shop practice, electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting. Prerequisite: MECH_V 230. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process I
description: Introduction to design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Prerequisite: All of APSC_V 160, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170; and one of APSC_V 100, APSC_V 150, APSC_V 151; and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150. Corequisite: MECH_V 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process II
description: Intermediate design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Design project representing mechanical mechanism design and thermofluid systems. Prerequisite: MECH_V 232. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Technical Skills Practicum IIA
description: Electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 230. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Technical Skills Practicum IIB
description: Machine shop practice. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 234. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to Mechanics of Materials
description: Statically determinate frames and trusses; normal and shear stresses and strains; shear force and bending moment diagrams; theory of beam bending, torsion of circular rods; transformation of stress and strain in two and three dimensions, Mohr's circle; yield and ultimate failure criteria. . Prerequisite: Either (a) all of MATH_V 101, PHYS_V 170 or (b) all of APSC_O 172, APSC_O 173, APSC_O 180. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
description: Fluid properties; statics; kinematics, dynamics, energy, and momentum principles for control volumes; dimensional analysis and similarity; laminar and turbulent flow; pipe flow; principles of centrifugal pumps. . Prerequisite: All of MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 170 and one of MATH_V 217, MATH_V 253; and either (a) PHYS_V 131 and one of PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118; or (b) PHYS_V 153 or (c) all of PHYS_V 157, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 159. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Data Analysis and Mechanical Engineering Laboratories
description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Data Analysis and Mechatronics Laboratories
description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials and heat transfer. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools. Common mechanical devices. For students in the Mechatronics Option only. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Machine Design
description: Selection of flexible drives, bearings, fluid power system components, and couplings. Design of shafts, bolted joints and power screws. Design and selection of gears, gear trains, and mechanisms. Recommended co-requisite: MECH_V 360. . Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 223, MECH_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Thermodynamics II
description: Air standard and vapor cycles; first and second law of cycles. Exergy. Gas mixtures. Energy conservation. Equilibrium. Reacting systems. Application to thermofluid systems such as power plants. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechanical Engineering Design Project
description: Applying the design process, making educated assumptions and decisions, and working in teams to provide a new mechanical design. Weekly lecture discussing product development and various factors affecting the design. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher in Mechanical Engineering. Prerequisite: MECH_V 223. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Materials for Mechanical Design
description: Selection of material properties for mechanical design. Metals and alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites and other hybrid materials. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 224 or (b) all of APSC_V 278, MECH_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering Analysis
description: Fourier series; auto- and cross-correlation; power spectra; discrete Fourier transform; boundary-value problems; numerical methods; partial differential equations; heat, wave, Laplace, Poisson, and wave equations. Applications to mechanical engineering and practical computing emphasized. . Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225. Equivalency: MATH_V 358. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Computational Methods for Mechanical Engineering
description: Computational methods for solving mechanical engineering problems. Numerical computation of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations; interpolation and extrapolation; numerical integration and differentiation; numerical solution of differential equations. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 358 or MECH_V 359. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechanics of Materials
description: Beam deflections, singularity functions; use of tabulated solutions; column buckling; Castigliano's theorem, statically indeterminate beams, bending of beams with asymmetric cross-sections, shear centre; principal stresses and stress invariants in three dimensions. . Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 224, MECH_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Modelling of Mechatronic Systems
description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, thermal, fluid elements and mixed mechatronic systems. Signal processing, signal conditioning. Sensors, data acquisition systems, actuators. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering Measurements and Instrumentation
description: Industrial measurement needs including: architecture of electronic instrumentation systems; electrical representation of physical quantities; sensors and actuators; analog signal processing using linear and non-linear circuits; computer-based readout including programming for user-interface and data acquisition. Prerequisite: Either (a) two of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 224, ELEC_V 203 or (b) all of MANU_V 230, ELEC_V 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Heat Transfer
description: Steady and transient conduction. Radiation heat transfer. Convective heat and mass transfer in pipes and from external surfaces. Design of heat exchangers. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257, PHYS_V 203 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Fluid Dynamics
description: Review of principles, compressible flow, potential flow, simple laminar viscous flow, boundary layers, flow around bluff bodies. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of MATH_V 255 or MATH_V 256 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280 and one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257, PHYS_V 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Manufacturing Processes
description: Manufacturing characteristics of materials and their control. Metal forming processes, plastic deformations, rolling, forging, drawing, extrusion, sheet metal forming. Machining processes and machine tools, turning, milling, drilling, grinding. Metal fabrication, welding and casting. An introduction to process planning. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Professionalism and Ethics in Engineering
description: Professionalism, ethical frameworks, decolonization, equity, diversity, inclusion, law. Obligations of the engineer. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in B.A.Sc. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Lectures and readings on specialized topics of current interest in Mechanical Engineering. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Air Pollution, Technology and Society
description: Causes and effects of air pollution in the context of technology and society. Topics include: impact of air pollutants on air quality and climate, atmospheric science, public policy, collective action, environmental justice, science communication, economic externalities, and ethical engineering design. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. . Prerequisite: Second-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering in Society and Technological Stewardship
description: Societal influences that affect engineering activities, including interactions between engineering and the economic, health, safety, legal, and cultural aspects of society; uncertainties in the prediction of such interactions; industrial policy; sustainable development; entrepreneurship; and environmental and technological stewardship. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Sensors and Actuators
description: Measurement of motion, stress, force, torque, temperature, flow and pressure; principles of sensors and signal conditioning methods; actuators. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 360, MECH_V 463, ELEC_V 343. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechatronics System Instrumentation
description: Architecture of mechatronics devices; integration of mechanical, electronics, sensors, actuators, computer and real time software systems; PLC and PC based systems; discrete and continuous automation system design. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 366. Corequisite: MECH_V 420. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
description: Fundamentals of MEMS (MicroElectroMechanical Systems). Microfabrication of MEMS with solid-state technology. LIGA and micro injection molding. Physics of MEMS. Operational principles of various MEMS devices. [2-3--0]. Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 224, ELEC_V 204 and all of MECH_V 360, MECH_V 368. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechatronic Product Design
description: Design of mechatronic systems for industrial and human-centric applications compliant structures; electronic circuits to interface with sensors and actuators; embedded systems; precision timing and control; data acquisition and processing; user interfaces; and product innovation. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 366, ELEC_V 302, CPEN_V 312. and 4th year standing. Corequisite: CPEN_V 333, MECH_V 421. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechanical Design
description: Design of shafts and welded joints. Fatigue and fracture considerations in design: failure types, failure under static and dynamic loading, fatigue failure, crack initiation, and propagation. Introduction to the FEM in mechanical design. Students can only receive credit for one of MECH_V 326 or MECH_V 426. Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 223, MECH_V 260. Corequisite: MECH_V 360. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering Data Analysis
description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Engineering Economics
description: Discounted cash flows. Sources of funds, cost of capital. Effects of depreciation, taxes, inflation. Evaluation and comparison of economic models for engineering projects. Replacement decisions. Public project analysis. Risk analysis. Project control, inventory analysis, simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Biofluids
description: Review of principles, Navier-Stokes equations, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in human body. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 433 or MECH_V 533. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of MATH_V 255, MATH_V 256 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280. Equivalency: MECH_V 533. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Muscle and joint loads. Muscle mechanics. Musculoskeletal dynamics. Gait. Tissue mechanics of tendon, ligament, articular cartilage, and bone. Biomaterials. Application examples in orthopaedics including joint replacement and fracture fixation. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 435 or MECH_V 535. Students who have received credit for BMEG_V 230 or 330 cannot also receive credit for MECH_V 435. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 221 or (b) all of APSC_V 278, MECH_V 260. Equivalency: MECH_V 535. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, spine, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets. Recommended pre-requisites: MECH_V 224, or all of MECH_V 260 and BMEG_V 330. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 436 or MECH_V 536. . Equivalency: MECH_V 536. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Biomechanics Research
description: Seminar in Biomechanics research. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Fuel Cell Systems
description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion: fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution. Recommended prerequisites: MECH_V 327 and MECH_V 375. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 445 or MECH_V 577. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280. Equivalency: MECH_V 577. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Aerospace Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and aerospace devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, MECH_V 490. . Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 327, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360, MECH_V 426. And fourth-year standing in the Aerospace Option. Equivalency: MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Thermofluids Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and thermofluids devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 327, MECH 328, MECH 360. and fourth-year standing in the Thermofluids Option. Equivalency: MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical naval architecture and marine engineering devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490. . Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360, MECH_V 380. And fourth-year standing in the Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Option. Equivalency: MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Energy and Environment Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical energy and environment devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490. . Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 327, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360. and fourth-year standing in the Energy and Environment Option. Equivalency: MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Flex Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone design project designed to give students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490. [1-2-2; 1-2-2-] Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in Mechanical Engineering. Equivalency: MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechatronics Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone design program designed to give students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and mechatronics devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in the Mechatronics Option. Equivalency: MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Biomechanics and Medical Devices Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone design program designed to give students experience in the design and development of practical biomedical devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. For students in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option only. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490. [1-2-2; 1-2- 2-] Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option. Equivalency: MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Advanced Mechanics of Materials
description: Mechanics of rubber, tissue, and gels at large viscoelastic deformation; large plastic deformations and damage of materials; mechanical characterization of materials (property extraction from mechanical tests); selected problems in linear elasticity. Prerequisite: MECH_V 360 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Finite Element Analysis
description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametric elements. Development of computer programs for simple problems. Utilization of existing computer packages. Application to mechanical engineering problems. Recommended prerequisite: MECH 360. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 462 or MECH_V 514. Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 224 or MECH_V 260. Equivalency: MECH_V 514. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Mechanical Vibrations
description: Theory of vibration of mechanical systems. Undamped 1 degree of freedom vibration, forced vibrations and resonance, damping, multiple degree of freedom systems, mode shapes and orthogonality, continuous systems, vibration measuring instruments and frequency spectrum analysis. Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 224, MECH_V 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Industrial Robotics
description: Definition and classification of industrial robotic devices. Selection and implementation issues. Workcell environments. Forward and inverse kinematics, dynamics, trajectory planning. Sensing and manipulation tasks. Control architectures. Recommended co-requisite: MECH_V 466 or MECH_V 467. Credit will be granted for only one of ELEC_V 442, EECE_V 571R, EECE_V 589, MECH_V 464 or MECH_V 563. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Control Systems I
description: Introduction to control systems: system modelling and transfer functions; block diagrams; principles of feedback; stability; Bode plots; root locus methods; frequency response; control design. Laboratory experiments to support the lecture content. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 466, ELEC_V 341, or MECH_V 467. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 224 or (b) MATH_V 255 and one of ELEC_V 201, ELEC_V 202, ELEC_V 204, EECE_V 251, EECE_V 253; or (c) all of ELEC_V 204, ELEC_V 221, ENPH_V 270, MATH_V 255. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Computer Control of Mechatronics Systems
description: Block diagrams and transfer functions, continuous and discrete domain transformations, feedback control system characteristics, control design in both continuous and discrete domain, absolute and relative stability, laboratory examples of Mechatronic systems design. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 467 or MECH_V 541. Credit cannot be obtained for both MECH_V 466 and MECH_V 467. Prerequisite: One of MECH_V 366, MANU_V 386. Equivalency: MECH_V 541. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Control Systems II
description: Introduction to state space control methods for linear systems including modal control, controllability, observability, linear quadratic regulators, optimal control. Recommended co-requisite: MECH_V 366. Prerequisite: MECH_V 466, ELEC_V 341, or CHBE_V 356. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 468 or MECH_V 509. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Dynamic System Modelling
description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal systems; analytical models; model representations such as linear and bond graphs; response analysis; digital simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Energy Conversion Systems
description: Energy supply and demand. Energy conversion chain. Electrical power generation using thermal power plants, renewable energy, and fuel cells. Rankine cycle steam power. Brayton cycle gas turbine power plants, intercooling, reheat, and regeneration. Internal combustion engines. Exhaust gas after treatment. Combined and binary cycles. Nuclear power. Recommended pre-requisites: All of MECH_V 327, MECH_V 375. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: An Introduction to Pulp and Papermaking
description: Overview of pulp and paper operations. Conversion of wood to fibre through mechanical or chemical pulping, processing of recycled fibre, the papermaking process and paper converting operations. Contemporary developments. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning
description: Principles of air conditioning; psychometrics and refrigeration. Heat transfer through building materials. Estimation of heating and cooling loads including the use of current software. System design. Ground, air and water source heat pumps. . Prerequisite: MECH_V 375. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Aerospace Propulsion
description: Cycle analysis of jet engines, thermodynamic cycles, mechanics and thermodynamics of combustion, components and the performance characteristics of chemical rockets. The detailed analysis of operating characteristics of turbojet, turbofan, turboprop, afterburning, and ramjet propulsion systems. . Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 327, MECH_V 375, MECH_V 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Internal Combustion Engines
description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power, and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Engine emission and control systems. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH_V 327. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 478 or MECH_V 578. . Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280. Equivalency: MECH_V 578. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Techniques for numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, including an introduction to the finite difference, finite volume and finite element approaches. Simulation of laminar and turbulent flows, including common turbulent models. Validation techniques. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH_V 380. . This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: MECH
title: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 481 or MECH_V 581.
