Readings are drawn from complete original texts, and assessment is based on a research essay. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: Topics in Political Theory
description: Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: Policy Analysis
description: Analytical tools and practical policy analysis to address real-world issues for clients or employers. Involves collecting and analyzing policy-relevant data, generating alternatives, and evaluating trade-offs. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: Foreign Policy Analysis
description: A seminar devoted to the analysis of the foreign policies of one or more states, as well as to the study of literature pertaining to foreign policy analysis. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: Peace and Conflict Studies
description: A seminar on a selected topic concerning the causes of war and strategies for the promotion of peace. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: International Relations Theory
description: This seminar examines some of the major theoretical approaches to the study of international relations. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: International Interdependence
description: Topics and public policies relating to international economic relations. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses . Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or above.

subject: POLI
title: Advanced Topics in International Relations
description: Topics and public policies related to interactions between states and non-state actors, such as armed conflict management or international institutions. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses . One section (3 credits) reserved for fourth-year International Relations Majors. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or above.

subject: POLI
title: The Politics of International Law
description: Seminar on the origins and politics of international law, and its impact on international affairs; the laws of war, human rights, environment, law of the sea, and international criminal law. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

subject: POLI
title: Data and Models Capstone
description: Seminar on data analysis and modeling in Political Science. Restricted to Certificate in Data and Models in Political Science students. Prerequisite: All of POLI_V 310, POLI_V 380, POLI_V 381.

subject: POLI
title: Honours Thesis
description: In consultation with faculty, students develop a research project, report on their project during seminars, give feedback on their fellow students' projects, and write a thesis. Restricted to students with an Honours or Honours with specialization in Political Science. Fourth-year standing or higher required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: RELG
title: Introduction to Religions in Asia
description: A survey of religious traditions of Asia, including communities, professionals, practices and beliefs of small-scale and large-scale societies. Approaches and theories drawn from the field of religious studies. Equivalency: ASIA110

subject: RELG
title: Introduction to Asian Religions
description: The religions of India, China, and Japan in their interactions and cultural contexts, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism, Taoism, Confucianism, and Shinto.

subject: RELG
title: Classical Islam
description: The history and culture, values, and achievements of Islamic societies from 700-1500; the interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in Islamic societies. This course is highly recommended as a basis for all 300- and 400-level Islamic Studies courses.

subject: RELG
title: Modern Islam
description: The history and culture, values, and socio-political movements of the Islamic world from 1500 to the modern day; the interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in modern Islamic societies. This course is highly recommended as a basis for all 300- and 400-level Islamic Studies courses.

subject: RELG
title: History of Christianity II (15th C. C.E. - present)
description: The history of Christianity from the Reformation to the present day. Provides an historical overview of Christian thought and its institutions and significant people during the rise of the Reformation in various locales of Europe and beyond (Germany, France, Great Britain, Switzerland, and Scandinavia).

subject: RELG
title: Death and Afterlife in Western Religious Tradition
description: A survey of traditional attitudes toward death and beliefs regarding human existence after death in Western religions.

subject: RELG
title: Jews and Christians
description: Aspects of Jewish-Christian relations from the beginnings of Christianity to the present day. Emphasis on the study of Christian and Jewish texts in translation.

subject: RELG
title: Jewish Responses to Catastrophe
description: Topics include the destruction of the Second Temple, the Crusades, the expulsions from Spain and Portugal, and the Holocaust. A study of texts in translation.

subject: RELG
title: Jewish Literature in Translation
description: A survey of Jewish literature in medieval and modern times.

subject: RELG
title: Jews and Judaism in Canada
description: The history of the Jewish community in Canada, from New France to the present. Emphasis on the relationship between immigration and religious transformation, Jewish-Christian relations, the development of community structures.

subject: RELG
title: History of Christian Thought
description: Selected topics with special emphasis on doctrinal change and development, orthodoxy and heresy, tradition and authority, and Church and State in the Patristic, Medieval, Reformation, and Modern periods.

subject: RELG
title: Prophetic Figures in the Christian Tradition
description: Examined in their historical context and in terms of their continuing significance. Selection will vary from year to year, but may include Augustine, Thomas Aquinas, Martin Luther, and Teresa of Avila.

subject: RELG
title: Christianity in the Modern World
description: The interaction between Christianity and the major intellectual, social, and cultural developments since 1648 with special attention to the expansion of Christianity and its encounter with urban industrial society.

subject: RELG
title: Medieval Philosophy
description: Survey of Western European thought from Augustine to the fourteenth century. Possible topics and authors include: Augustine; Abelard; the influence of Islam; the rediscovery of Aristotle; Aquinas; Scotus; Ockham. Credit will be granted for only one of RELG 328 or PHIL 313. Equivalency: PHIL 313

subject: RELG
title: Medieval Jewish History
description: The political, social, economic, and cultural history of the Jews from the time of the Christianization of the Roman Empire to the expulsion of professing Jews from Spain and Portugal at the end of the fifteenth century.

subject: RELG
title: Modern Jewish History
description: The political, social, economic, and cultural history of the Jews from the beginning of the sixteenth century to the present, with special emphasis on changing attitudes to Jews and Judaism, and social and cultural transformations.

subject: RELG
title: Daoist (Taoist) Religion and Its Philosophical Background
description: A study of the Daoist religious traditions from their beginnings in the second century C.E. in cultural, intellectual and social contexts. Equivalency: ASIA381

subject: RELG
title: Buddhism in China
description: History, thought and practices of Chinese Buddhism from its beginnings until the twentieth century. Equivalency: ASIA382

subject: RELG
title: Concepts and Methods in the Study of Religion
description: Required of Major and Honours students in their third year. Open to others by permission of the instructor.

subject: RELG
title: Mystical Traditions: Jewish and Christian
description: Methodology, textual study and scholarly analysis of selected texts from these traditions.

subject: RELG
title: Topics in Medieval Judaism
description: The work of Maimonides and other Jewish philosophers, early developments in Jewish mysticism, the Jews as a minority culture in Islamic and Christian lands.

subject: RELG
title: Topics in Modern Judaism
description: The Jews in the ghetto culture, Hasidism, the Emancipation, Reform, Orthodox, and Conservative Movements.

subject: RELG
title: Seminar in the History of the Religion of Islam
description: A topic relevant to the study of Islam as a religion: e.g., the text and doctrines of the Qur'an; the Hadith (or Traditions) of the Prophet; Islamic Law; mysticism in Islam; the Shi'ah and the Isma'ilis. Not offered every year. Consult the departmental brochure for the topic to be offered.

subject: RELG
title: Readings in Hindu Religious Texts
description: Representative texts, in translation, of the Vedic, Epic, Puranic, Classical, Medieval, and Modern periods. Emphasis in the second term on texts of particular periods, movements, or sects, depending on the students' needs and interests. Those with the necessary preparation may read some texts in the original languages. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: RELG
title: Directed Studies
description: Reading and, where appropriate, other research on a topic arising in the discipline, arranged by agreement between the student and the instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: RELG
title: Images of Eve
description: The story of Adam and Eve, and its influence on the role and image of women in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

subject: SPAN
title: Beginners' Spanish I
description: Fundamentals of the Spanish language. Communicate with basic vocabulary in common tasks and situations related to present and future events. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Credit will be granted for either SPAN 103 or both SPAN 101, SPAN 102.

subject: SPAN
title: Beginners' Spanish II
description: Continuation of foundational elements of the language. Communicate using essential vocabulary in common tasks and situations related to past, present and future events. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 101. Credit will be granted for either SPAN_V 103 or both SPAN_V 101, SPAN_V 102.

subject: SPAN
title: Intensive Beginners' Spanish
description: Fundamentals of the Spanish language. Ideal for students with Spanish 12 or expertise in another Romance language. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed Grade 12 Spanish or for native or near-native speakers of other Romance languages. Credit will be granted for SPAN_V 103 or both SPAN_V 101, SPAN_V 102.

subject: SPAN
title: Elementary Spanish I
description: Expansion of fundamentals. Enhanced ability to exchange information, discuss the past and future, and express wishes, hopes and feelings in common personal and social contexts. Aligned with CEFR level A1-A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of Grade 11 Spanish, SPAN_V 102, or SPAN_V 103. Credit will be granted for either SPAN_V 203 or both SPAN_V 201, SPAN_V 202.

subject: SPAN
title: Elementary Spanish II
description: Expansion of fundamental notions and presentation of more elaborate structures in a variety of tenses and modes. Communicate to explore Hispanic culture and to hypothesize about present and past situations. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 201. Credit will be granted for either SPAN_V 203 or both SPAN_V 201, SPAN_V 202.

subject: SPAN
title: Intensive Elementary Spanish
description: Continuation of SPAN_V 103. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of SPAN_V 102, SPAN_V 103, or placement test for native or near-native speakers of other Romance Languages. Credits will be granted for SPAN_V 203 or both SPAN_V 201, SPAN_V 202.

subject: SPAN
title: Conversational Spanish I
description: Emphasizes communication skills through discussion, debate, and presentations; developing oral fluency and listening comprehension, through discussion of written texts and films. May include experiential learning projects involving native speakers from the Hispanic community. Prerequisite: One of BC High School Spanish Grade 12, SPAN 202, or SPAN 203.

subject: SPAN
title: Conversational Spanish II
description: Builds on communication skills through discussion, debate, and presentations; exploration of cultural topics through discussion of written texts and other media. May include experiential learning projects involving native speakers from the Hispanic community. Aligned with CEFR A2 objectives. Prerequisite: One of BC High School Spanish Grade 12, SPAN 202, SPAN 203 or SPAN 206.

subject: SPAN
title: Conversational Spanish and Culture
description: Exploration of cultural topics, concepts, and practices and how they frame and relate to the diverse geographies and cultural traditions from Spain, Latin America, and the diaspora through oral and written expressions. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 202 or SPAN_V 203.

subject: SPAN
title: Introduction to Literature in Spanish
description: Major texts, authors, periods, and genres of Hispanic literature; key concepts, terminology, and practices of literary analysis that serve as a foundation for higher-level Spanish literature courses. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 202, SPAN_V 203 or successful completion of language placement exam.

subject: SPAN
title: Introduction to Hispanic Culture
description: Media, figures, periods, and genres of Hispanic culture; key concepts, theories, and practices of cultural analysis that serve as a foundation for higher-level Spanish culture courses. Prerequisite: One of BC High School Spanish Grade 12, SPAN 202, SPAN 203 or successful completion of language placement exam or an assessment interview.

subject: SPAN
title: Intermediate Spanish I
description: Complex grammatical structures in context to enhance proficiency. Explores relevant cultural topics through reading, writing, and discussion. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of Grade 12 Spanish, SPAN_V 202, SPAN_V 203, SPAN_V 206, SPAN_V 207 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Intermediate Spanish II
description: Expansion of and reflection on the use of complex grammatical structures in context to broaden lexical repertoire. Enhances proficiency through reading, writing, and discussion of relevant cultural topics. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 301 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Intensive Intermediate Spanish
description: Expands the comprehension and communicative skills of upper-level students and heritage speakers through topics drawn from Hispanic culture and current events. Aligned with CEFR B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 202, SPAN_V 203, and for native and near-native speakers of other Romance languages.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish for Business
description: Language of commerce, finance, marketing, and economics. Competence in business practices of the Hispanic world. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Business Spanish of International Trade in the Hispanic World (in Spanish)
description: Language of international commerce through real world business practices in the Hispanic world; key issues concerning business practices, engaging with real-world materials, and interacting with professionals specializing in trade with the Hispanic world. Pre-requisites: One of SPAN 206, 207, 301, 302, 308. Or successful completion of a language placement exam or an assessment interview.

subject: SPAN
title: Literatures and Cultures of Spain: From Medieval to Present
description: Spanish Literature from the Middle Ages to Present. Literary analysis of narrative, poetic, dramatic, essay and other texts by considering the main literary genres and trends as well as historical and cultural context. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221 or SPAN_V 301.

subject: SPAN
title: Literatures and Cultures of Latin America: From Pre-Columbian to Present
description: Explore a diverse range of texts, themes and genres of Latin American literature from pre-Columbian times to present day. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221 or SPAN_V 301.

subject: SPAN
title: Tradition and Diversity in Spanish History and Culture
description: Conservation and progress on the Iberian Peninsula, from the Middle Ages to the present. Includes the first modern European state and its diverse cultures. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Dependency and Revolution in Latin American History and Culture
description: Continuities and changes in the Americas from before Columbus to the present. Includes the first modern global empire and its ambivalent legacies. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Hispanic Cinema
description: Explores the rich and diverse cinematic landscape of the Global Hispanic World analyzing films, writers, and directors within their historical, social, and cultural contexts. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ . Credit will only be granted for one of SPAN_V 340 or SPAN_V 404. Equivalency: SPAN_V 404.

subject: SPAN
title: Gender Representation(s) in Hispanic Literature and Culture
description: Gender and sexuality in Spain and Latin America. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ . Credit will only be granted for one of SPAN_V 360 or SPAN_V 406. Equivalency: SPAN_V 406.

subject: SPAN
title: Hispanic Theatre
description: Explores areas of study relating to Hispanic Theatre, focusing on the diverse historical, cultural, and performance aspects of the genre. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ . Credit will only be granted for one of SPAN_V 390 or SPAN_V 409. Equivalency: SPAN_V 409.

subject: SPAN
title: Special Topics Abroad
description: Study of Hispanic literature, history, culture, or communities in an authentic context. Topics and locations may vary. Consult Department for current offerings. Recommendation: CEFR A2 Spanish proficiency level

subject: SPAN
title: Upper Intermediate Spanish I: Translation
description: Strengthening fluency and accuracy in spoken and written communication. Emphasis on mediation, interpretation, and metalinguistic competencies through translation and comparative stylistics. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Upper Intermediate Spanish II: Spanish for Community
description: Continued strengthening of fluency, accuracy, and spontaneity in spoken and written communication. Emphasis on contextualized grammar and vocabulary; critical reading and discussion of texts. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 401.

subject: SPAN
title: History of the Spanish Language
description: Major features of the development of the Spanish language, from its origins to the present. Includes the history of Spanish phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and dialectology. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Hispanic Literature and Culture
description: Selected topics relating to the diversity of cultural production in Peninsular and Latin American Culture. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Multicultural Beginnings: Topics in Medieval Literature and Culture
description: Selected areas of study relating to literature and culture of the Iberian Peninsula to the 15th century. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. Recommended pre-requisites: SPAN 221; and SPAN 301 or equivalent expertise in written and spoken Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Hispanic Linguistics
description: Spanish as a linguistic system. Includes the structure of Spanish words and sentences, dialectal varieties in both Spain and Latin America, and linguistic theory. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Peninsular Literatures and Cultures
description: Study of Peninsular literatures, cultures, languages, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings. May be taken twice on different subjects for credit. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of language placement exam.

subject: SPAN
title: Ascent and Decline: Topics in Golden-Age Peninsular Literature and Culture
description: Selected areas of study relating to sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Spain. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. Recommended pre-requisites: SPAN 221; and SPAN 301 or equivalent expertise in written and spoken Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Latin American Literatures and Cultures
description: Study of Latin American literatures, cultures, languages, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings. May be taken twice on different subjects for credit. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of language placement exam.

subject: SPAN
title: Modernization and Autonomy: Topics in Peninsular Literature and Culture since the 18th Century
description: Selected areas of study relating to the literature and culture of modern Spain. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. Recommended pre-requisites: SPAN 221; and SPAN 301 or equivalent expertise in written and spoken Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Global Hispanism
description: Study of the dynamic and evolving nature of Hispanic identities, literatures, and cultures within a global context. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings. May be taken twice on different subjects for credit. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of language placement exam.

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Spanish Language
description: Selected areas of study relating to Spanish linguistics or its relation to other languages spoken in the Hispanic world. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: SPAN
title: Imperial Eyes and Foundational Fictions: Topics in Spanish-American Colonial and Nineteenth-Century Culture
description: Selected areas of study relating to colonial and/or nineteenth-century Spanish America. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. Recommended pre-requisites: SPAN 221; and SPAN 301 or equivalent expertise in written and spoken Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Peoples and Nations: Topics in Twentieth- and Twenty-First Century Spanish-American Culture
description: Selected areas of study relating to modern and/or contemporary Spanish America. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. Recommended pre-requisites: SPAN 221; and SPAN 301 or equivalent expertise in written and spoken Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Research Intensive Seminar in Hispanic Literature and Culture
description: Theories and methodologies of the discipline. Consult the Department for this year's offering. Recommended pre-requisites: SPAN_V 221; and SPAN_V 301 or equivalent expertise in written and spoken Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Directed Reading
description: Focus on a topic agreed on by both Faculty Supervisor and student. Restricted to students with 4th year standing and permission from both the Department Head and Faculty Supervisor. This course may be taught as a Student Directed Seminar. This course is recommended for students who have completed SPAN_V 221, SPAN_V 302, SPAN_V 303 or successful completion of the language placement test: https://fhis.air.arts.ubc.ca/spanish-placement-questionnaire-tool/ .

subject: THTR
title: Introduction to Theatre
description: Theory and practice of the theatrical arts. Attendance at plays is required.

subject: THTR
title: Introduction to Production
description: Foundation study of production for the performing arts.

subject: THTR
title: Graphics for Theatre and Film Design

subject: THTR
title: Drama: Forms and Ideas I
description: The Anatomy of Drama: Its history, aesthetic principles, performative potential.

subject: THTR
title: Drama: Forms and Ideas II
description: Topics in comparative drama; drama and the other performing arts; dramaturgy.

subject: THTR
title: Performance Study I
description: Study of the actor's process.

subject: THTR
title: Play-Interpretation and Production-Analysis
description: Basic methods of interpreting dramatic texts and analyzing plays in performance. The plays presented on the Frederic Wood Stage will be studied in this course.

subject: THTR
title: Technical Production
description: The construction and execution of scenery, costumes, properties, lighting, and sound for the stage. Credit will be granted for only one of THTR_V 250 or THTR_V 254. Equivalency: THTR_V 254

subject: THTR
title: Beginning B.F.A. Acting I
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. An audition is required. Prerequisite: At least one theatre course.

subject: THTR
title: Beginning B.F.A. Acting II
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students.

subject: THTR
title: Beginning Voice and Movement I
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. An audition is required. Prerequisite: At least one theatre course.

subject: THTR
title: Beginning Voice and Movement II
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students.

subject: THTR
title: Production I
description: Assigned projects in theatre production. Corequisite: One of THTR_V 205, THTR_V 250. Credit will be granted for only one of THTR_V 299 or THTR_V 251.

subject: THTR
title: Styles of Decor and Dress
description: Artistic, decorative, cultural, and social contexts of selected theatrical genres and periods.

subject: THTR
title: Scenery Design I
description: Principles and practice of scenery design for the performing arts.

subject: THTR
title: Costume Design I
description: Principles and practice of costume design for the performing arts.

subject: THTR
title: Lighting Design I
description: The optical, distribution, and control systems used in stage lighting design.

subject: THTR
title: Sound Design
description: Audio design and production.

subject: THTR
title: Theory of Drama Performance
description: The basic principles of dramaturgy and theory of performance. Historical and contemporary writing on dramatic theory and criticism and their relation to theatrical practice.

subject: THTR
title: Studies in Drama
description: Topics will vary from year to year.

subject: THTR
title: Introduction to Directing

subject: THTR
title: History of Theatre I
description: Core concepts in world theatre history and the development of theatre prior to the nineteenth century.

subject: THTR
title: Performance Study II
description: Study of performance styles. Prerequisite: One of THTR 130, THTR 230.

subject: THTR
title: Voice and Movement Study
description: Prerequisite: One of THTR 130, THTR 230.

subject: THTR
title: Creating Theatre I
description: Study and practice of processes and forms used to create ensemble performance. Prerequisite: One of THTR 130, THTR 230.

subject: THTR
title: Studies in Asian Theatre
description: Open to all students in third year and above.

subject: THTR
title: Scenery Production I
description: Scenery construction, rigging, and systems. Prerequisite: THTR 250.

subject: THTR
title: Scene Painting I
description: Media, techniques, and textural treatments used in scene painting.

subject: THTR
title: Stage Management
description: Principles and procedures of stage management: organizations, systems, and operations.

subject: THTR
title: Costume Construction

subject: THTR
title: Intermediate B.F.A. Acting I

subject: THTR
title: Intermediate B.F.A. Acting II

subject: THTR
title: Intermediate Voice, Speech, and Movement I
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Prerequisite: All of THTR 271, THTR 272, THTR 273, THTR 274.

subject: THTR
title: Intermediate Voice, Speech, and Movement II
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Corequisite: All of THTR 371, THTR 372, THTR 373.

subject: THTR

description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Prerequisite: All of THTR 271, THTR 272, THTR 273, THTR 274.

title: Production II
description: Assigned projects in theatre design and production. Corequisite: One of THTR 305, THTR 306, THTR 307, THTR 308, THTR 350, THTR 352, THTR 354, THTR 356.

subject: THTR
title: Scenery Design II
description: Exploration of complex scenery design and development of design portfolio. Prerequisite: [THTR305]

subject: THTR
title: Costume Design II
description: Complex problems and selected historical studies in costume design. Prerequisite: THTR 306.

subject: THTR
title: Lighting Design II
description: Complex design and advanced technologies in stage lighting and scenography. Prerequisite: THTR 307.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Study in Design and Scenography
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consent of Department required. Credit will be granted for only one of THTR_V 408 or THTR_V 459.

subject: THTR
title: Dramaturgy
description: Advanced problems in dramaturgy, both in a historical and a contemporary context.

subject: THTR
title: Directing Lab
description: Prerequisite: THTR 317. Permission of the instructor is required for admission to this course.

subject: THTR
title: History of Theatre II
description: Key movements in world theatre history from the nineteenth century to the present. Prerequisite: THTR 320.

subject: THTR
title: History of Theatre from 1900 to the present
description: The development of Western Theatre from 1900 to the present

subject: THTR
title: Theory of Drama and Performance
description: The basic principles of dramaturgy and theory of performance. Historical and contemporary writing on theatrical theory and criticism and their relation to theatrical practice.

subject: THTR
title: Creating Theatre
description: Ensemble creation culminating in the presentation of a theatrical work. Permission of the instructor is required. Credit will be granted for only one of THTR_V 439 or THTR_V 490.

subject: THTR
title: Topics in Theatre
description: An examination in depth of a selected area of theatre history, theory or practice. Topics will change from year to year. May be repeated for credit when topics differ. Prerequisite: 6 credits of THTR at the 300-level or above.

subject: THTR
title: Women in Theatre and Film
description: A course dealing with women's involvement in and contribution to various aspects of Theatre and/or Film Topics will change from year to year. Credit will be granted for only one of THTR_V 443 or THTR_V 415.

subject: THTR
title: Directed Studies in Theatre Theory and Practice

subject: THTR
title: Scenery Production II
description: Technical direction; complex techniques and problems in scenery production. Prerequisite: [THTR350]

subject: THTR
title: Scene Painting II
description: Study of selected scene painting styles. Prerequisite: [THTR352]

subject: THTR
title: Production and Theatre Management
description: Production and theatre management with emphasis on budgeting, publicity, scheduling, press relations, special events, legal issues, season selection, resumes and interpersonal skills. Prerequisite: [THTR354]

subject: THTR
title: Costume Construction II
description: Pattern development and cutting for costume for stage and screen using flat pattern and draping. Prerequisite: THTR 356.

subject: THTR
title: Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Group projects and workshops with students majoring in other creative arts. Credit will be granted for only one of THTR 469 or CRWR 440, VISA 469, MUSC 469. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Equivalency: CRWR 440, VISA 469, MUSC 469

subject: THTR
title: Advanced B.F.A. Acting I
description: Open only to B.F.A. (Acting) students. Prerequisite: All of THTR 371, THTR 372, THTR 373, THTR 374, THTR 391.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced B.F.A. Acting II
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Corequisite: All of THTR 471, THTR 473, THTR 474.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Speech and Movement I
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Prerequisite: Three of THTR 371, THTR 372, THTR 373, THTR 374, THTR 391.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Speech and Movement II
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Corequisite: All of THTR 471, THTR 472, THTR 473.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Rehearsal and Performance
description: Open only to B.F.A. Acting students. Prerequisite: Three of THTR 371, THTR 372, THTR 373, THTR 374, THTR 391.

subject: THTR
title: Production III
description: Assigned projects in Theatre or Film design and production. Prerequisite: THTR 399. Corequisite: One of THTR 405, THTR 406, THTR 407, THTR 408, THTR 450, THTR 452, THTR 454, THTR 456, THTR 470.

subject: VISA
title: BFA Studio Practice
description: Introduction to a broad range of contemporary studio practice. Intended for first year Bachelor of Fine Arts VISA students.

subject: VISA
title: Foundation Studio: Digital Media
description: Foundation instruction in techniques and approaches to digital practice. The nature of digital technologies and their role in contemporary culture will be examined. (This course is open to all UBC students, regardless of prior experience.)

subject: VISA
title: Foundation Studio: Approaches to Media
description: Drawing, painting, and related media in an introduction to studio practice. (This course is open to all UBC students, regardless of prior experience.)

subject: VISA
title: Foundation Studio: Ideas as Practice I
description: Contemporary art practices, emphasizing the relationship between meanings and materials, art historical contexts and concepts, and non-traditional materials. (This course is open to all UBC students, regardless of prior experience.)

subject: VISA
title: Digital Arts
description: Examination of current art practices and issues related to digital technologies and contemporary culture, with an emphasis on the theoretical conceptualization of digital artistic media. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183; or BMS student and VISA 110.

subject: VISA
title: Drawing
description: Development of skills in drawing including life drawing. Introduction to the development of personal style and concepts. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Painting
description: Development of a variety of techniques and approaches to painting. Emphasis on developing a strong paint vocabulary as well as acquiring knowledge of historical and contemporary issues in painting. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Photography
description: Introduction to photography techniques and image-making. Emphasis on camera techniques and film and darkroom production. Only one of VISA 240 or VISA 241 may be used toward requirements for Major, Minor, or Honours programs in Visual Arts. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Digital Photography
description: Introduction to digital photography image creation in relation to contemporary art. Emphasis on digital camera use, file management, and digital print production. Only one of VISA 240 or VISA 241 may be used toward requirements for Major, Minor, or Honours programs in Visual Arts. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183; or BMS student and VISA 110.

subject: VISA
title: Print Media
description: Visual print culture, and contemporary and historical technical print practices. Emphasis on hand-drawn intaglio, relief, screen and/or stencil printing, and graphic digital applications. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Sculpture
description: Contemporary sculpture practice and theory. Various sculpture materials and technologies including machinery use. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Special Studies
description: Introduction to various aspects of contemporary studio practice. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in two of VISA 110, VISA 180, VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Contemporary Art: Ideas as Practice II
description: Development and history of contemporary art practice, with a focus on how artists realize and exchange ideas. Intended for second year BFA VISA students. Prerequisite: A score of 72% or higher in VISA 183.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Digital Arts I
description: Exploring issues and topics in interactive digital media and culture through the creation of critical contemporary art. Includes technical instruction with a focus on the development of individual and group projects. Prerequisite: One of VISA 210, VISA 287, FINA 287.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Digital Arts II
description: Investigation of issues and topics in digital media and visual culture through the production of contemporary video art. Technical instruction in video manipulation software. Individual and/or group projects. Prerequisite: One of VISA 240, VISA 241.

subject: VISA
title: Expanded Visual Media
description: Pre- and/or post-production strategies, techniques, and processes for time-based media effects. Credit will only be granted for one of THFL 312 or VISA 312. Prerequisite: One of VISA 241, VISA 210, FIPR 133, FIPR 233. Or B.M.S. students with 3rd year standing. Equivalency: THFL 312.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Drawing I
description: Investigation of drawing as a discipline in the context of contemporary art. Emphasis on expanding definitions of the drawing practice while focusing on technical and conceptual development. Prerequisite: One of VISA 220, VISA 281, FINA 281.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Drawing II
description: Investigation of drawing as a discipline in the context of contemporary art and theory. Emphasis on self-directed projects in consultation with the instructor. Prerequisite: One of VISA 220, VISA 281, FINA 281.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Painting I
description: Development of techniques and personal style in relation to ideas. History and contemporary issues in painting will be introduced to assist students in conceptualizing their painting practice. Prerequisite: One of VISA 230, VISA 282, FINA 282.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Painting II
description: Further investigation of painting in the context of contemporary art. Emphasis on self directed projects in consultation with the instructor. Prerequisite: One of VISA 230, VISA 282, FINA 282.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Photography I
description: An investigation of approaches to photography and its meaning in the context of contemporary art. The term theme will be determined by the instructor. B & W, colour and digital production. Prerequisite: One of VISA 240, VISA 241.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Photography II
description: An investigation of contemporary photography production and approaches to the constructed image with emphasis on medium and large format camera use and studio lighting techniques. Prerequisite: One of VISA 240, VISA 241.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Print Media I: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Image Production
description: Intaglio and relief print applications (i.e., etching, wood and/or lino cut, and collagraph) in combination with digital and photographic technologies, and drawing; discussion of contemporary and historical visual print culture. Prerequisite: Either (a) VISA 250 or (b) one of VISA 290, VISA 283, VISA 284, FINA 290, FINA 283, FINA 284.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Print Media II: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Image Production
description: Screen printing and other print applications in combination with digital and photographic technologies, and drawing, explored within the context of contemporary art. Prerequisite: Either(a) VISA 250 or (b) one of VISA 283, VISA 284, VISA 290, FINA 283, FINA 284, FINA 290.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Print Media III: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Image Production
description: Lithographic printing; suitable for students interested in drawing and print media interface in context of contemporary art; related digital and photographic technologies employed. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of VISA 220, VISA 250 or (b) one of VISA 281, FINA 281, VISA 283, VISA 284, VISA 290, FINA 283, FINA 284, FINA 290.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Sculpture I
description: Investigation of contemporary practices in sculpture and the use of scale. Emphasis on public sculpture. Prerequisite: One of VISA 260, VISA 285, VISA 286, FINA 285, FINA 286.

subject: VISA
title: Intermediate Sculpture II
description: Development of personal concerns in three-dimensional work. Emphasis on the integration of diverse materials and techniques. Prerequisite: One of VISA 260, VISA 285, VISA 286, FINA 285, FINA 286.

subject: VISA
title: Special Studies I
description: Intermediate tutorial. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 200-level VISA.

subject: VISA
title: Special Studies II
description: Intermediate tutorial. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 200 level VISA

subject: VISA
title: Artists in Society
description: Exploring artistic practice through community-engaged partnerships and critical study. Prerequisite: Restricted to students with at least third-year standing, majoring in Visual Art or Art History. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Artist Books as Form and Idea
description: Approaches to book creation from the perspective of contemporary art and exploration of the artist book as an expansion of both art and books. Prerequisite: 3 credits of any 200-level VISA course.

subject: VISA
title: Studio Theory
description: A seminar in problems in contemporary art practice and related theory. Preference given to Visual Art students. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Studio Seminar
description: A seminar in problems in contemporary art practice and related theory. Preference given to Visual Art students. Prerequisite: VISA_V 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Performance Art
description: Seminar-based studio focusing on performance and actions in the field of contemporary art. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 200-level VISA with an average of at least 72%.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Open Studio
description: Research-based studio with thematic or disciplinary focus. Intended for senior Visual Art undergraduate students. Prerequisite: Three of VISA_V 310, VISA_V 311, VISA_V 320, VISA_V 321, VISA_V 330, VISA_V 331, VISA_V 340, VISA_V 341, VISA_V 350, VISA_V 351, VISA_V 352, VISA_V 360, VISA_V 361, VISA_V 370, VISA_V 375, VISA_V 390. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Digital Arts I
description: Development of contemporary art works utilizing digital technologies including 3-dimensional applications, spatial, interactive and time-based installations. Focus on student-generated projects, either individual or group. Prerequisite: One of VISA_V 310, VISA_V 311. Plus an additional 3 credits of 300-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Digital Arts II: Video
description: Contemporary practices in video media examined through individual projects and directed study. Prerequisite: One of VISA_V 310, VISA_V 311. Plus an additional 3 credits of 300-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Drawing and Painting I
description: Interdisciplinary studio practice with emphasis on drawing, painting, and related media. Prerequisite: Two of VISA_V 320, VISA_V 321, VISA_V 330, VISA_V 331. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Drawing and Painting II
description: Interdisciplinary studio practice with emphasis on drawing, painting, and related media. Prerequisite: Two of VISA_V 320, VISA_V 321, VISA_V 330, VISA_V 331. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Photography I
description: Photography practice in the context of contemporary art. Interdisciplinary connections to other media will be encouraged. Prerequisite: Two of VISA_V 340, VISA_V 341, VISA_V 310. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Photography II
description: The production of self-directed projects investigating photography as art. Focus on integrative approaches including conventional, digital and multi-media. Prerequisite: Two of VISA_V 340, VISA_V 341, VISA_V 440. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Print Media and Sculpture I
description: Studies in contemporary trends in studio practice and theory. Emphasis on advanced two and three-dimensional work developed out of experimental approaches to sculpture, installation art and print-based media. Prerequisite: One of VISA_V 350, VISA_V 351, VISA_V 360, VISA_V 361. Plus an additional 3 credits of 300-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Print Media and Sculpture II
description: Further studies in advanced two and three-dimensional work developed out of experimental approaches to sculpture, installation art and print-based media. Prerequisite: One of VISA_V 350, VISA_V 351, VISA_V 360, VISA_V 361. Plus an additional 3 credits of 300-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Group projects and workshops with students majoring in other creative arts. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Credit will be granted for only one of VISA_V 469, THTR_V 469, CRWR_V 440, MUSC_V 469. Equivalency: THTR_V 469, CRWR_V 440, MUSC_V 469. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Special Studies I
description: Advanced work in contemporary and historical aspects of studio practice. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 300-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Special Studies II
description: Advanced work in contemporary and historical aspects of studio practice. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 300-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Exhibition Theory and Practice
description: Exhibition course focusing on current curatorial practices and theories with an emphasis on contemporary visual art with the aim of preparing students to engage in the active organization of a large exhibition. Restricted to 4th year Majors in either VISA or ARTH, or permission of the instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Performance Actions and Approaches
description: Advanced performance art practices and research methodologies. Credit will be granted for only one of VISA_V 479 or ARTH_V 479. Equivalency: ARTH_V 479. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Seminar I
description: Readings in art theory and criticism. Prerequisite: VISA_V 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Seminar II
description: Readings in art theory and criticism. Prerequisite: VISA_V 480. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Tutorial in Studio I
description: Advanced work in contemporary and historical aspects of studio practice. Permission of instructor required. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 300-level VISA_V and 3 credits of 400-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: VISA
title: Advanced Tutorial in Studio II
description: Advanced work in contemporary and historical aspects of studio practice. Permission of instructor required. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 300-level VISA_V and 3 credits of 400-level VISA_V. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

subject: UFOR
title: Greening the City
description: Roles played by urban forestry and greenspace systems in a rapidly changing world; topics include urban ecology, urban forest conservation, urban forest management, climate change, society and human well-being, design and planning, urban/rural interface issues, and urban forest policy.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Introduction to Urban Forest Design
description: Basic concepts of landscape design as it relates to urban forestry.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Urban Forests and Well-Being
description: Basic relationships between urban residents' mental and physical well-being and their urban forest environment.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Urban Forest Inventory and Assessment
description: Overview of urban forest resources: structure and composition, extent, and ecosystem services and benefits provided; introduces methods and tools for urban forest inventory, monitoring, and assessment, and how they are integrated into the planning and management of urban forests. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Introductory Statistical Methods for Urban Forestry
description: Basic theories and practice of statistical methods in an urban forestry context. Intended only for students in the Bachelor of Urban Forestry program. Students in the Bachelor of Science, Natural Resources should take NRES 231.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Arboriculture Principles and Practice
description: Principles and practices of individual urban tree management with emphasis on underlying biological and ecological concepts, plant-environment interactions above and below ground and implications for establishment, evaluation, and conservation of individual trees in a variety of urban situations. Prerequisite: Pre-req or co-req: UFOR 316 and Third-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Trees and Shrubs in Landscape
description: Identification and suitability of woody plants used in the urban environment, with a focus on biological characteristics for plant identification, criteria for species selection, and other considerations for urban woody plant cultivation. Prerequisite: One of FRST 200, NRES 200. Corequisite: All of UFOR 316, UFOR 300.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Urban Ecology
description: The nature and dynamics of urban ecosystems with emphasis on urban forests and greenspaces. The role of green infrastructure in urban sustainability with particular focus on the ecological impact of urban forest management, design, and policy decisions. .
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Environmental Justice and Urban Green Equity
description: Theory, concepts and applications of urban green equity and urban environmental justice with particular focus on implications for urban forest policy, planning, management, and design. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Urban Forestry Field School
description: Development of field skills, professional judgment, critical reflection, and integration of theory, practice, and policy. Offered at Malcolm Knapp Research Forest over a 7-day period in April. Prerequisite: All of UFOR_V 300, UFOR_V 316. And third year standing in the B.U.F. program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Integrated Urban Forestry Capstone Studio
description: Integration of biophysical and socio-economic components of urban greenspace management and planning through within a collaborative holistic group project linked to a real-world urban forestry situation. . Prerequisite: All of UFOR_V 300, UFOR_V 400. And fourth year standing in the B.U.F. program. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Urban Forestry Administration, Policy and Law
description: The administrative, legal, policy, and business environments for urban forestry governance, management, and planning. Prerequisite: UFOR 300. And third year standing.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Ecological Restoration
description: Perspectives and practices of ecological restoration in diverse ecosystems worldwide. Prerequisite: One of FRST_V 201, NRES_V 201, BIOL_V 230. And third-year standing. Equivalency: APBI_V 423. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Planting Design
description: An introduction to the design of enhanced environments through the use of plants. Prerequisites: Third-year standing
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Green Network Planning
description: Theory and methods of long-range green space planning for urban areas.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Directed Studies in Urban Forestry
description: In special cases and with the approval of the instructor concerned, a student may carry out directed studies on a specific topic/problems in Urban Forestry and related greenspace planning, management, or governance.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

subject: UFOR
title: Biodiversity in Urban Areas
description: Urban centres can be designed and managed to contribute to biodiversity conservation commitments. Topics include designing human-dominated landscapes to promote biodiversity, the tools required, assessing outcomes, and the benefits and negatives of nature in the city. Prerequisite: One of FRST 201, NRES 201, BIOL 230. or permission of the instructor.
faculty_school: Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship
